While the total amount of waking and sleep or the response to SD were not altered, L6b-silenced mice showed a slowing of theta frequency (6–9 Hz) during wake and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, and a marked reduction of total EEG power, especially in non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep. The infusion of orexin A increased wakefulness in both genotypes, but subsequent levels of EEG slow-wave activity during NREM sleep were lower in L6b-silenced animals in the occipital derivation. In summary, these results demonstrate a role for cortical L6b in state-dependent brain oscillations and in the response to orexinergic neurotransmission. Our findings provide new insights in functions of L6b neurons and could inform the understanding of abnormal regulation of brain states in neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders.
items.title_zh: 皮层6b层介导脑活动的状态依赖性变化及食欲素对清醒与睡眠的影响
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了小鼠皮层6b层（L6b）在状态依赖性脑活动中的作用。我们对条件性“沉默”的L6b神经元进行慢性脑电图（EEG）记录，比较了未干扰状态、睡眠剥夺（SD）后及脑室内注射食欲素后的情况。结果显示，尽管清醒和睡眠的总时长未改变，L6b沉默小鼠在清醒和快速眼动（REM）睡眠期间的θ频率（6-9 Hz）减慢，且非快速眼动（NREM）睡眠中的EEG总功率显著降低。食欲素A的注入在两种基因型中均增加了清醒状态，但L6b沉默动物在NREM睡眠中的EEG慢波活动水平较低。研究表明，皮层L6b在状态依赖性脑振荡及对食欲素神经传递的反应中发挥重要作用，为理解神经发育和精神疾病中的脑状态异常调节提供了新视角。
items.l1_lead: 本研究揭示了小鼠皮层6b层在状态依赖性脑活动中的关键作用，食欲素对清醒与睡眠的影响，以及其在神经发育和精神疾病中的潜在调节机制。
items.l2_summary:
本研究探讨了小鼠皮层6b层（L6b）在状态依赖性脑活动中的作用，特别是食欲素（orexin）对清醒与睡眠状态的影响。研究者对条件性“沉默”的L6b神经元进行了慢性脑电图（EEG）记录，比较了小鼠在未干扰状态、经历睡眠剥夺（SD）后以及脑室内注射食欲素后的脑电活动。结果显示，尽管清醒和睡眠的总时长没有显著变化，L6b沉默小鼠在清醒和快速眼动（REM）睡眠期间的θ频率（6-9 Hz）明显减慢，且在非快速眼动（NREM）睡眠中的EEG总功率显著降低。这表明L6b层在调节脑电活动方面具有重要作用。

进一步的实验发现，食欲素A的注入在两种基因型的小鼠中均能增加清醒状态的时间，但L6b沉默动物在NREM睡眠中的EEG慢波活动水平较低。这一发现提示，L6b层不仅参与状态依赖性脑振荡的调节，还对食欲素的神经传递反应产生影响。综上所述，本研究为理解神经发育和精神疾病中脑状态异常的调节机制提供了新的视角，强调了皮层L6b在脑活动状态变化中的关键角色。

items.title: Slap restricts oncogenic Src-family kinase signaling to maintain colonic epithelial homeostasis
items.abstract: Src-family kinases (SFKs) regulate proliferation in colonic epithelial cells (CECs), but the mechanisms that restrain their activity remain poorly defined. We identify Src-like adaptor protein (SLAP), a negative regulator of receptor tyrosine kinase signaling, as a key suppressor of SFK activity in the colon. Constitutive and inducible epithelial-specific Slap deletion using a villin-CreERT2 model increases CEC proliferation and accelerates tumorigenesis in the azoxymethane/dextran sodium sulfate model. Slap deficiency also enhances SFK-dependent expansion of normal and tumor-derived colonic organoids. Mechanistically, we identify the receptor tyrosine kinase EPHB2 as a critical upstream activator of SFKs and a direct target of SLAP-mediated regulation. Loss of Slap increased EphB2 protein abundance and tyrosine phosphorylation, and enhanced its association with active SRC. Pharmacological inhibition of EPHB2 suppressed SRC activation and reversed the hyperproliferative phenotype induced by Slap deficiency. Together, these findings uncover a non-genetic mechanism driving SFK activation during colonic transformation and establish SLAP as a tumor suppressor that constrains oncogenic EPHB2–SFK signaling in the colonic epithelium.

items.title: Centrosome migration and apical membrane formation during epithelial polarization in MDCK cysts
items.abstract: Polarization is crucial for the proper functioning of epithelial cells. Early hallmarks include the trafficking and enrichment of polarity molecules to form the apical membrane (AM) or cell–cell junctions, and the apical positioning of the centrosome. However, the dependencies among polarity molecules, AM formation, and centrosome positioning remain poorly understood. When cultured in Matrigel, de novo polarization of a single epithelial cell is often coupled with cytokinesis. During mitotic exit, centrosomes move to the future AM site, raising questions about their role in polarization. We perturbed centrosomes and polarity regulators in Matrigel-cultured cells and manipulated polarity direction using suspension culture to examine the relationships among polarization features. Surprisingly, centrosomal microtubules may not be necessary for centrosome positioning or AM formation, but their absence reduces the efficiency of AM formation. The polarity regulator Par3, rather than AM component trafficking, influences centrosome positioning. In suspension culture, centrosomes migrate in the direction opposite to AM formation. Taken together, our findings define the hierarchical relationships among several polarization features and show that centrosome-based polarity is not universal in epithelial cells, providing new insights into the mechanisms of epithelial polarization.
items.title_zh: MDCK囊泡上皮极性化过程中的中心体迁移与顶膜形成
items.summary_zh: 上皮细胞的极性化对其正常功能至关重要。早期特征包括极性分子的运输和富集以形成顶膜（AM）或细胞间连接，以及中心体的顶端定位。然而，极性分子、AM形成和中心体定位之间的依赖关系仍不清楚。在Matrigel中培养的单个上皮细胞的极性化通常与细胞分裂相关。在有丝分裂退出期间，中心体移动到未来的AM位置，这引发了关于其在极性化中作用的问题。我们在Matrigel培养的细胞中扰动中心体和极性调节因子，并通过悬浮培养操控极性方向，以研究极性特征之间的关系。令人惊讶的是，中心体微管可能不是中心体定位或AM形成的必要条件，但其缺失会降低AM形成的效率。极性调节因子Par3影响中心体定位，而非AM组分的运输。在悬浮培养中，中心体向与AM形成相反的方向迁移。综合来看，我们的研究定义了多个极性特征之间的层级关系，并表明基于中心体的极性在上皮细胞中并非普遍存在，为上皮极性化机制提供了新见解。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，中心体在上皮细胞极性化过程中并非必需，但其缺失会降低顶膜形成效率，揭示了极性特征之间的复杂关系。
items.l2_summary:
上皮细胞的极性化是其正常功能的重要基础，涉及极性分子的运输和富集，从而形成顶膜（apical membrane, AM）和细胞间连接。尽管中心体（centrosome）的顶端定位被认为与极性化过程密切相关，但极性分子、AM形成和中心体定位之间的具体依赖关系仍不明确。研究者们在Matrigel中培养的单个上皮细胞中探讨了这一问题，发现极性化通常与细胞分裂相关。在有丝分裂退出期间，中心体会移动到未来的AM位置，这引发了对其在极性化中作用的深入思考。

通过对中心体和极性调节因子的扰动，以及在悬浮培养中操控极性方向，研究者们发现中心体微管并不是中心体定位或AM形成的必要条件，尽管其缺失会显著降低AM形成的效率。此外，极性调节因子Par3对中心体定位有影响，但并不涉及AM组分的运输。在悬浮培养的实验中，中心体向与AM形成相反的方向迁移，这一发现进一步揭示了极性特征之间的复杂关系。

综合这些研究结果，研究者们定义了多个极性特征之间的层级关系，表明基于中心体的极性在上皮细胞中并非普遍存在。这为理解上皮极性化机制提供了新的视角，挑战了传统观点，并为未来的研究指明了方向。

items.title: Small mammalian herbivores at moderate densities facilitate livestock growth by improving vegetation composition in grasslands
items.abstract: Small mammals and large herbivores have co-evolved in grasslands for millions of years, yet how they interact remains unclear. Although large herbivores can significantly affect the smaller ones, the reverse effect is largely unknown. On the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau, plateau pikas ( Ochotona curzoniae ) are often considered pests that compete with livestock at high densities. Using field experiments, we show that the presence of pikas facilitates weight gains of yaks ( Bos grunniens ) by improving vegetation composition at a moderate density level. Compared to the pika-present treatment, pika removal dramatically increased cover of the poisonous Stellera forbs by twofold, reducing the abundance and protein content of palatable grasses and sedges, yak foraging efficiency, and yak weight gain by up to 42%. Notably, we found a humped relationship between yak weight gains and pika burrow densities in the pika-present plots; the facilitative effect of pikas on yaks was highest at about 200 burrows/ha, but shifted to a competitive effect at pika densities exceeding 400 burrows/ha. These results provide the first empirical evidence that maintaining a moderate density of small mammalian herbivores can benefit growth performance of livestock by improving vegetation composition. Our study highlights the significance of moderate populations of ecosystem-engineering small mammals in sustaining pastoral productivity in rangelands.

items.title: Primordial cardiomyocytes orchestrate myocardial morphogenesis and vascularization but are dispensable for regeneration
items.abstract: The vertebrate heart is composed of heterogeneous cardiomyocyte (CM) populations; however, the roles of distinct CM subpopulations in heart development and repair remain poorly defined. Here, using single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of adult zebrafish heart, we identified a unique CM subpopulation marked by the expression of phlda2 , which is associated with anaerobic metabolism and different from mature CMs, which are enriched for oxidative phosphorylation genes. We demonstrated that phlda2 + cells constituted a primordial CM compartment localized between compact and trabecular muscles. Genetic ablation of phlda2 + CMs during development severely disrupted heart morphogenesis, leading to defective myocardial trabeculation and compaction, and impaired coronary vascularization. Surprisingly, despite their essential roles in development, the depletion of phlda2 + CMs didn’t impair myocardial restoration and revascularization following ventricular resection. We found that this was probably due to the limited regenerative capacity of the primordial CMs themselves, as they failed to regenerate after either surgical amputation or genetic ablation. Our findings identify primordial CMs as an organizer for heart morphogenesis but not essential for regeneration, revealing a fundamental difference between developmental and regenerative programs in the vertebrate heart.
items.title_zh: 原始心肌细胞在心脏形态发生中的作用及其再生的非必需性
items.summary_zh: 脊椎动物心脏由异质心肌细胞（CM）群体组成，但不同CM亚群在心脏发育和修复中的作用尚不明确。本研究通过对成年斑马鱼心脏进行单细胞RNA测序分析，识别出一种以phlda2表达为标志的独特CM亚群，该亚群与厌氧代谢相关，且不同于富含氧化磷酸化基因的成熟CM。我们证明phlda2+细胞构成了位于致密肌和小梁肌之间的原始CM区间。发育过程中基因去除phlda2+ CM严重干扰心脏形态发生，导致心肌小梁和致密化缺陷，以及冠状血管化受损。令人惊讶的是，尽管在发育中发挥重要作用，去除phlda2+ CM并未影响心室切除后的心肌恢复和再血管化。我们发现这可能是由于原始CM自身的有限再生能力，因为它们在外科截肢或基因去除后未能再生。我们的研究表明，原始CM在心脏形态发生中起组织者作用，但对再生并非必需，揭示了脊椎动物心脏发育与再生程序之间的根本差异。
items.l1_lead: 原始心肌细胞在心脏形态发生中起关键作用，但其并非心脏再生的必需成分，揭示了发育与再生之间的显著差异。
items.l2_summary:
本研究探讨了脊椎动物心脏中不同亚群心肌细胞（CM）在心脏形态发生和再生中的作用，特别关注一种以phlda2表达为标志的独特CM亚群。通过对成年斑马鱼心脏进行单细胞RNA测序分析，研究团队识别出这种phlda2+ CM亚群与厌氧代谢相关，且其基因表达特征明显不同于成熟CM中富含氧化磷酸化基因的细胞。研究发现，phlda2+细胞主要位于致密肌和小梁肌之间，构成了原始CM区间。

在发育过程中，去除phlda2+ CM会严重干扰心脏的形态发生，导致心肌小梁和致密化的缺陷，以及冠状血管化的受损。这表明phlda2+ CM在心脏发育中扮演着重要的组织者角色。然而，令人意外的是，尽管这些细胞在发育过程中至关重要，去除phlda2+ CM并未对心室切除后的心肌恢复和再血管化产生影响。这一发现提示，原始CM的再生能力有限，因为在外科截肢或基因去除后，它们未能实现再生。

综上所述，研究表明原始CM在心脏形态发生中具有关键作用，但在心脏再生过程中并非必需。这一结果揭示了脊椎动物心脏发育与再生程序之间的根本差异，为理解心脏生物学提供了新的视角。

items.title: A simplified and highly efficient cell-free protein synthesis system for prokaryotes
items.abstract: Cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) systems are a powerful platform with immense potential in fundamental research, biotechnology, and synthetic biology. Conventional prokaryotic CFPS systems, particularly those derived from Escherichia coli , often rely on complex reaction buffers containing up to 35 components, limiting their widespread adoption and systematic optimization. Here, we present an optimized E. coli cell-free protein synthesis ( e CFPS) system, which is significantly streamlined for high efficiency. Through systematic screening, we successfully reduced the essential core reaction components from 35 to a core set of 7. The thorough optimization of these seven key components ensured that protein expression levels were not only maintained but even substantially improved. Furthermore, we developed a much simpler procedure for preparing the bacterial cytosolic extracts, a ‘fast lysate’ protocol that eliminates the traditional time-consuming runoff and dialysis steps, thereby enhancing the overall accessibility and robustness of e CFPS. This optimized and user-friendly e CFPS efficiently synthesizes challenging proteins, including functional, self-assembling vimentin, and active restriction endonuclease Bsa I despite its strong cytotoxicity, and serves as a powerful tool that will facilitate diverse applications in basic life science research and beyond.
items.title_zh: 简化高效的原核细胞无细胞蛋白合成系统
items.summary_zh: 无细胞蛋白合成（CFPS）系统在基础研究、生物技术和合成生物学中具有巨大潜力。传统的原核CFPS系统，尤其是源自大肠杆菌的系统，通常依赖于含有多达35种成分的复杂反应缓冲液，限制了其广泛应用和系统优化。本文提出了一种优化的E. coli无细胞蛋白合成（e CFPS）系统，显著简化以提高效率。通过系统筛选，我们成功将核心反应成分从35种减少至7种。对这7种关键成分的彻底优化确保了蛋白表达水平不仅得以维持，甚至显著提高。此外，我们开发了一种更简单的细菌细胞质提取制备程序，即“快速裂解”协议，省去了传统的耗时的流出和透析步骤，从而增强了e CFPS的整体可及性和稳健性。该优化的e CFPS系统能够高效合成具有挑战性的蛋白，包括功能性自组装的波形蛋白和活性限制性内切酶Bsa I，尽管其具有强细胞毒性，为基础生命科学研究及其他领域的多样化应用提供了强有力的工具。
items.l1_lead: 本文提出了一种优化的E. coli无细胞蛋白合成系统，通过将反应成分从35种减少至7种，显著提高了蛋白表达效率和系统可及性。
items.l2_summary:
无细胞蛋白合成（Cell-Free Protein Synthesis, CFPS）系统在基础研究、生物技术和合成生物学中展现出巨大的应用潜力。然而，传统的原核CFPS系统，尤其是基于大肠杆菌（E. coli）的系统，通常需要复杂的反应缓冲液，成分多达35种，这限制了其广泛应用和系统优化。为了解决这一问题，本文提出了一种优化的E. coli无细胞蛋白合成（e CFPS）系统，显著简化了反应成分，从而提高了合成效率。

通过系统筛选，研究团队成功将核心反应成分从35种减少至7种。这7种关键成分经过彻底优化，确保了蛋白表达水平不仅得以维持，甚至显著提高。此外，研究还开发了一种更为简便的细菌细胞质提取制备程序，称为“快速裂解”协议。这一新方法省去了传统CFPS流程中耗时的流出和透析步骤，增强了e CFPS的整体可及性和稳健性。

优化后的e CFPS系统能够高效合成一些具有挑战性的蛋白质，包括功能性自组装的波形蛋白和活性限制性内切酶Bsa I，尽管后者具有较强的细胞毒性。这一成果为基础生命科学研究及其他领域的多样化应用提供了强有力的工具，展示了简化和优化CFPS系统在提高蛋白合成效率方面的潜力。通过减少反应成分和简化提取流程，研究为未来的蛋白合成技术奠定了基础，推动了相关领域的发展。

items.title: Cellular modifiers of TDP-43 phase transition and cytoplasmic aggregation
items.abstract: RNA-binding protein TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) can form liquid-like nuclear assemblies whose phase behavior is thought to influence its aggregation propensity and neurotoxic activity. The mechanisms that govern the liquid-to-solid phase transition of TDP-43 remain poorly defined. Here, we combined chemical and genome-wide genetic screens to identify cellular factors that modulate the phase behavior of an RNA-binding-defective TDP-43 mutant. Our screens uncovered multiple cellular processes, including RNA splicing, protein translation, proteostasis imbalance, and nuclear export as TDP-43 phase regulators. We also developed a semi-permeabilized cell system that partially recapitulates the TDP-43 phase transition in vitro, and showed that nuclear export inhibition reshapes the nuclear environment to favor RNA-dependent liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of TDP-43, which mitigates its aggregation. Nuclear export inhibition in a brain organoid model bearing an ALS-associated mutation reduces pathogenic phospho-TDP-43 accumulation. These findings identify multiple modulators of TDP-43 phase transitions in a sensitized model system and establish a framework for further dissecting the link between nuclear transport and TDP-43 phase dynamics.
items.title_zh: TDP-43相变及细胞聚集的调节因子研究
items.summary_zh: RNA结合蛋白TAR DNA结合蛋白43（TDP-43）能够形成液态核组装，其相行为被认为影响其聚集倾向和神经毒性活性。本文结合化学和全基因组遗传筛选，识别出调节RNA结合缺陷型TDP-43突变体相行为的细胞因子。筛选结果揭示了多个细胞过程，包括RNA剪接、蛋白质翻译、蛋白质稳态失衡和核输出，作为TDP-43相调节因子。我们还开发了一种半透膜细胞系统，部分重现了TDP-43的相变，并显示核输出抑制重塑核环境，促进TDP-43的RNA依赖性液-液相分离（LLPS），从而减轻其聚集。在携带与ALS相关突变的脑类器官模型中，核输出抑制减少了致病性磷酸化TDP-43的积累。这些发现识别了多个TDP-43相变的调节因子，并为进一步解析核运输与TDP-43相动力学之间的联系奠定了基础。
items.l1_lead: 研究发现多个细胞因子调节TDP-43的相变和聚集，抑制核输出可减轻其在ALS模型中的致病性积累。
items.l2_summary:
RNA结合蛋白TAR DNA结合蛋白43（TDP-43）在细胞内能够形成液态核组装，其相行为被认为与其聚集倾向和神经毒性活性密切相关。本文通过结合化学实验和全基因组遗传筛选，识别出调节RNA结合缺陷型TDP-43突变体相行为的细胞因子。筛选结果揭示了多个细胞过程，包括RNA剪接、蛋白质翻译、蛋白质稳态失衡和核输出，均作为TDP-43相调节因子。

研究中，研究者们开发了一种半透膜细胞系统，部分重现了TDP-43的相变现象。实验结果显示，核输出的抑制能够重塑细胞核环境，促进TDP-43的RNA依赖性液-液相分离（LLPS），从而减轻其聚集现象。此外，在携带与肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）相关突变的脑类器官模型中，核输出抑制显著减少了致病性磷酸化TDP-43的积累。这些发现不仅识别了多个调节TDP-43相变的因子，还为进一步探讨核运输与TDP-43相动力学之间的关系奠定了基础。

综上所述，本文的研究为理解TDP-43的相变机制及其在神经退行性疾病中的作用提供了新的视角，揭示了细胞内多种过程如何影响TDP-43的聚集和毒性，具有重要的科学价值和潜在的临床意义。

items.title: Preserved cerebellar functions despite structural degeneration in older adults
items.abstract: Aging is frequently perceived negatively due to its association with declines in brain and motor function yet not all aspects of brain function are equally affected. The cerebellum, a brain region closely linked to motor control, undergoes clear structural changes with age, but the impact of this degeneration on cerebellar function remains debated. The present study thoroughly investigates the impact of age on cerebellar function by measuring cerebellar motor and cognitive performance across the lifespan in 50 young adults (20–35 years), 80 older adults (55–70 years), and 30 older-old adults (over 80 years). Participants completed a test battery comprising seven motor control tasks and one cognitive task each designed to probe both cerebellar-specific and general sensorimotor function. Our results revealed that, despite age-related changes in cerebellar structure, cerebellar-specific functions remained intact in older adults compared to young adults, even among those above 80 years old. In contrast, general sensorimotor measures showed a clear pattern of decline with age. Together, these findings indicate that cerebellar function is largely preserved despite pronounced structural degeneration, providing compelling evidence for the cerebellum’s remarkable functional resilience.
items.title_zh: 老年人小脑功能保持良好，尽管结构退化明显
items.summary_zh: 衰老常被负面看待，因其与大脑和运动功能的下降相关，但并非所有大脑功能都受到同等影响。本研究通过对50名年轻成人（20-35岁）、80名老年成人（55-70岁）和30名高龄老年人（80岁以上）进行小脑运动和认知表现的测量，深入探讨了年龄对小脑功能的影响。参与者完成了包括七个运动控制任务和一个认知任务的测试，旨在探测小脑特异性和一般感觉运动功能。结果显示，尽管小脑结构随年龄变化明显，但老年人（包括80岁以上者）的小脑特异性功能与年轻人相比依然保持完整。相反，一般感觉运动测量则呈现出明显的年龄相关下降模式。这些发现表明，尽管小脑结构退化明显，小脑功能在很大程度上得以保持，提供了小脑功能韧性的有力证据。
items.l1_lead: 研究发现，尽管小脑结构在老年人中明显退化，但其特异性功能仍保持良好，显示出小脑功能的韧性。
items.l2_summary:
衰老通常被视为一种负面现象，因其与大脑和运动功能的下降密切相关。然而，最新研究表明，老年人的小脑功能在一定程度上能够保持良好，尽管其结构明显退化。该研究对180名参与者进行了深入分析，其中包括50名年轻成人（20-35岁）、80名老年成人（55-70岁）和30名高龄老年人（80岁以上）。研究者通过测量参与者在七个运动控制任务和一个认知任务中的表现，旨在探讨年龄对小脑功能的影响。

研究结果显示，尽管小脑的结构随着年龄的增长而明显变化，老年人（包括80岁以上者）在小脑特异性功能方面与年轻人相比依然保持完整。这一发现表明，小脑在处理特定运动和认知任务时的功能韧性较强。相对而言，一般感觉运动的测量结果则显示出明显的年龄相关下降模式，表明在这一方面，老年人的表现较年轻人有所减弱。

这些结果为小脑功能的韧性提供了有力证据，挑战了传统上对衰老的消极看法，提示我们在理解老年人运动和认知能力时，不能仅仅依赖于结构变化的表面现象。总的来说，尽管小脑结构退化明显，但其功能在很大程度上得以保持，这为老年人群体的运动和认知能力提供了新的视角。

items.title: Trpv4 links environmental temperature to testicular differentiation in hermaphroditic ricefield eel
items.abstract: The ricefield eel ( Monopterus albus ), an economically important aquaculture species in China, is a freshwater teleost fish that exhibits protogynous hermaphroditism. Although progress has been made in understanding the sex determination and differentiation of this species, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that warm temperature promotes gonadal transformation by up-regulating testicular differentiation genes, such as dmrt1 / sox9a in ovaries. Trpv4, a Ca 2+ -permeable cation channel expressed in gonadal somatic cells, is highly sensitive to ambient temperature and links environmental temperature to testicular differentiation in ricefield eel. In female fish reared at cool temperature, injection of Trpv4 agonist into the ovaries leads to a significant upregulation of male pathway genes and in female fish exposed to warm temperature, Trpv4 inhibition or trpv4 siRNA knockdown suppresses warm temperature-induced male gene expression. pStat3 signaling is downstream of Trpv4 and transduces Trpv4-controlled calcium signaling into the sex determination cascades. Inhibition of pStat3 activity prevents the up-regulation of testicular differentiation genes by warm temperature treatment and ovarian injection of Trpv4 agonist, whereas activation of pStat3 is sufficient to induce the expression of male genes in the presence of Trpv4 antagonist. pStat3 binds and activates jmjd3 / kdm6b , an activator of the dmrt1 gene. Consistently, ovarian injection of Kdm6b inhibitor blocks the up-regulation of testicular differentiation genes by warm temperature exposure. We propose that environmental factors, such as temperature, promote gonadal transformation of ricefield eel by inducing the expression of male pathway genes in ovaries via the Trpv4-pStat3-Kdm6b- dmrt1 axis. Our results provide new insights into the molecular mechanism underlying natural sex change of ricefield eel, which will be useful for sex control in aquaculture.
items.title_zh: Trpv4在杂交稻田鳗的环境温度与睾丸分化中的作用
items.summary_zh: 稻田鳗（Monopterus albus）是一种在中国经济上重要的水产养殖物种，表现出原雌性杂交现象。尽管对该物种的性别决定和分化已有所了解，但其机制仍不清楚。本研究表明，温暖的环境温度通过上调睾丸分化基因（如dmrt1和sox9a）促进性腺转化。Trpv4是一种在性腺体细胞中表达的钙离子通道，对环境温度高度敏感，并将环境温度与稻田鳗的睾丸分化联系起来。在低温下饲养的雌鱼中，向卵巢注射Trpv4激动剂显著上调雄性通路基因，而在高温下，抑制Trpv4或敲低trpv4 siRNA则抑制温度诱导的雄性基因表达。pStat3信号通路是Trpv4的下游，负责将Trpv4控制的钙信号转导至性别决定级联反应。抑制pStat3活性可阻止温暖温度处理和卵巢注射Trpv4激动剂引起的睾丸分化基因上调，而激活pStat3则足以在Trpv4拮抗剂存在下诱导雄性基因的表达。
items.l1_lead: 研究发现，Trpv4钙离子通道通过调控pStat3信号通路，连接环境温度与稻田鳗的睾丸分化，促进性腺转化。
items.l2_summary:
稻田鳗（Monopterus albus）是中国重要的水产养殖物种，具有原雌性杂交现象。尽管对其性别决定和分化的研究已有一定进展，但具体机制仍不明确。本研究探讨了温暖环境温度对稻田鳗睾丸分化的影响，重点关注钙离子通道Trpv4（Transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily V member 4）的作用。研究发现，温暖的环境温度能够通过上调睾丸分化基因，如dmrt1和sox9a，促进性腺的转化。

Trpv4在性腺体细胞中表达，对环境温度变化高度敏感，研究表明其在稻田鳗的睾丸分化中起着关键作用。在低温条件下饲养的雌性稻田鳗中，向卵巢注射Trpv4激动剂显著上调了雄性基因表达通路的基因，而在高温环境下，抑制Trpv4或通过siRNA敲低trpv4则抑制了温度诱导的雄性基因表达。这表明Trpv4在温度调控下对性别决定具有重要影响。

此外，研究还揭示了pStat3信号通路作为Trpv4的下游效应，负责将Trpv4介导的钙信号转导至性别决定的级联反应中。抑制pStat3活性能够阻止温暖温度处理和卵巢注射Trpv4激动剂引起的睾丸分化基因上调，而激活pStat3则能够在Trpv4拮抗剂存在的情况下诱导雄性基因的表达。这些结果表明，Trpv4通过调节pStat3信号通路在环境温度影响下调控稻田鳗的性别分化，进一步揭示了环境因素与性别决定之间的复杂关系，为理解稻田鳗的性别分化机制提供了新的视角。

items.title: REM sleep prefrontal high-frequency oscillation chains mediate distinct cortical – hippocampal reactivation patterns compared to NREM sleep
items.abstract: REM (rapid eye movement) and non-REM (NREM) sleep stages contribute to systems memory consolidation in hippocampal–cortical circuits. However, the physiological mechanisms underlying REM memory processes remain relatively unclear compared to NREM memory reactivation. Here we report, in rodents, the existence of prefrontal cortical (PFC) high-frequency oscillation (HFO) chains in REM sleep during the consolidation of recently acquired spatial memory. High-density tetrode recordings in hippocampal area CA1 and PFC reveal that REM cortical HFOs occur in characteristic chains that are phase-modulated by theta oscillations, corresponding to increased CA1-PFC theta coherence and delineating periods of enhanced hippocampal–cortical communication. REM HFO chains sequentially organize sparse PFC ensemble reactivation of behavioral activity during periods of local suppression, distinct from widespread reactivation bursts during NREM ripple oscillations. REM HFO chains also preferentially engage CA1 neuronal populations that demonstrate a shift in their preferred theta-phase from behavior to REM sleep. CA1 neuronal activation during REM HFO chains was correlated with CA1 activity suppression during NREM PFC ripples, and linked to differential changes in CA1 firing rates in sleep, suggesting REM-driven regulation of hippocampal excitability. A cortical network model incorporating the effects of acetylcholine can reproduce the distinct REM and NREM activity patterns, providing a mechanistic basis for widespread coactivity during NREM cortical ripples, compared to sparse, temporally extended reactivation on a background of local suppression during REM HFO chains. Overall, these findings establish a role for PFC HFOs in regulating distinct dual sleep stage reactivation patterns.
items.title_zh: REM睡眠前额叶高频振荡链介导独特的皮层-海马重激活模式
items.summary_zh: REM（快速眼动）睡眠和非REM（NREM）睡眠阶段在海马-皮层回路的系统记忆巩固中发挥作用。然而，与NREM记忆重激活相比，REM记忆过程的生理机制仍不够明确。本研究在啮齿动物中发现，REM睡眠期间存在前额叶皮层（PFC）高频振荡（HFO）链，伴随最近获得的空间记忆的巩固。通过在海马CA1区和PFC进行高密度四电极记录，发现REM皮层HFO以特征性链的形式出现，受θ振荡相位调制，表明CA1-PFC θ相干性增强，划定了海马-皮层通信增强的时期。REM HFO链在局部抑制期间顺序组织稀疏的PFC集体重激活，与NREM波动期间的广泛重激活突发不同。此外，REM HFO链优先激活CA1神经元群体，这些神经元的偏好θ相位从行为转变为REM睡眠。REM HFO链期间CA1神经元的激活与NREM PFC波动期间CA1活动抑制相关，并与睡眠中CA1放电率的差异变化相关，提示REM驱动的海马兴奋性调节。
items.l1_lead: 研究发现，REM睡眠期间前额叶皮层高频振荡链介导了独特的海马-皮层重激活模式，增强了记忆巩固过程。
items.l2_summary:
本研究探讨了快速眼动（REM）睡眠在海马-皮层回路中的记忆巩固机制，特别是与非REM（NREM）睡眠相比，REM睡眠期间的生理过程尚不明确。研究发现，在啮齿动物的REM睡眠阶段，前额叶皮层（PFC）出现高频振荡（HFO）链，这一现象与最近获得的空间记忆的巩固密切相关。通过在海马CA1区和PFC进行高密度四电极记录，研究人员观察到REM睡眠期间的皮层HFO以特征性链的形式出现，并受到θ振荡相位的调制，表明CA1-PFC之间的θ相干性增强，从而划定了海马-皮层通信增强的时段。

与NREM睡眠期间的广泛重激活突发不同，REM HFO链在局部抑制期间顺序组织稀疏的PFC集体重激活。这种重激活模式优先激活CA1神经元群体，这些神经元的偏好θ相位在行为状态与REM睡眠之间发生了转变。此外，REM HFO链期间CA1神经元的激活与NREM PFC波动期间CA1活动的抑制相关，并且与睡眠中CA1放电率的变化差异有关。这些结果提示REM睡眠驱动的海马兴奋性调节可能在记忆巩固过程中发挥重要作用，揭示了REM睡眠在记忆重激活中的独特生理机制。

items.title: Stage-specific threats reveal the inadequacy of adult-centered conservation
items.abstract: In an era of severe global biodiversity threats, understanding the link between species’ traits and their endangerment helps uncover causes of risk and infer threats to understudied species. Most animals have complex life cycles with distinct stages that may face stage-specific threats. Current conservation frameworks rely heavily on adult traits, potentially misjudging extinction risk. Using Chinese anurans as a model, we integrated functional traits from both adult and tadpole stages to examine their association with extinction risk. We found that body size positively correlates with risk in both stages. Microhabitat use is related to extinction risk in tadpoles, but shows no significant link in adults. Adult relative tympanum diameter and head length also correlate with extinction risk. These results indicate that species vulnerability is correlated with multi-stage traits, with both shared and stage-specific threats. Conservation based solely on adult traits may fail to accurately assess species threats. We call for integrating a whole-life-history perspective into biodiversity assessment and conservation to more effectively address the global biodiversity crisis.
items.title_zh: 阶段特异性威胁揭示以成年为中心的保护不足
items.summary_zh: 在全球生物多样性面临严重威胁的时代，理解物种特征与其濒危之间的联系有助于揭示风险原因并推断对未充分研究物种的威胁。大多数动物具有复杂的生命周期，各阶段可能面临特定威胁。本研究以中国蛙类为模型，整合成年和蝌蚪阶段的功能特征，考察其与灭绝风险的关联。结果发现，体型在两个阶段与风险呈正相关。微栖息地使用与蝌蚪的灭绝风险相关，但在成年个体中未显示显著关联。成年个体的相对鼓膜直径和头长也与灭绝风险相关。这些结果表明，物种脆弱性与多阶段特征相关，存在共享和阶段特异性威胁。仅基于成年特征的保护可能无法准确评估物种威胁。我们呼吁在生物多样性评估和保护中整合全生命周期视角，以更有效地应对全球生物多样性危机。
items.l1_lead: 本研究揭示，物种的灭绝风险与其生命周期各阶段的特征密切相关，仅依赖成年特征的保护措施可能不足以有效应对生物多样性危机。
items.l2_summary:
在全球生物多样性面临严重威胁的背景下，理解物种特征与其濒危之间的关系显得尤为重要。本研究以中国蛙类为模型，探讨了成年和蝌蚪阶段的功能特征与灭绝风险之间的关联。研究发现，体型在两个生命周期阶段均与灭绝风险呈正相关，表明体型可能是影响蛙类生存的重要因素。此外，微栖息地使用与蝌蚪阶段的灭绝风险相关，但在成年个体中未显示出显著的关联性。这一发现提示我们，成年个体的栖息环境可能与其生存风险的关系不同于蝌蚪阶段。

研究还发现，成年个体的相对鼓膜直径和头长与灭绝风险存在相关性，进一步支持了物种脆弱性与多阶段特征之间的联系。总体而言，这些结果表明，蛙类的脆弱性不仅受到生命周期各阶段特征的影响，还存在共享和阶段特异性威胁。因此，单纯基于成年特征进行保护措施可能无法准确评估物种的威胁程度。

基于上述研究结果，作者呼吁在生物多样性评估和保护策略中，整合全生命周期的视角。这种方法将有助于更全面地理解物种面临的威胁，从而更有效地应对全球生物多样性危机。通过关注不同生命周期阶段的特征，保护措施能够更加精准地针对物种的实际需求，提升保护工作的有效性。

items.title: Squidly harnesses enzyme functional hierarchy and contrastive learning to efficiently predict catalytic residues from sequence
items.abstract: Enzymes present a sustainable alternative to traditional chemical industries, drug synthesis, and bioremediation applications. Because catalytic residues are the key amino acids that drive enzyme function, their accurate prediction facilitates enzyme function prediction. Sequence similarity-based approaches such as BLAST are fast but require previously annotated homologues. Machine-learning (ML) approaches aim to overcome this limitation; however, current gold-standard ML-based methods require high-quality 3D structures limiting their application to large datasets. To address these challenges, we developed Squidly, a sequence-only tool that leverages contrastive representation learning with a biology-informed, rationally designed pairing scheme to distinguish catalytic from non-catalytic residues using per-token Protein Language Model embeddings. Squidly surpasses state-of-the-art ML annotation methods in catalytic residue prediction while remaining sufficiently fast to enable wide-scale screening of databases. We ensemble Squidly with BLAST to provide an efficient tool that annotates catalytic residues with high precision and recall for both in- and out-of-distribution sequences.
items.title_zh: Squidly利用酶功能层次和对比学习高效预测催化残基
items.summary_zh: 酶为传统化学工业、药物合成和生物修复应用提供了可持续的替代方案。催化残基是驱动酶功能的关键氨基酸，其准确预测有助于酶功能的预测。基于序列相似性的BLAST方法快速但需依赖已注释的同源物。机器学习（ML）方法旨在克服这一限制，但现有的金标准ML方法需要高质量的3D结构，限制了其在大数据集中的应用。为解决这些挑战，我们开发了Squidly，这是一种仅基于序列的工具，利用对比表示学习和生物学启发的配对方案，通过每个标记的蛋白质语言模型嵌入区分催化和非催化残基。Squidly在催化残基预测上超越了最先进的ML注释方法，同时保持足够的速度以支持大规模数据库筛选。我们将Squidly与BLAST结合，提供了一种高精度和高召回率的工具，能够为分布内外的序列注释催化残基。
items.l1_lead: Squidly是一种基于序列的工具，通过对比学习有效预测催化残基，超越传统机器学习方法，支持大规模数据库筛选。
items.l2_summary:
酶在传统化学工业、药物合成和生物修复等领域中提供了可持续的替代方案，而催化残基是驱动酶功能的关键氨基酸，其准确预测对酶功能的理解至关重要。传统的基于序列相似性的BLAST方法虽然快速，但依赖于已注释的同源物，限制了其应用范围。为了克服这一限制，研究者们开发了机器学习（ML）方法，但现有的金标准ML方法通常需要高质量的三维结构数据，这在大数据集的应用中显得尤为困难。

为了解决这些挑战，Squidly应运而生。这是一种仅基于序列的工具，采用对比表示学习和生物学启发的配对方案，通过每个标记的蛋白质语言模型嵌入来区分催化和非催化残基。Squidly在催化残基的预测上表现出色，超越了现有的最先进的ML注释方法，同时保持了足够的速度，能够支持大规模数据库的筛选。这一工具的开发使得催化残基的预测更加高效和准确。

此外，Squidly与BLAST的结合，提供了一种高精度和高召回率的工具，能够有效地为分布内外的序列注释催化残基。这一创新不仅提升了催化残基预测的准确性，也为酶的功能研究和应用提供了新的思路和方法，推动了生物技术和相关领域的发展。通过这种方式，Squidly为酶的功能预测提供了一个强有力的工具，具有广泛的应用前景。

items.title: Realistic coupling enables flexible macroscopic traveling waves in the mouse cortex
items.abstract: Traveling waves are ubiquitous in neuronal systems across different spatial scales. While microscopic and mesoscopic waves are relatively well studied, the emergence of macroscopic traveling waves remains less understood. Here, by modeling the mouse cortex using spatial transcriptomic and connectivity data, we show that realistic cortical connectivity can generate a significantly higher level of macroscopic traveling waves than artificial local and uniform connectivity across multiple oscillation frequency bands, with the strongest advantage appearing in the theta, alpha, and beta frequency bands. By probing the model in different dynamic regimes, we find that macroscopic wave activity depends on both network connectivity and excitatory coupling strength, with a non-monotonic dependence on coupling. Together, our work shows how flexible macroscopic traveling waves can emerge in the mouse cortex and offers a computational framework to further study traveling waves in the mouse brain at the single-cell level.
items.title_zh: 真实耦合促进小鼠皮层中的宏观行波灵活性
items.summary_zh: 行波在不同空间尺度的神经系统中普遍存在。尽管微观和中观波动的研究相对成熟，但宏观行波的出现仍不够清楚。本文通过利用空间转录组学和连接性数据对小鼠皮层进行建模，发现真实的皮层连接性能够在多个振荡频率带中产生显著高于人工局部和均匀连接的宏观行波，尤其在θ、α和β频率带中优势最为明显。通过在不同动态状态下探测模型，我们发现宏观波动活动依赖于网络连接性和兴奋性耦合强度，并对耦合呈现非单调依赖关系。我们的研究展示了小鼠皮层中灵活的宏观行波如何产生，并提供了一个计算框架，以进一步在单细胞水平研究小鼠大脑中的行波。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，小鼠皮层中的真实连接性能够显著增强宏观行波的灵活性，尤其在θ、α和β频率带中表现突出，揭示了网络连接性对宏观波动的关键影响。
items.l2_summary:
在神经系统中，行波现象普遍存在于不同的空间尺度上。尽管对微观和中观波动的研究已相对成熟，但宏观行波的形成机制仍不够明确。本文通过空间转录组学和连接性数据对小鼠皮层进行建模，揭示了真实的皮层连接性在多个振荡频率带中能够产生显著高于人工局部和均匀连接的宏观行波，尤其在θ（4-8 Hz）、α（8-12 Hz）和β（12-30 Hz）频率带中表现出明显的优势。

研究中，作者探测了在不同动态状态下的模型，发现宏观波动活动的产生依赖于网络连接性和兴奋性耦合强度，并且对耦合的依赖关系呈现非单调特征。这一发现表明，皮层的真实连接性在宏观行波的形成中起着关键作用，且其灵活性与网络的结构和动态状态密切相关。

通过这一研究，作者不仅展示了小鼠皮层中灵活的宏观行波是如何产生的，还提供了一个计算框架，以便在单细胞水平上进一步研究小鼠大脑中的行波现象。这项研究为理解神经网络的动态特性以及其在信息处理中的作用提供了新的视角，具有重要的科学价值。

items.title: Clinical profiles, referral patterns and low vision aid prescribing across four rehabilitation centres in Ghana: protocol for a multicentre retrospective record review
items.abstract: BackgroundLow vision, defined as best-corrected visual acuity of less than 6/18 in the better eye or a visual field constriction of 20° or less, is a condition in which residual vision may be optimized through optical and non-optical aids. Despite the importance of low vision services in maximizing residual vision and supporting rehabilitation and quality of life, evidence on patient profiles and service delivery in Ghana remains limited. The HM KNUST Low Vision Project aims to address this service gap through a multicentre retrospective medical record review across four centres, characterizing patient profiles, referral patterns, and low vision aid prescribing to inform the strengthening of low vision services in Ghana.MethodsThe HM KNUST Low Vision Project is a collaboration between the Department of Optometry and Visual Science at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana, and the Department of Applied Sciences and Mechatronics at Munich University of Applied Sciences, Germany. As part of this collaboration a comprehensive low vision patient form was developed in collaboration with Ghanaian optometric stakeholders and distributed to clinicians across selected pilot eye care facilities. The form captures biodata, systemic health, visual characteristics, referral patterns, and low vision aid prescriptions to facilitate standardized data collection across centres. Descriptive statistics will summarize patient characteristics, clinical profiles, referral patterns, and low vision aid prescribing. Inferential analyses will assess associations between patient and clinical characteristics, referral patterns, and prescribing patterns across participating centres.DiscussionThis study will provide multicentre evidence on low vision service delivery in Ghana, offering insights to guide rehabilitation services, clinical decision-making, and service planning. The standardized patient form will enable consistent characterization of patient needs, referral pathways, and low vision aid prescribing across centres, establishing an important foundation for improving the accessibility, consistency, and responsiveness of low vision care in Ghana.

items.title: Development and temporal validation of a calibrated machine learning model for in-hospital blood culture positivity using routine clinical data
items.abstract: BackgroundAmong hospitalized patients who have already undergone blood culture collection, routinely available clinical information may support early risk stratification while microbiological results are pending. We developed and temporally validated a calibrated machine learning model for in-hospital blood culture positivity.MethodsThis single-center retrospective study included 44,389 blood culture-related hospitalization records from January 2022 to September 2024. Records from 2022 to 2023 were used for model development and records from 2024 for temporal validation. The primary outcome was at least one laboratory-recorded positive blood culture between index collection and hospital discharge. A Platt-calibrated XGBoost model using demographic characteristics, routine laboratory variables, and missingness indicators was compared with procalcitonin-only and regression-based models. Performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, threshold-specific metrics, decision curve analysis, and SHAP.ResultsThe cohort included 3,555 outcome-positive records (8.01%). In temporal validation, the final XGBoost model achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.798 (95% CI, 0.784–0.813), a PR-AUC of 0.266, a Brier score of 0.0619, and a calibration slope of 1.061. At the 5% threshold, sensitivity was 0.877, specificity 0.570, and negative predictive value 0.983. XGBoost showed a modest improvement over logistic regression with missingness indicators, while an exploratory post hoc Age + PCT + BMI logistic comparator achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.757. Performance was stable in the new-patient validation subset but decreased within adult and pediatric subgroups (ROC-AUC 0.679 and 0.663, respectively). Age, procalcitonin, and body mass index were the dominant contributors.ConclusionThe calibrated model provided moderate discrimination and favorable calibration for hospitalization-level blood culture positivity risk stratification in the pooled temporal validation cohort. Performance varied across age groups, and much of the predictive information was concentrated in age, PCT, and BMI. The model does not predict the index culture result alone or diagnose clinically adjudicated bloodstream infection. Multicenter external and prospective validation using fixed prediction horizons and adjudicated outcomes is required before clinical implementation.

items.title: Modified frailty index versus risk analysis index for 30-day mortality after noncardiac surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: BackgroundmFI and RAI are widely used in noncardiac surgical risk stratification, but they differ in content and data requirements. Because construct validity and outcome discrimination are distinct, we evaluated their prognostic discrimination for 30-day all-cause mortality without treating either instrument as a criterion-standard multidimensional frailty measure.MethodsThis PRISMA-aligned, prospectively registered systematic review used two complementary evidence levels: tool-specific random-effects meta-analyses across independent cohorts and direct within-study comparison. Standalone AUCs were pooled on the logit scale using REML with Hartung–Knapp inference and 95% prediction intervals. Risk of bias was assessed with QUIPS. CFS was analyzed post hoc as secondary exploratory evidence.ResultsSeventy-seven studies were included. For mFI, 39 independent cohorts yielded a pooled AUC of 0.634 (95% CI, 0.618–0.649; 95% prediction interval, 0.551–0.709). For RAI, 30 independent cohorts yielded 0.767 (95% CI, 0.737–0.795; 95% prediction interval, 0.579–0.888). Among 29 dual-tool studies, 21 had source-valid numeric comparisons in which RAI was higher, none had a source-valid numeric comparison in which mFI was higher, 2 supported RAI only qualitatively, and 6 could not be numerically classified; no paired meta-analysis was conducted because within-study covariance or delta-AUC standard errors were unavailable. Fourteen CFS studies were identified; 6 source-confirmed 30-day AUC cohorts yielded a post hoc exploratory AUC of 0.757 (95% CI, 0.618–0.857).ConclusionsRAI showed higher average prognostic discrimination than mFI, a pattern also observed in most directly comparative studies. Separate pooled AUCs are not a formal superiority test because case mix differs across studies. The analysis does not establish construct validity, and CFS evidence remains exploratory.Systematic Review Registrationhttps://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261378778, identifier PROSPERO, CRD420261378778.

items.title: Interdisciplinary care models for functional movement disorders: a systematic review of clinical effectiveness and implications for integrated healthcare delivery
items.abstract: IntroductionFunctional movement disorders (FMD) are a group of highly disabling conditions that are often managed through fragmented care, despite increasing support for interdisciplinary coordinated clinical approaches. This systematic review assessed the clinical efficacy and safety of interdisciplinary interventions in adults diagnosed with FMD.MethodsMEDLINE (Ovid), Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CINAHL, PsycINFO, PEDro, INAHTA, trial registries, and HTA agency websites were searched from inception to October 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing coordinated multidisciplinary/interdisciplinary interventions combining therapeutic components delivered by professionals from different discipline with non-coordinated or non-multidisciplinary care were included. Outcomes of interest included quality of life, motor function, mental health, and reported adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias-2 tool.ResultsMeta-analysis was not feasible because of substantial heterogeneity across studies. Five RCTs published between 2002 and 2024, including 186 participants (105 females) were included. One study was rated as having an overall high risk of bias. Compared with control interventions, interdisciplinary interventions may improve quality of life (physical domain) and motor function in the short to medium term, although findings were inconsistent across studies. No clear benefits were found for mental health status, overall clinical assessment, or social impact. Reported adverse events were infrequent and generally mild.PerspectiveThis systematic review synthesizes current evidence on interdisciplinary care in FMD. While short-term functional improvements have been noted, the uncertainty regarding the sustainability of these effects and their possible psychosocial impact underscores the necessity for rigorous longitudinal research in this population.Systematic Review RegistrationOSF (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/56GYX).

items.title: Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, with spontaneous transdural and calvarial invasion: a case report and literature review
items.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM), IDH-wildtype, is the most aggressive adult-type diffuse glioma. Although extracranial spread may occur after craniotomy, radiotherapy, or other interventions, spontaneous transdural and calvarial invasion before treatment is exceedingly rare. We report a 37-year-old woman who presented with long-standing right temporal-parietal headache and acute worsening with vomiting. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a right temporal mass with intratumoral hemorrhage, peritumoral edema, and contiguous extension through the dura and temporal bone into the temporalis muscle. The lesion was resected through a transcranial approach, and postoperative imaging showed gross total resection. Histological examination demonstrated an infiltrating high-grade glial neoplasm with brisk mitotic activity and palisading necrosis. Immunohistochemical and molecular findings, including the absence of IDH1/IDH2 mutations, supported a diagnosis of glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4. At 18 months after surgery, the patient remained alive. This case highlights a rare pattern of primary extracranial extension in GBM and suggests direct contiguous transdural invasion as a plausible route of spread in the absence of prior intervention.

items.title: Adapting the Girandole framework for cross-disciplinary social justice reflection in health professions education
items.abstract: Equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) are increasingly embedded within the standards and strategic priorities of health professions education. However, persistent inequities, hidden curricula and differences between institutional commitments and learners' lived experiences indicate a need for approaches that move beyond policy compliance towards critical, socially informed reflection. This Perspective paper explores the cross-disciplinary adaptation of the Girandole Framework, originally developed in nursing education, for application across health professions education. The framework uses six interconnected domains—Power, Hidden Curriculum, Professional Values, Personal Values, Culture, and EDI Education and Awareness—to support examination of the individual, cultural and structural influences shaping educational and professional experiences. An exploratory cross-disciplinary workshop involving healthcare professional students informed the adaptation of the framework. Informal discussions suggested that Power, Culture, and Personal and Professional Values were readily connected to learners' experiences. In contrast, Hidden Curriculum and EDI Education and Awareness required clearer language, practical examples and additional educational scaffolding. These insights informed the refinement of the framework's reflective prompts and the development of examples relevant to nursing, pharmacy, biomedical science and transferrable to other health professions. The adapted Girandole offers a shared language through which students and educators can critically examine power relationships, informal norms, professional cultures and educational omissions. Potential future applications include clinical and laboratory placements, professionalism teaching, portfolio-based learning, interprofessional education and curriculum review; however, these applications require empirical evaluation. The framework is intended to complement established reflective models by foregrounding equity and social justice. Further student–educator co-production and empirical evaluation are needed to assess its contribution to EDI literacy, belonging, reflective practice and meaningful organisational change across health professions curricula.

items.title: Case Report: Beyond the stomach: the role of preoperative imaging in assessing regurgitation risk in patients with esophageal dilatation: a report of two cases
items.abstract: BackgroundPerioperative regurgitation of gastric or esophageal contents remains a severe complication during anesthesia. While standard fasting protocols and rapid sequence induction (RSI) are routinely employed, esophageal dilatation creates a hidden reservoir for retained food and secretions that conventional methods often fail to mitigate. Furthermore, standard gastric ultrasound lacks the field of view to detect mid-to-proximal esophageal pooling.Case presentationWe present two parallel cases emphasizing this critical challenge. Case 1 involves a 68-year-old male with esophageal carcinoma who experienced massive regurgitation of white foam during RSI, despite five days of preoperative fasting. Airway security was ultimately achieved after intensified suctioning. Case 2 describes a 42-year-old female with achalasia and marked esophageal dilatation. Informed by preoperative computed tomography (CT) and barium swallow imaging, she was safely managed using targeted pre-anesthetic conscious endoscopic suctioning, leading to an uneventful induction and peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM).ConclusionThese cases highlight the limitations of conventional fasting in managing proximal pooling. They underscore the diagnostic value of preoperative cross-sectional imaging, such as CT, when clinically indicated. Active pre-induction decompression, specifically through tailored endoscopic evacuation, is a valuable adjunctive strategy for preventing perioperative regurgitation in selected patients with megaesophagus.

items.title: Identification and validation of early vital sign trajectory subphenotypes for risk stratification in sepsis-associated liver injury: a multicenter retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: BackgroundSepsis-associated liver injury (SALI) is a serious clinical syndrome with heterogeneity in outcome among affected individuals. Physiological changes that are critical to outcome prediction are not considered in the existing system of stratification based on single-point observations. This could compromise the effectiveness of individualized treatment.ObjectiveTo develop and validate dynamic clinical subphenotypes of SALI using early vital sign trajectories.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 1,159 patients from MIMIC-IV as the derivation cohort and 168 patients from the Second Xiangya Hospital as the external validation cohort. Early vital sign trajectories within 12 h of ICU admission were summarized as trajectory-derived features and clustered using K-means. Candidate solutions (k = 2–6) were assessed using internal clustering metrics and bootstrap stability. A four-cluster solution was retained as an exploratory partition, considering trajectory interpretability and subgroup sizes. Clinical characteristics, organ support, and mortality outcomes were compared across the identified subphenotypes.ResultsFour exploratory SALI subphenotypes with distinct early vital sign trajectories were identified, ranging from relatively stable profiles to marked hemodynamic and physiological stress. Subphenotype 3 exhibited the most stable vital signs and was associated with lower adjusted 28-day (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.56–0.97) and 90-day mortality (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.59–0.97) compared with the highest-risk Subphenotype 4. These prognostic differences were consistently replicated in the external cohort, supporting short- to intermediate-term prognostic generalizability.ConclusionEarly vital sign trajectories identified exploratory SALI groups associated with differences in 28-day and 90-day mortality. Their reproducibility, incremental prognostic value, and clinical utility require further evaluation.

items.title: Concurrent Bartholin gland and perianal abscesses in a woman: a case report of a diagnostic challenge
items.abstract: BackgroundBartholin gland abscess and perianal abscess are common suppurative infections involving anatomically adjacent regions of the female perineum. Because both conditions may present with localized pain and swelling, distinguishing their respective origins and determining the extent of infection can be challenging. The concomitant occurrence of these two abscesses is uncommon, and its diagnostic and therapeutic considerations remain poorly characterized. We report a rare case of concomitant Bartholin gland and perianal abscesses and describe the diagnostic process and multidisciplinary surgical management.Case presentationAn 18-year-old woman presented with progressive perineal and perianal pain and swelling. Pelvic computed tomography demonstrated abscess formation involving the perianal and left perineal soft tissues, and a possible communication between the two lesions was initially suspected. Emergency surgery was performed. The perianal abscess was incised and drained, and an infected anal gland was identified and excised, with bridge drainage established between the drainage incisions. Intraoperative exploration revealed no communication between the perianal abscess and the adjacent perineal lesion. Following gynecological consultation, the separate left vulvar abscess was drained and treated with Jacobi ring fistulization. Culture of the perineal abscess grew Escherichia coli, whereas the perianal abscess culture showed no bacterial growth. Follow-up magnetic resonance imaging 1 month after surgery demonstrated a cystic lesion in the anatomical region of the left Bartholin gland, supporting the Bartholin gland origin of the previously drained perineal abscess. The patient showed satisfactory clinical recovery, with complete healing of the perianal and perineal wounds at 4 months and no evidence of recurrent abscess during the available follow-up.ConclusionConcomitant Bartholin gland and perianal abscesses may be difficult to distinguish because of their overlapping clinical manifestations and anatomical proximity. Clinicians should consider the possibility of multiple independent or potentially related infectious foci and systematically evaluate adjacent anatomical regions. Careful physical examination, appropriate imaging, intraoperative assessment, and timely multidisciplinary collaboration can facilitate accurate diagnosis and individualized surgical management.

items.title: Expect the unexpected: cervical gastric-type adenocarcinoma in situ in a patient with long-standing Peutz-Jeghers syndrome — a case report and literature review
items.abstract: BackgroundPeutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS) is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by germline mutations in the STK11 tumor suppressor gene, associated with a significantly elevated lifetime risk of various malignancies. Gastric-type endocervical adenocarcinoma (G-EAC) and its precursor lesions represent one of the most challenging gynecologic manifestations due to their “deceptively bland” appearance, HPV-independent nature, and propensity to evade routine screening, often leading to delayed diagnosis and poor prognosis.Case presentationWe report a 37-year-old woman with a 30-year history of PJS, presenting with persistent watery vaginal discharge for one year. Despite negative cervical cytology, negative HPV testing, normal colposcopic findings, and inconclusive imaging, her request for hysterectomy was initially declined due to absence of definitive malignant features. The patient subsequently sought care at a tertiary referral center in Shanghai, where post-hysterectomy pathological examination unexpectedly confirmed cervical gastric-type adenocarcinoma in situ (GAS-AIS).ConclusionThis case highlights a critical message: a PJS patient with persistent watery vaginal discharge may harbor gastric-type cervical glandular neoplasia despite negative cytology, negative HPV testing, apparently normal cervical examination, and inconclusive imaging. Persistent watery discharge in this specific population should be considered a “red flag” for gastric-type lesions, which may arise from lobular endocervical glandular hyperplasia (LEGH). For PJS patients with persistent unexplained vaginal discharge, we suggest that clinical suspicion — rather than cytology or colposcopy findings — should be the primary trigger for diagnostic excisional procedures. We present a comprehensive literature review of PJS-associated G-EAC and advocate for updated surveillance protocols, including random cervical biopsies or excisional procedures in symptomatic PJS patients, regardless of colposcopic findings.

items.title: Effects of liraglutide on blood pressure and renal function in patients with type 2 diabetic nephropathy: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
items.abstract: ObjectivesThe effects of liraglutide on blood pressure in patients with T2DN remain unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of liraglutide on blood pressure and renal function in patients with T2DN.MethodsWe conducted comprehensive searches of Web of Science, PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Elsevier ScienceDirect, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP databases. Eligible studies were RCTs of ≥12 weeks’ duration evaluating liraglutide for T2DN. Two independent reviewers screened citations, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool. Statistical analyses were performed in Stata 17.0 and RevMan 5.4, with effect sizes presented as RR or MD and 95% CI. The Cochrane Q test and I2 statistic were used to quantify statistical heterogeneity.ResultsThis meta-analysis included 23 RCTs involving 1,723 participants. Compared with the control group, liraglutide significantly reduced SBP [MD = −5.00, 95% CI (−7.17, −2.84)], while no significant effect was observed on DBP. In addition, liraglutide was associated with favorable changes in some renal biomarkers, as evidenced by reductions in Scr, UACR, Cys-C, BUN, and β2-MG, as well as elevations in eGFR. Improvements were also observed in glycemic control, lipid profiles, BMI, and inflammatory markers. Subgroup analyses indicated dose-dependent differences in UACR and LDL-C. In addition, both UACR and Scr were affected by intervention-regimen type, while HbA1c was affected by baseline albuminuria category. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings, and adjustment for publication bias did not alter the statistical significance of the key outcomes.ConclusionLiraglutide may be associated with favorable changes in selected BP, renal, metabolic, and inflammatory outcomes in patients with T2DN. However, further high-quality studies are needed to confirm these findings.Systematic Review Registrationhttps://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251232844, PROSPERO CRD420251232844.

items.title: A multi-class fundus disease classification framework based on self-supervised contrastive learning and dual-branch network
items.abstract: IntroductionFundus diseases including diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and age-related macular degeneration are primary causes of blindness worldwide. Manual interpretation of retinal images is time-consuming and heavily reliant on clinical expertise. Although deep learning has shown promise in automated fundus image analysis, its performance remains highly data-dependent, requiring large amounts of expert annotations. Moreover, single-architecture models may have limited capacity to capture the diverse pathological features present in fundus images.MethodsThis study proposes a unified framework integrating self-supervised contrastive pre-training with a hybrid dual-branch architecture. Pre-training on unlabeled fundus images enables the model to learn generalizable representations, thereby reducing reliance on manual annotations. The dual-branch design combines EfficientNet-B4 for fine-grained detail extraction and MambaOut for large receptive field modeling. Their outputs are adaptively fused via a learnable cross-fusion module. A dendritic classifier is adopted to further improve classification performance. Comprehensive evaluations were conducted on two public datasets, OIHC and FIVES.ResultsOn the OIHC dataset, the proposed model achieved an F1-score of 96.32 ± 0.38% and a Kappa coefficient of 95.89 ± 0.43%. On the FIVES dataset, it attained 95.10 ± 0.54% and 93.49 ± 0.71%. The macro-average AUC exceeded 98% on both datasets. Ablation studies demonstrated the contribution of each component to the overall performance.ConclusionThis study indicates that combining self-supervised pre-training with a hybrid dual-branch architecture is a feasible approach for multi-class fundus disease classification. Interpretability analyses suggest that the model's attention regions partially overlap with clinically relevant pathological features. The framework achieved competitive performance on both datasets, showing its potential utility in scenarios with limited annotated data. Future work will focus on multi-center validation and model compression for lightweight architecture design.

items.title: Healthcare professionals’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding perioperative ischemic stroke in elderly patients
items.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate healthcare professionals’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to perioperative ischemic stroke in elderly patients.MethodsA single-center, cross-sectional survey was conducted at a tertiary hospital in Ningxia, China, between 1 March 2025 and 1 June 2025. Healthcare professionals were recruited by convenience sampling and completed a structured questionnaire covering demographic information and their KAP regarding perioperative ischemic stroke.ResultsA total of 273 valid responses were included in the final analysis. The majority of respondents were physicians (75.46%), with most affiliated with anesthesiology departments (86.08%). The scores for knowledge, attitude, and practice were 14.41 ± 4.22 (possible range: 0–20), 36.77 ± 3.57 (possible range: 8–40), and 30.07 ± 6.51 (possible range: 8–40), respectively. Structural equation modeling showed that knowledge, attitude, and practice were positively interrelated, whereas training related to perioperative ischemic stroke and specialization in elderly patient care showed negative associations with knowledge or practice (β range: −0.287 to 0.352; all P < 0.05). Knowledge was also indirectly associated with practice through attitude, whereas training and specialization in elderly care showed negative indirect associations with attitude and practice.ConclusionHealthcare professionals exhibited inadequate perceived knowledge, positive attitudes, and suboptimal practices regarding perioperative ischemic stroke in elderly patients. These findings underscore the necessity for targeted, evidence-based educational interventions to strengthen knowledge awareness and practice-related competencies, thereby addressing the observed gaps between perceived knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices.

items.title: Amelanotic subungual melanoma becoming clinically apparent within 24 h after minor blunt trauma: a case report
items.abstract: Amelanotic subungual melanoma (ASM) is a rare variant of nail unit melanoma (NUM) lacking melanin pigmentation, frequently misdiagnosed as a benign post-traumatic or infectious lesion. To our knowledge, ASM becoming clinically apparent within 24 h following minor blunt trauma has not been reported previously. We report the case of a 66-year-old male who presented with a persistent flesh-colored nodule beneath his right thumbnail that was manifested within 24 h after minor blunt trauma caused by nail clippers. The lesion was non-tender, non-pigmented, and unresponsive to 2 weeks of antibiotic therapy. Histopathology revealed diffuse subepidermal proliferation of atypical cells with signet-ring morphology. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrated positivity for vimentin, HMB45, and Melan-A, and negativity for cytokeratin 5 (CK5) and S-100. Ki-67 was approximately 30%; Breslow thickness was 2.5 mm. Final diagnosis: ASM, AJCC stage IIA (T3aN0M0). Diagnostic excisional biopsy with a 2-mm margin was performed; sentinel lymph node biopsy of two axillary lymph nodes was negative. At 1-year follow-up, no local recurrence or distant metastasis was observed. This case demonstrates that ASM can become clinically evident within 24 h after acute trauma, likely through unmasking of a pre-existing subclinical tumor. For post-traumatic nail lesions unresponsive to antibiotics, early biopsy with a comprehensive IHC panel (including Melan-A, HMB45, and S-100) is essential.

items.title: Low arterial oxygen-content burden during the first 24 h and hospital mortality in mechanically ventilated adults: analyses of MIMIC-IV and eICU
items.abstract: BackgroundArterial oxygen content (CaO2) combines hemoglobin-bound and dissolved oxygen. A time-weighted CaO2 deficit could capture changing anemia and desaturation that a hemoglobin-only summary misses. We examined its association with hospital mortality and its added value beyond hemoglobin.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, we included mechanically ventilated adults from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) and eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU). The MIMIC-IV 25th percentile of the first matched CaO2 value (12.48 mL O2/dL) was prespecified as an empirical cutoff and was applied unchanged to eICU. The first-24-h burden integrated the time-weighted deficit below this cutoff. Models were adjusted for demographics and diagnosis-derived case mix. We compared CaO2 burden with hemoglobin burden calculated at the same blood-gas time points and performed landmark, measurement-coverage, severity, and post hoc peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2)-stratified analyses.ResultsBurden was available for 14,050 MIMIC-IV and 20,780 eICU stays. CaO2 was strongly correlated with hemoglobin (r = 0.965 and 0.949, respectively), which explained R2 = 0.932 and 0.901 of first-measurement CaO2 variation, respectively; median dissolved-oxygen contributions were 2.9% and 2.5%, respectively. Per 1-SD higher burden, adjusted odds ratios for hospital mortality were 1.33 (95% confidence interval 1.28–1.39) in MIMIC-IV and 1.29 (1.24–1.35) in eICU. Additional Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation adjustment attenuated the eICU estimate to 1.14 (1.10–1.19), while 24-h landmark estimates were 1.26 (1.21–1.32) and 1.19 (1.14–1.25), respectively. Cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) gains over matched hemoglobin burden were 0.006 and 0.010, respectively, and calibration was similar. In post hoc analyses, hemoglobin explained less CaO2 variation when first SpO2 was <90% (R2 = 0.787 and 0.682, respectively) than when it was ≥95% (R2 = 0.973 and 0.978, respectively); corresponding AUROC gains were 0.045 and 0.044 versus 0.002 in both databases.ConclusionIn cohorts dominated by preserved oxygen saturation, low CaO2 was predominantly an anemia-related signal, and its association with mortality was substantially attenuated by illness-severity adjustment. The burden is best viewed as a compact observational summary of the depth and duration of low arterial oxygen content, not as an independent measure of tissue oxygenation, a superior prediction model, or a treatment target.

items.title: Biomarker-guided immunotherapy in osteosarcoma: from immune microenvironment profiling to patient stratification and combination strategies
items.abstract: Osteosarcoma remains a therapeutically difficult malignancy, particularly after metastatic relapse, and immune checkpoint blockade or adoptive cell therapy has not reproduced the durable responses achieved in more immunogenic cancers. The central translational problem is not a complete absence of immune activity, but marked interpatient, intratumoral, and spatial heterogeneity in immune access, antigen presentation, myeloid suppression, stromal exclusion, and target-antigen expression. This Mini Review synthesizes recent single-cell and spatial profiling studies with tissue, circulating, and clinical biomarker evidence to define a practical framework for biomarker-guided immunotherapy. Osteosarcoma ecosystems can contain lymphoid-excluded, myeloid-dominant, angiogenic-hypoxic, checkpoint-rich, and antigen-high states that may coexist within the same patient. Consequently, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) alone is unlikely to function as a reliable treatment-selection marker. A composite assessment integrating human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class I and antigen-processing competence, CD8/regulatory T-cell topology, macrophage and myeloid-derived suppressor cell programs, vascular and extracellular-matrix barriers, and quantitative surface-antigen density is more biologically defensible. Dynamic measurements, including circulating tumor DNA, soluble B7-H3, exosomal immune signals, and serial imaging, may complement tissue profiling but remain investigational. Clinical experience with checkpoint inhibitors, antiangiogenic combinations, mifamurtide, HER2-directed approaches, and emerging B7-H3-, GD2-, ALPL-1-, CD166-, IL-11Ralpha-, and NKG2D-based cellular therapies underscores the need to match mechanism to phenotype. Prospective studies should therefore use standardized, spatially resolved, and longitudinal biomarker panels to enrich trials, distinguish prognostic from predictive effects, and adapt therapy when immune exclusion or antigen escape emerges.

items.title: Osteopathic manipulative treatment as an adjunct therapy in a pediatric patient with chronic pancreatitis and visceral hyperalgesia: a case report
items.abstract: BackgroundChronic abdominal pain arising from visceral hyperalgesia is difficult to manage, and the use of osteopathic manipulative medicine in pancreatitis-associated visceral hyperalgesia is rarely described. This case adds to the literature by highlighting a potential integrative, mechanism-informed approach for pain modulation in a complex pediatric patient.CaseA 17-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis in the setting of a heterozygous SPINK1 N34S (c.101A > G; p.Asn34Ser) variant, presented with acute-on-chronic abdominal pain severe enough to require escalating opioid therapy; imaging demonstrated calcifications, edema, and peripancreatic fluid collections. A multimodal treatment plan was initiated that included gabapentin, nortriptyline, and targeted osteopathic manipulative treatment. A secretin-enhanced MRCP obtained during a prior admission one month earlier demonstrated pancreatic calcifications, edema, and peripancreatic fluid collections. During the current hospitalization, serum lipase decreased from 979 U/L on admission to 90 U/L by hospital day 3, when gabapentin, nortriptyline, and targeted osteopathic manipulative treatment were initiated as part of a multimodal treatment plan. The patient had two sessions of osteopathic treatment and they were each associated with reductions in pain without adverse effects. As-needed opioid medications were discontinued by discharge as part of a multimodal therapy plan. The patient remained pain-free at one-month follow-up with minimal opioid use, suggesting a potential role for osteopathic manipulative medicine as part of a multimodal strategy in the treatment of chronic pancreatitis related pain. At three-month follow-up, the patient reported pain rated 4/10 occurring several times per week and subsequently underwent total pancreatectomy with islet autotransplantation for definitive management.ConclusionThis case describes an association between OMT and short-term pain improvement within a multimodal treatment strategy for chronic pancreatitis-related visceral pain. Although causality cannot be established from a single uncontrolled observation, the findings support further investigation of OMT as a potential adjunctive therapy in pediatric patients with chronic pancreatitis and secondary visceral hyperalgesia.

items.title: Explainable machine learning for preoperative prediction of acute kidney injury after intertrochanteric fracture surgery in older adults
items.abstract: BackgroundAcute kidney injury (AKI) is an important postoperative complication in older patients undergoing surgery for intertrochanteric femoral fracture. This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate an explainable model for preoperative AKI risk assessment.MethodsThis retrospective study included 616 patients aged ≥60 years, including 54 (8.8%) who developed postoperative AKI. Candidate predictors were processed and selected using development-cohort data, and seven machine-learning algorithms were compared. Model performance was assessed across 100 repeated stratified 70/30 partitions and by 500-repetition model-specific and complete-pipeline bootstrap analyses. Calibration, decision-curve analysis, and SHAP were used to evaluate and interpret the selected model.ResultsThe reported Naive Bayes model comprised baseline serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, chloride, uric acid, and chronic kidney disease or renal insufficiency. Across 100 repeated partitions, its mean validation AUC was 0.7231 (SD, 0.0260). The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.8004 for the fixed five-predictor Naive Bayes specification and 0.756 when the complete development pipeline was repeated; the latter analysis yielded a corrected Brier score of 0.084, calibration intercept of 0.02, and calibration slope of 1.70. In the original algorithm-comparison cohort, the observed AUC was 0.795 (95% CI, 0.698–0.892). When the first serum creatinine measurement obtained after admission was used as the alternative reference value, the number of AKI events decreased from 54 to 43 and the validation AUC was 0.706 (95% CI, 0.586–0.826).ConclusionThe model showed moderate internal discrimination across repeated partitions. Model-specific and complete-pipeline bootstrap analyses provided complementary estimates of internal optimism. The model may complement routine preoperative renal assessment while its calibration and transportability are evaluated in additional cohorts.

items.title: Clinical challenges in vaccine and monoclonal antibody development against ESCAPE pathogens: insights from EMA scientific advice procedures
items.abstract: BackgroundCombating ESCAPE pathogens (E. faecium, S. aureus, C. difficile, A. baumannii, P. aeruginosa, and Enterobacteriaceae) remains a major public health concern due to their treatment resistance and immune evasion. Vaccines and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) are promising solutions, yet only one mAb is licensed and no vaccine has reached that stage. To identify recurring clinical challenges, we analyzed final advice letters (FALs) issued through the European Medicines Agency's (EMA) Scientific Advice procedure.MethodsWe searched both the Paul-Ehrlich-Institut local database and the EMA database for FALs on vaccines and mAbs targeting ESCAPE pathogens. We included FALs that matched the pathogen and product criteria and addressed clinical development. We excluded those focused solely on quality, non-clinical, safety, or post-marketing aspects. From the included FALs, we extracted information across four main categories: primary endpoint, statistical analyses, study population, and study design. Regulatory responses were classified as fully, silently, partially, or not endorsed. We subsequently reviewed related clinical trial protocols to assess whether recommendations were implemented and to provide a narrative summary of changes to the development programs.ResultsWe included 14 FALs for each of the two medicine categories, related to six vaccine and 13 mAb trials. To address common challenges across the primary endpoints, regulators recommended selecting single, infection-related endpoints and emphasized precise clinical and laboratory case definitions to ensure attribution of infection to the target pathogen. They further advised on incorporating supportive evidence, such as subgroup analyses of cases or inflammation markers, direct microbiological or indirect measures (e.g., antibiotic use, hospital stay), or survival-related endpoints. Recommendations for study populations focused on refining the inclusion/exclusion criteria to identify those most likely to benefit. Regulators also advised on changes in the statistical analysis plan (mainly due to lower-than-expected incidence) and generally discouraged single pivotal trials.ConclusionThe development of vaccines and mAbs against ESCAPE pathogens is challenged by pathogen diversity, unpredictable infection rates, heterogeneous trial populations, and diagnostic uncertainty. In a field with no one-size-fits-all development pathway, early regulatory interaction and multidisciplinary disease-expert input are essential to reduce uncertainty and support robust, efficient clinical development programs.

items.title: Extensive vulvar and perianal langerhans cell histiocytosis with clinical improvement during low-dose thalidomide and topical therapy: a case report
items.abstract: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) involving the female genital region is uncommon and can closely resemble chronic inflammatory, infectious, or neoplastic vulvar diseases. We report a case of a 35-year-old woman with a 6-month history of recurrent painful brownish-red plaques, nodules, erosions, and ulcerations that began in the perianal region and subsequently extended to the vulva. Topical fusidic acid only provided temporary symptomatic relief. Histopathological examination revealed epidermal erosion and crusting, acanthosis, elongated rete ridges, and a dense dermal and subcutaneous infiltrate containing numerous large histiocytes with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and focal nuclear grooves. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed that the lesional cells exhibited positivity for S100, CD1a, and langerin and negative for HMB45, SOX10, ALK-1A4, and BRAF V600E. Broader molecular testing for MAPK-pathway alterations was not performed, and the lesion was therefore described as BRAF V600E-immunonegative rather than genetically BRAF/MAPK wild type. The pathological diagnosis was vulvar LCH, with clinically suspected involvement of the perianal region. Positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) revealed an enlarged cervical lymph node, with no other abnormalities documented; its relationship to LCH could not be determined. Oral thalidomide (50 mg nightly) was subsequently administered while topical Pevisone was continued. Symptomatic improvement, particularly pain relief, was observed after 1 week, and further clinical improvement of the anogenital lesions was documented at 3 months. Because both therapies were used concomitantly, the independent contribution of thalidomide could not be determined. This case underscores the diagnostic challenges associated with anogenital LCH and documents short-term clinical improvement during a low-dose thalidomide-containing regimen without establishing thalidomide monotherapy efficacy. It also highlights the necessity for biopsy, comprehensive systemic evaluation, and ongoing follow-up.

items.title: Linear NeuroPaint: An Efficient Baseline for Cross-Session Neural Alignment and Inpainting
items.abstract: Large-scale Neuropixels recordings sample many brain areas, but no single experimental session records every area of interest. NeuroPaint, a transformer-based autoencoder, integrates such recordings by aligning area-specific latent dynamics across sessions and "inpainting" activity in unrecorded areas. Could a linear model, which would be computationally efficient and potentially more interpretable, suffice to achieve this? To address this question, we introduce Linear NeuroPaint, a linear variant of NeuroPaint, and evaluate it on two multi-area Neuropixels datasets. Linear NeuroPaint achieves strong predictive performance on recorded areas, however, it is less accurate than nonlinear models at cross-area inpainting, despite extensive hyperparameter optimization. Moreover, its parameters are not readily interpretable: incomplete cross-session alignment leads parameter-defined neuron clusters to exhibit heterogeneous response profiles. Together, these results show that linear transformations are insufficient for cross-session alignment and cross-area prediction. Nevertheless, Linear NeuroPaint provides a computationally efficient baseline for benchmarking multi-session neural models.
items.authors: Yao, Y. J.; Xia, J.; Paninski, L.; Miller, K. D.

items.title: Scalable methylome-transcriptome profiling resolves clonal organization in human hematopoiesis
items.abstract: Understanding human tissue maintenance and remodeling requires linking clonal ancestry to molecular state, yet scalable joint measurement remains challenging. Here, we introduce Droplet-MT and an integrated computational workflow for joint transcriptome and methylome profiling at ~10,000 cells per library. Methylation epimutations enable mutation-independent clonal reconstruction from high-coverage methylomes, while reference-based label transfer assigns cells to established clones at ~0.2% CpG coverage, reducing sequencing cost. Clone-aggregated somatic variants provide genetic annotation without additional single-cell genotyping. Across ~21,000 paired profiles from healthy blood and longitudinal acute myeloid leukemia, we resolved small and expanded clones with heterogeneous lineage output. In leukemia, the framework distinguished changes in malignant clonal abundance, state remodeling within persistent clones, and recovery of healthy polyclonal hematopoiesis. Malignant monocytes remained transcriptionally and epigenetically distinct from healthy and recovery-associated cells despite treatment-associated remodeling. Droplet-MT enables scalable analysis of human tissues by linking clonal organization with molecular state and retrospective genetic annotation.
items.authors: Shao, J.; Chen, M.; Liu, Y.; Sun, J.; Zhang, G.; Yan, Z.-Y.; Lin, H.; Ren, M.; Pei, S.; Peng, J.; Gong, Y.; WANG, S.

items.title: An iPSC-based experimental framework for investigating phenotypic variation associated with Jomon ancestry in the present-day Japanese population
items.abstract: Ancestry-related genomic variation may contribute to phenotypic diversity. However, its cellular consequences remain difficult to evaluate. To address this, we developed a human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-based framework for investigating such phenotypes. We used the Japanese population as a model of Jomon-related and continental East Asian ancestry admixture. Jomon ancestry, estimated using the Jomon allele score (JAS), was associated with clinical measures, including renal-related traits and serum triglycerides in 34,152 Tohoku Medical Megabank participants. Peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomics of donors from the upper and lower extremes of the JAS distribution (n = 10) suggested group-level differences in immune-related gene expression. To test whether the serum triglyceride association coincided with hepatic cellular phenotypes, we differentiated hiPSCs from these donors into hepatocyte-like cells. Neither intracellular triglycerides nor lipid-related gene expression differed between groups. These findings highlight the value of a genetically characterized hiPSC-based framework for investigating ancestry-associated phenotypes across cellular contexts.
items.authors: Nakamura, Y.; Watanabe, Y.; Tanabe, H.; Hirai, A.; Higashi, K.; Kurokawa, K.; Toyoda, A.; Kato, T.; Tsukahara, M.; Koganebuchi, K.; Hamazaki, Y.; Takebe, T.; Imamura, M.; Ishida, T.; Ohashi, J.; Oota, H.

items.title: Cromosomal genomes assemblies of twelve sheep breeds
items.abstract: The sheep research community benefits from a genome assembly that has been refined over the last 15 years. However, the rich diversity of sheep breeds suggests that a single individual genome is not enough to represent the species full genomic content. Third-generation sequencing technologies have recently made it possible to generate high quality assemblies that should enable to elucidate unique and/or complex phenotype determinisms depending on genetic structural variations. In the SeqOccin project, twelve breeds were selected to represent (mostly French) sheep genetic diversity: Basco-Bearnaise, Black Belly, Blanche du Massif Central, Corse, Ile de France, Lacaune, Manech Tete Noire, Noire du Velay, Ouessant, Rambouillet, Vendeen, Soay. High-molecular-weight DNA was extracted from blood samples and subjected to long read whole-genome sequencing. The reads were used to generate de novo assemblies and were aligned onto the public reference to call structural variants. PacBio HiFi and parental Illumina reads were used to assemble phased haplotypes of the Lacaune breed. For the other breeds, PacBio raw (CLR) or ONT reads were generated.
