items.abstract: Whether large language models (LLMs) can contribute to non-trivial science, beyond summarising literature and writing routine code, is an open question. We report a case study in which an LLM (Claude) was asked to formulate, implement, verify and parameterise a new equation of state of the statistical associating fluid theory (SAFT) family. The target was a SAFT-VR variant for polar and dipolar molecules in which the segments interact through the isotropic multipolar potential (IMP) of Müller and Gelb, expressed as a temperature-dependent sum of Sutherland terms and treated with the Barker–Henderson perturbation theory of SAFT-VR Mie and SAFT-VR Sum. Over three sessions the LLM produced a stepby-step derivation, a 600-line implementation in the open-source Julia package Clapeyron.jl, a suite of 97 verification tests, a parameter-estimation pipeline applied to DIPPR data for six cyclic ethers, ketones and a sulfide, and a comparison with the group-contribution SAFT-γ
items.authors: Werner A. Müller, Benoit Creton, Carlos Nieto-Draghi, Erich A. Müller

items.title: Adsorption and Separation of Dihydroxybenzenes by Colorimetric Molecular Adsorbing Host•Guest Crystals
items.abstract: Hydrogen-bonded Organic Frameworks (HOFs) form a rapidly expanding alternative to Metal Organic Frameworks (MOFs). Among HOFs, the Molecular Adsorbing Host•Guest ( MAHG ) crystals introduced here combine cucurbit[8]uril (CB[8]) macrocycles and a tetraacid derivative of diphenyl-viologen (TETRAC). Despite their non-porous crystalline framework, MAHG crystals enable the diffusion of dihydroxybenzenes (DHB), which tend to localize in specific crystalline sites. The diffusion of DHB inside the permeable crystals is followed by striking color changes related to the formation of charge-transfer (CT) complexes between the electron-rich DHB and the electron-poor viologen units confined within the CB[8] cavities. Kinetic and crystallographic studies indicate the possible separation of DHB mixtures. This work highlights the potential of MAHG crystals for the rapid detection of DHB via colorimetric changes and their separation in water, offering a promising approach for industrial applications dedicated to hydroquinone and catechol production.
items.authors: Melvin Raulin, Eric Merlet, Florian Ferrer, Isabelle Braccini, Didier Siri, Brice Kauffmann

items.title: From Retrosynthetic Prediction to the Bench: Experimental Evaluation of Computer-Generated Synthetic Routes
items.abstract: Retrosynthesis tools propose bond disconnections and precursor assignments, but the chemist must still evaluate these choices and select reaction conditions and purification before a route can be run. In this work, we examine 53 PostEra Manifold and AiZynthFinder proposals for three small organic targets by combining chemist assessments with selected synthesis outcomes. Proposals were rejected or deprioritised for different reasons: incorrect connectivity, unsupported transformations, or extra steps and costly precursors in routes that would otherwise work. For a methoxy-substituted biaryl ketone, a Suzuki–Miyaura coupling using the chemist-preferred assignment of coupling partners gave 94% isolated yield. For a naphthylphenol, coupling with 2hydroxyphenylboronic acid gave 92% isolated yield with an aryl bromide and 7% with the corresponding chloride under the same procedure. The chloride result supports the chemist’s preference for the bromide, whereas the 92% yield shows that the earlier concern about this boronic acid, based on its behaviour in water, was not limiting under the tested conditions. We therefore propose that each generated route be judged on four separate points: whether it gives the correct target, whether the transformation is chemically supported, whether the route is practical, and whether it has been tested experimentally.
items.authors: Laura d’Andrea, Heidi Fuglsang Christiansen, Casper Steinmann

items.title: Self-quenched growth of monodisperse SnO2 nanocrystals—insensitive to synthesis conditions
items.abstract: Metal oxide thin film fabrication from colloidal nanocrystal dispersions separates the materials synthesis from the device (layer) fabrication, enabling fast solution processing. However, nanocrystal ink syntheses can be still too complex to be truly scalable for large-area ultra-lowcost applications such as solar modules. Here, we present a self-quenched (by precipitation) nanocrystal synthesis at room temperature. The synthesis is independent of the precursor concentrations, precursor addition speed (injection vs. slow addition), mixing dynamics of the solutions, reaction duration, and temperature. Crystalline and monodisperse tin(IV) oxide nanocrystals ( 3 nm diameter) are obtained with a near-unity reaction yield. After purification, the nanocrystal surface is modified with acetate ligands and brought into a colloidal dispersion, again with near-unity yield. Nip perovskite solar cells containing tin oxide nanocrystal thin films 2 achieve power conversion efficiencies of at least 21%. This method introduces a highly scalable SnO2 nanocrystal ink synthesis, which may be applicable to other metal oxides for coating technologies such as displays, windows, and perovskite solar modules, as well as the deposition on polymer films.
items.authors: Yongli Lu, Meng-Chen Shih, Shaun Tan, Yu-Kuan Lin, Moungi Bawendi, Matthias J. Grotevent
items.title_zh: 自熄灭法合成单分散SnO2纳米晶体——与合成条件无关
items.summary_zh: 金属氧化物薄膜的制备通过胶体纳米晶体分散液将材料合成与器件（层）制造分开，从而实现快速溶液处理。然而，纳米晶体墨水的合成仍然过于复杂，难以真正实现大面积超低成本应用，如太阳能模块。本文提出了一种在室温下自熄灭（通过沉淀）合成纳米晶体的方法。该合成与前驱体浓度、前驱体添加速度（注入与缓慢添加）、溶液混合动力学、反应时间和温度无关。获得了直径约3纳米的单分散四氧化锡纳米晶体，反应产率接近100%。经过纯化后，纳米晶体表面被乙酸配体修饰，并再次形成胶体分散液，产率同样接近100%。含锡氧化物纳米晶体薄膜的钙钛矿太阳能电池实现了至少21%的光电转换效率。该方法引入了一种高度可扩展的SnO2纳米晶体墨水合成，可能适用于其他金属氧化物的涂层技术，如显示器、窗户和钙钛矿太阳能模块，以及在聚合物薄膜上的沉积。

items.title: Inconsistent odor-threshold measurements limit prediction from molecular structure
items.abstract: Existing work treats odor detection threshold prediction as a supervised regression problem, assuming published thresholds are clean targets. In current public datasets, they are not: values come from different measurement sources and often disagree for the same molecule. Across the three largest public air-phase compilations, thresholds for identical molecules differ systematically by median factors of 3 to 11. Individual source studies vary around a compound’s underlying threshold by about 1.4 log 10 units, so under an independent-source approximation, a new study is expected to differ from the compiled value by about 1.6 log 10 units. This exceeds the best structure-based model’s error against that value (root-mean-square error 1.34), meaning the model matches the published compilation more closely than a new experiment would be expected to. Although averaging multiple studies makes the compiled value more precise, its remaining uncertainty still accounts for at least one-third of the model’s prediction-error variance, and a single source-study threshold has estimated reliability near 0.5. Changing the molecular representation, by comparison, changes root-mean-square error by only about 0.2 log 10 units. We therefore introduce a joint calibration model that places the compilations on a common scale, estimates source-specific offsets and noise, and improves cross-compilation prediction over a simple fixed-offset correction while providing calibrated uncertainty. These results show that progress in odor detection threshold prediction depends not only on better molecular models, but also on better measurements and methods that account for disagreement across data sources.
items.authors: Anand R. Mysorekar, Lekha Challappa

items.title: Spatially Refined Analysis of Emission Burdens and Equity from Light-, Medium-, and Heavy-Duty Vehicle Traffic in the United States
items.abstract: We estimate block-level emission intensities of nitrogen oxides (NO X ) and fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) from on-road vehicle traffic for every census block in the United States, combining MOVES-based emission factors with street level traffic data. We use this spatially refined, computationally efficient, and policy-sensitive metric to evaluate emissions burden. Despite comprising less than 11% of vehicle kilometers traveled, we find that medium- and heavy-duty trucks account for 46% of NO X and 50% of PM 2.5 emission burden nationally — with PM 2.5 burden from trucks dominated by exhaust emissions while tire and brake wear constitute nearly half of light-duty vehicle PM 2.5 burden. People of color face emission burdens averaging 40% above the national mean, with Asian populations exceeding 60%, and lower-income populations face 20–25% higher burdens. Statistically significant racial-ethnic or income disparities are present in 85–89% of US counties. Critically, these disparities are not confined to large metropolitan areas. They are widespread across both urban and rural counties nationwide. We also show that spatial aggregation substantially attenuates estimated disparities of burdened groups, underscoring the importance of spatially refined analysis.
items.authors: Brittany Antonczak, Clare Nelson, Tammy Thompson, Mindi DePaola, Gregory Rowangould

items.title: Electronic and Steric Effects on the Photoswitching and Thermal Relaxation of Ortho-Substituted Pyrazole Azo Phthalimides
items.abstract: A series of ortho-substituted phthalimide–azopyrazole photoswitches bearing CH3, CF3, tert-Bu, and Ph groups was developed to determine how local steric and electronic perturbations control photochemical addressability and thermal Z→E relaxation. The substituents strongly altered the preferred irradiation wavelength while producing modest differences in the attainable Z-rich photostationary states. The CF3 derivative underwent E→Z photoisomerization at 530 nm, whereas the other derivatives were switched at 370 nm. TD-DFT analysis attributes this spectral differentiation to orbital reordering, configuration mixing, and redistribution of oscillator strength within the low-energy excited-state manifold. Thermal Z→E half-lives span more than three orders of magnitude, from 112 s for the CH3 derivative to 73 h for the CF3 derivative. Eyring analysis reveals predominantly entropic differentiation among the CH3, tert-Bu, and Ph derivatives, whereas CF3 persistence is primarily enthalpic. Adiabatic S0 calculations reproduce the experimental stability order but do not account for the substantially negative experimental activation entropies. Relaxed T1 scans and optimized S0/T1 crossing points identify accessible twisted crossing regions. The combined results support a multidimensional relaxation landscape in which CNNC torsion, azo-nitrogen bending, and changes in N=N bond character constitute coupled coordinates whose energetic and configurational accessibility is reshaped by ortho substitution.
items.authors: Sheelbhadra Chatterjee, Kosuke Nakashima, Miroslav Dangalov, Yasuyuki Matsushima, Shin-ichi Hirashima, Tsuyoshi Miura

items.title: Nucleotide-mediated catalytic peptide synthesis from aminonitriles
items.abstract: Aminonitriles are accessible from simple feedstock compounds and their hydrolysis offers an abiotic route to life’s amino acids on the early earth. However, controlled aqueous polymerisation of amino acids into peptides remains challenging. Here we show that peptides can be directly generated and elongated by aminonitriles when the latter are coupled to nucleotides as a phosphoramidate. Upon thiol catalysis and pH shifts, a series of selective reactivities drives iterative peptide bond formation in water. The high energy nitrile bond of aminonitriles circumvents amino acids’ need for concurrent activation chemistry in peptide elongation. Coupling the building blocks of life’s central biopolymers in this manner provides a pathway for early integration of peptides into biology.
items.authors: Luis Ohlendorf, Jyoti Singh, Erica Park, Sofija Spric, Qian Zhang, Josh Maiklem

items.title: Beyond Organic Molecules: MetalLipoDB, a Lipophilicity Dataset for Metal Complexes and Machine Learning Benchmarks
items.abstract: Lipophilicity governs the uptake, distribution and toxicity of drug candidates, yet the experimental logP datasets used to build predictive models contain almost exclusively organic molecules. Here we present MetalLipoDB, a manually curated dataset of 5158 experimental logP and logD values of complexes of 23 metals from 1192 articles, including 556 entries for multinuclear and heterometallic complexes, annotated with the measurement conditions and counterions. The dataset quantifies the inter-study reproducibility of these measurements (0.56 log units) and serves as a benchmark for machine learning, with a mean absolute error of 0.72–0.75 for complexes from unseen articles. For articles with at least four measurements, anchoring the predictions to three measured complexes of the series reduced the error on the remaining complexes from 0.73 to 0.51. MetalLipoDB, the code and an interactive web application (https://biometaldb.streamlit.app/) are openly available to support the design of metal-based drugs.
items.authors: Lev Krasnov, Dmitriy Malikov, Marina A. Kiseleva, Artem Lvov, Sergei V. Tatarin, Stanislav I. Bezzubov

items.title: AI Agents for CRISPR Diagnostics: From Automation to Bounded Autonomy
items.abstract: Recent years have witnessed rapid advances in clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) diagnostics, artificial intelligence (AI), and self-driving laboratories for automation. CRISPR diagnostics have emerged as a promising strategy for earlier disease detection, with Cas12a and Cas13a targeting DNA and RNA, respectively, and converting that recognition into collateral reporter cleavage. In parallel, different subsets of AI have advanced rapidly, with machine learning (ML) interpreting biosensor readouts, and large language models (LLMs) and AI agents applied to automation. Laboratory automation and self-driving platforms reduce the workload of human experimentalists and enable scale-up, having run long unattended campaigns in materials discovery. However, how these advances in AI, CRISPR diagnostics and automation could be integrated to enable a future of autonomous biosensing remains unresolved. In this perspective, we evaluate CRISPR diagnostics as autonomous systems, where analytical metrics alone cannot ensure robustness, failure-mode predictability, recoverability and auditability. We then propose a bounded-autonomy layer in which multimodal evidence, scored by ML, gates a Sense, quality control (QC), Decide, Act and Report loop, with guardrailed LLM agents invoked only when QC flags a run, selecting pre-validated actions under deterministic validation. By tying detectable failure modes to validated recovery actions, we outline a path toward bounded autonomy in CRISPR diagnostics, where a device unable to act safely abstains and escalates.
items.authors: Sina Jamalzadegan, Mahsa Bagi, Sepehr Soltani, Zahra Joudaki, Akhil Penumudy, David Haussler

items.title: The Problem of NMR Data Analysis in Synthetic Chemistry: Why Is It Important to Understand Spectra?
items.abstract: High-resolution NMR (nuclear magnetic resonance) is one of the key methods for establishing the structures of organic compounds. Modern instrumentation and reference data provide a sufficient range of experiments for unambiguous assignment. However, in practice these resources are applied selectively. An assignment is commonly treated as complete once it no longer contradicts the expected structure. It is complete only when the spectrum as a whole has been explained, including signals at odds with that structure. The discussion is built on six papers retracted between 2020 and 2025, in which the reported structure was incorrect and the original assignment rested on NMR data. These cases are not used to estimate how often such errors occur, but to illustrate types of error that keep recurring in the literature. The same errors are then shown in a paper where the structure is correct and firmly supported by orthogonal methods. Two criteria are proposed for assessing a reported spectrum without access to the raw data. The first is the resolution indicated by the multiplet of the residual solvent signal. Therefore, this multiplet should remain visible in spectra reproduced in the Supporting Information. The second is the internal consistency of the reported data. The stated multiplicity must match the number of coupling constants. The notation must also make sense for the structure: simple descriptions such as “d” or “t” are not valid, for example, for the signals of a monosubstituted or unsymmetrically 1,4-disubstituted benzene ring. Automated approaches inherit rather than remove this difficulty: their output is accepted with the same confidence.
items.authors: Artur V. Eshtukov-Shcheglov

items.title: A New Route to Macrobicyclic Dibridgehead Diphopsphines P((CH 2 ) n ) 3 P; Reductive Demetalation of Cage-Like Fe(CO) 3 Adducts
items.abstract: When THF solutions of cage-like trans-Fe(CO) 3 (P((CH 2 ) n ) 3 P) ( 1 , n = a /10, b /12, c /14, d /16, e /18) are exposed to a potassium mirror, reduction occurs to give ferrate salts of the formula 2K + [(R 3 P)(CO) 3 Fe] 2– , as supported by IR data. Following additions of excess CO and methanol, the dibridgehead diphosphines P((CH 2 ) n ) 3 P ( 1a-e ) are isolated as white solids in 61-98% yields (average 80%) as mixtures of in/in and out/out isomers that interconvert by homeomorphic isomerization. This protocol represents an alternative to a photochemical demetalation that requires PMe 3 , as well as oxidative recipes that give dibridgehead diphosphine dioxides 1a-e ·2O with byproducts that are difficult to remove. The practicality of the new route is demonstrated by a half gram-scale synthesis of 1b .
items.authors: Simon M. Popovic, John A. Gladysz

items.title: Synthesis of nitride materials by atmospheric pressure metathesis
items.abstract: Nitride materials have many important technological applications, yet they remain underexplored compared to other classes of compounds, as reflected by the smaller number of reports in databases and literature. The primary reason for this is the difficulty of synthesizing nitrides, which must outcompete energetically stable molecular N 2 and oxide compounds. As a result, bulk synthesis of nitrides often requires high pressure or corrosive fluxes in addition to oxygen-free conditions. We present our perspective on the metathesis technique as an accessible method for synthesizing nitrides at or below atmospheric pressure for the broader chemistry community. To highlight the advantages of this synthesis approach, we also review traditional methods for bulk nitride synthesis, including high pressure techniques, sodium and halide fluxes, and gas- and liquid-ammonia-based routes. We provide a brief tutorial on metathesis reactions including tips and tricks to help researchers get started. Finally, we discuss the future outlook for metathesis reactions, with an opportunity for precise structural selection during nitride synthesis through the controlled formation of stable and metastable polymorphs within the multidimensional potential-energy landscape of material nucleation and growth.
items.authors: Anna Berseneva, Christopher Rom, Rebecca Smaha, Andriy Zakutayev

items.title: Water-Responsive Shape-Memory Origami Enabled by a Washi–Bulk pNIPAAm Hydrogel Hybrid Sheet
items.abstract: Origami transforms two-dimensional sheets into complex three-dimensional forms through folding and has evolved from a traditional art into a versatile design principle for deployable and reconfigurable structures. Here, we develop a water-responsive shape-memory origami sheet by combining highly concentrated poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (bulk pNIPAAm) hydrogel with Japanese kozo paper. Bulk pNIPAAm undergoes pronounced hydrationinduced softening and recovers its permanent shape upon rehydration, whereas the paper scaffold enables the hydrogel to be fabricated and handled as a thin, foldable sheet. Rather than programming only individual active creases, the hybrid sheet allows complex folded three-dimensional configurations to be programmed directly as permanent shapes. Two complementary programming strategies are demonstrated: photopolymerization of precursorimpregnated paper in a pre-folded configuration and post-fabrication programming by local photopolymerization at selected creases. Kozo washi-based hybrid sheets exhibited more than 90% recovery within several seconds in a simple folding test, and Miura-fold, crane, dolphin, and kirigami structures recovered their memorized geometries after unfolding and dehydration-induced temporary fixation. Finally, simply pouring warm water onto a flowershaped structure triggers spontaneous blooming without full immersion. This approach transforms a bulk shape-memory hydrogel into a fold-programmable sheet material and
items.authors: Kohei Murata, Hiroaki Suzuki

items.title: Giant barocaloric effect from spin crossover in a green nitroprusside framework†
items.abstract: The interest in spin crossover for solid-state cooling is growing. We investigate the spin crossover transitions of [Fe(pyridine)2Fe(CN)5NO] and [Fe(pyrazine)Fe(CN)5NO] by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, high-pressure X-ray diffraction, magnetometry, and high-pressure calorimetry. The dehydrated form of the latter compound shows a reversible cooling effect (∆Tad,rev) of ∼15K at 1.2 kbar. This is high in the context of other reported spin-crossover barocalorics, and competitive within the field at large. The excellent performance results from a large barocaloric coefficient (dT1/2/dp = 35K kbar−1). In addition, the one-pot synthesis is simple and free from toxic solvents.
items.authors: Matthew G. Robb, Anthony E. Phillips, Lukas Sippach, Andreas Rydh, Gregor Kieslich, Hanna L B Boström

items.title: Kinetically Synchronized Aqueous Co-precipitation and Hydrothermal Crystallisation of (Mg1−xCox)CO3 Rhombohedral Solid-Solution Nanoparticles: Thermodynamic Feasibility, Ethylene Glycol Kinetic Control, and Prospective Functional Applications
items.abstract: Cobaltoan magnesite, (Mg1−xCox)CO3 (R3c; x = 0–1), has previously been accessible only under extreme solid-state conditions (≥600 °C, ≥15 kbar; Goldsmith Northrop, 1965) or over geological timescales in supergene ore environments (Barton et al., 2014). We report the first deliberate laboratory synthesis of phase-pure (Mg,Co)CO3 solid-solution nanoparticles at 250 °C under autogenous pressure (~40 bar) via a modified polyol-assisted aqueous coprecipitation route. Thermodynamic feasibility is established through saturation-index analysis (SI(CoCO3) = +10.6, ΔG° = −60.5 kJ mol−1; SI(MgCO3) = +2.6, ΔG° = −14.8 kJ mol−1), confirming that both carbonate end-members are thermodynamically driven to precipitate from solution at ambient conditions and that the hydrothermal step supplies kinetic — not thermodynamic — activation energy. The principal kinetic challenge, the seven-order-ofmagnitude disparity in solubility products (Ksp(CoCO3) = 10−13 vs. 6.8×10−6 for MgCO3), is surmounted by ethylene glycol (EG) coordination of Co2+, confirmed in situ by a spontaneous pink→blue colour transition upon EG addition, which elevates the desolvation activation barrier and synchronises Co2+ and Mg2+ precipitation rates. Convergent evidence from five independent characterisation techniques confirms the R3c solid-solution product: (i) PXRD with Vegard's Law analysis of the composition-sensitive (113) reflection yields x(Co) ≈ 0.73 (Sample 3, pre-hydrothermal) and x(Co) ≈ 0.44 (Sample 4, post-hydrothermal); (ii) FTIR reveals a single ν2(CO32−) band at 870 cm−1, intermediate between MgCO3 (880) and CoCO3 (860 cm−1) endmembers — a necessary and sufficient criterion for isomorphic solid-solution identification by infrared spectroscopy; (iii) SEM-EDX shows a continuous unimodal composition distribution (x(Co) = 0.27–0.73) with no bimodal clustering indicative of phase separation; (iv) UV–Vis spectroscopy identifies characteristic Co2+ ligand-field and charge-transfer transitions with a direct optical band gap of ~3.1–3.4 eV; (v) DLS confirms near-monodisperse product (PDI = 0.053, Dh = 306 nm) following hydrothermal treatment, representing an 83% reduction in polydispersity relative to the amorphous precursor (PDI = 0.314). Prospective applications spanning heterogeneous catalysis, Li-ion battery cathode precursors, CO2 mineralisation, photocatalysis, and pH-responsive drug delivery are evaluated on the basis of the crystal chemistry and mixed-metal composition of the product phase.
items.authors: Abdul Haseeb Tanoli, Arfeen, Laiba Irshad Khattak, Tasbiha Rehman Bhatti, Muhammad Muneeb Yousafzai, Tayyaba Ghani

items.title: Electrochemical Detection of Ethanol in Liquid Samples and Simulated Breath: Investigating Calibration, Selectivity, and Preconcentration
items.abstract: Advances in miniaturized and point-of-care electrochemical sensors have expanded their applications in healthcare, environmental monitoring, and public safety. Consequently, it is important to study the principles of these technologies in an undergraduate setting. This experiment uses screen-printed electrodes for electrochemical detection of ethanol and introduces students to electrocatalysis, calibration curves, chemical interference, selectivity, and preconcentration. Students use cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry to make calibration curves and determine ethanol concentrations in ethanol standards and diluted beer and wine samples. Glucose interference is investigated, and a simulated breath experiment demonstrates how selecting breath as the analytical sample and condensing it can eliminate interference while simultaneously preconcentrating ethanol. The activity provides an opportunity to discuss blood alcohol concentration (BAC), breath alcohol concentration (BrAC), and modern alcohol-sensing technologies. This experiment is suitable for upper-level undergraduate courses in analytical chemistry, physical chemistry, and electrochemistry.
items.authors: Benjamin Nelson, Keya Pandey, Oliver Powell, Setareh Soureshjani, Lida Khalafi, Mahsa Hosseini

items.title: Practical In Situ Generation of Phosphorus Pentafluoride as a Metal-Free Potent Lewis Acid
items.abstract: Metal-free potent Lewis acids are of great interest in the pharmaceutical and food industries to avoid metal contaminants. Phosphorus pentafluoride (PF 5 ) is a potent Lewis acid, but its practical use is severely restricted by its gaseous state and corrosiveness. Here we report a simple and convenient method for either the rapid or slow in situ generation of PF 5 from widely available and easy to handle hexafluorophosphate (PF 6 − ) salts and either aluminum chloride (AlCl 3 ) or boron trifluoride etherate (BF 3 ·Et 2 O), respectively. The potency of PF 5 in Lewis acid catalysis is demonstrated in the tandem Friedel–Craft alkylation of thiophene derivatives with ketones, where PF 5 outperforms conventional Lewis acids such as BF 3 ·Et 2 O, AlCl 3 , and SnCl 4 .
items.authors: Roy Lavendomme, Alexia Dussart, Alice Dufau--Malon, Ivan Jabin

items.title: Electron Paramagnetic Resonance on a Tip Reveals Thickness-Dependent Spin Heterogeneity in Two-
items.abstract: Direct characterization of the spin centers that provide the magnetic states of low-dimensional magnetic materials is key to understand whether the magnetic properties arise from defects, interfaces, or surface-specific coordination environments, and how they can thus be employed in devices. The spectroscopic technique par excellence for this purpose is electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) which has seen recent expansion to single spins but remains challenging for nanostructures on insulating surfaces. Here, we overcome this limitation and demonstrate local spin-resonance spectroscopy of nanoscale systems on insulators. We achieve this by combining EPR detection with scanning microwave microscopy (SMM) at X-band frequencies of ≈9.3 GHz, with resonant spin absorptions identified as local field-dependent microwave losses, available by mapping the complex admittance under a swept magnetic field. We demonstrate the potential of the technique on single flakes of the two-dimensional Fe–Ni Hofmann clathrate. The new technique reveals a thickness-dependent evolution from bulk-like toward low-dimensional spinresonance behavior, allowing the investigation of flakes from ≈5-15 nm to 100–200 nm thick, in conditions inaccessible to other surface EPR methods. The observed thickness-dependent response is consistent with increasing contributions from surface, interface, and undercoordinated Fe environments. These new developments allow a unique route to probe dimensional effects in magnetism, make surface effects and defects accessible in insulators, and open the possibility of directly observing EPR not just on atoms and molecules, but on single electronic nanodevices, such as Single Electron Transistors and quantum dots.
items.authors: Gianluca Fabi, Ramon Torres, Maxwell Sparey, Javier Castells-Gil, Christopher S. Allen, Joaquin Soriano-Lopez

items.title: Improved electrostatic machine learning embedding ML/MM scheme for a phosphoryl transfer reaction
items.abstract: The promise of hybrid machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) simulations is to provide QM/MM-quality free energy profiles at a fraction of the cost. One of the challenges is to accurately treat the interaction between the ML subsystem and the MM environment. Here we test the Electrostatic ML Embedding (EMLE) scheme on a minimal model of RNA cleavage in water, which is already challenging due to a doubly charged reactant dissociating into two anions. The original scheme, a MACE potential embedded by an independent EMLE model, is compared with a new EMLE–MACE architecture, in which a single equivariant network predicts the gas-phase energy together with the atomic charges, valence widths, polarizabilities and static dipoles required by the embedding. The models were trained by active learning against M06-2X/def2- TZVP data, with structures selected by query-by-committee from the ML/MM dynamics itself. About 1500 single point calculations were sufficient for stable 100 ps umbrella sampling simulations in 73 windows along the reaction pathway. The EMLE–MACE profile reproduces the reference DFT/MM profile within its sampling error, including a metastable pentacoordinate intermediate. Energy decomposition shows that the static dipoles are essential: without them the static error stays above chemical accuracy even for an ideally trained model, due to the irreducible error of approximating electron density with spherical atoms.
items.authors: Laetitia Kantin, Iñaki Tuñón, Kirill Zinovjev, Elise Duboué Dijon

items.title: First principles study of stability, electronic and optical properties of Diphenylhexatriene under pressure
items.abstract: Using density functional theory (DFT), this work investigated the structural, mechanical, electrical, and optical characteristics of (E,E,E)-1,6-Diphenyl-1,3,5-hexatriene (DPH) under hydrostatic pressures ranging from 0 to 65 GPa.Increasing pressure resulted in systematic lattice compression, with the a-axis exhibiting the greatest contraction.Notwithstanding these structural alterations, no phase transition was seen in this pressure range, suggesting the resilience of DPH's molecular packing.However, when mechanical instability was detected at 65 GPa, as indicated by negative values in the elastic constants and stiffness matrix eigenvalues, structural disintegration started.The electronic band structure study demonstrated a steady decrease in the band gap with increasing pressure, suggesting enhanced electronic conductivity at higher pressures.Furthermore, optical property simulations showed a redshift in dielectric constants, absorption coefficients, and refractive indices, indicating that DPH might be adjustable for optoelectronic uses.The behavior of molecular crystals under pressure is revealed by this research, which could have implications for their use in high-performance organic electronics and photovoltaics.
items.authors: Ramen Patra, Mousumi Das

items.title: Accelerating discovery of phosphorescent blue OLED emitters using chemical foundation models
items.abstract: In OLED displays, phosphorescent emitter molecules are used for red and green but not for blue pixels. Iridium organometallics are promising phosphorescent emitters, but a molecule satisfying the requirements of color, brightness, and stability has not yet been developed. One strategy to discover an emitter is virtual screening, in which computational predictions are used to prioritize candidates for synthesis. Due to the computational difficulty of screening with first-principles methods such as density functional theory (DFT), empirical machine-learning methods have been used for virtual screening. Recently, machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have provided fast proxies for DFT energies. This suggests that virtual screening could be conducted with ML proxies for DFT calculations rather than empirical ML, but this has not yet been applied to OLEDs. We show on a dataset of experimental values extracted from the literature that for emission wavelength, MLIP-based predictions are not inferior to empirical ML. Using an MLIP, we screened millions of molecules for blue emission. Although blue emission is not sufficient for an emitter, our results suggest that further development of virtual screening could focus on machine learned proxies for DFT prediction pipelines rather than models trained to experimental data.
items.authors: Alexander Davis, Ihor Neporozhnii, Félix Therrien, Suhas Mahesh, Zhibo Wang, Ze-Lin Zhu

items.title: Case Studies of Homemorphic Isomerization: Interconversion of In/Out Isomers of Bicyclo[6.5.1]tetradecane and Related Bicyclic Hydrocarbons
items.abstract: Homeomorphic isomerization is equivalent to turning a molecule inside out in the same manner as a reversible article of clothing. Manifestations include the interconversion of (a) in,in and out,out isomers, or (b) in,out and out,in isomers of bicyclic molecules, but without inverting the configurations of the bridgehead atoms. In this preprint, this topological process is probed computationally for the title molecules. For the in,in/out,out manifold, the CH 2 tether is able to transit through the CH(CH 2 ) 6 CH tether with a barrier of ~26 kcal/mol, in good agreement with an experimental measurement. The geometries of the ground and transition states are analyzed in detail and the process of isomerization is visualized in animations.
items.authors: Marsel Z. Shafikov, John A. Gladysz

items.title: A field-deployable method for measuring picomolar mercury levels in natural waters
items.abstract: Measurements of mercury (Hg) at sub- to picomolar concentrations in natural waters often rely on cold vapor atomic fluorescence spectrometry (CVAFS), which provides the sensitivity required for trace detection. However, CVAFS instruments are not well suited for routine field deployment and require compressed high-purity argon or helium gas to operate, limiting their use in remote regions and locations without established analytical infrastructure. Cold-vapor atomic absorption spectrometry (CVAAS) offers a robust alternative but generally lacks the sensitivity required for low-level natural waters. Here, we optimized and tested the Nippon Instruments EMP Gold+, a purge-and-trap preconcentration system coupled to a portable CVAAS detector, to address this analytical challenge. We developed protocols for total Hg (THg) and dissolved gaseous Hg (DGM) and evaluated their performance in seawater during field deployments in Monterey Bay, California, USA and the Gulf of Guinea, Ghana. The optimized methods achieved detection limits of 0.97 pM for THg and 0.25 pM for DGM. THg measured in the Gulf of Guinea agreed closely with laboratory CVAFS measurements (R 2 = 0.953, slope = 1.11), with field matrix-spike recoveries of 90.6-96.2%. In Monterey Bay, portable DGM measurements reproduced the vertical structure observed independently for dimethylmercury using gas chromatography coupled to CVAFS. We demonstrate that this new approach can support direct measurements in regions where compressed gases and specialized analytical infrastructure are unavailable and provide rapid screening to guide subsequent sampling for more detailed Hg speciation.
items.authors: Roland P. Ovbiebo, Johannes West, Abril Hernandez, Hannah M. Adams, Ziheng Kuang, Gabriella A. Yeboah

items.title: High-Throughput Compositional Tuning of Thin-Film (La,Ca)MnO 3 Perovskites as Bifunctional Oxygen Catalysts
items.abstract: Systematic investigations of composition-dependent performance in thin-film material libraries help to understand how descriptors influence performance and enable materials optimization. The fundamental challenges of such studies are the discrete synthesis of multiple compositions within one material family and the subsequent characterization steps, which are time-consuming and limit experimental throughput. In this work, the A-site-substituted thin-film (La,Ca)MnO 3 (LCMO) material family is studied for oxygen electrocatalysis performance. Discrete synthesis is circumvented by a combinatorial pulsed laser deposition approach, enabling the synthesis of the full material family within a single deposition. High-throughput characterization methods, including X-ray diffraction, spectroscopic ellipsometry, and Raman spectroscopy, allow assessment of structural, optical, and vibrational properties. Electrocatalytic performance, including oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity and stability in terms of dissolution, is probed using a scanning flow cell coupled with inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (SFC-ICP-MS). Principal component analysis (PCA) is used to identify correlations between structural, optical, and vibrational descriptors and electrochemical performance. The analysis reveals distinct composition-property-performance relationships, demonstrating that the A-site composition of LCMO governs activity. This work establishes a workflow that combines combinatorial synthesis, physicochemical and functional characterization, and multivariate data analysis to identify performance-relevant descriptors in oxide electrocatalysts.
items.authors: Lisa Laa, Joanna M. Przybysz, Marc Nuñez‐Eroles, William Berthou, Francesco Chiabrera, Carlota Bozal-Ginesta

items.title: Data-Driven Prospective Design of Phase-Inversion Conductive Polymer Membranes
items.abstract: Conductive polymer membranes combine separation and electrical functionality, but their design remains challenging because performance emerges from coupled effects of composition, fabrication, and operating conditions. Here, we assembled 396 membrane records from 77 publications and developed target-specific machine-learning models for pure-water permeability (PWP), solute rejection, and electrical conductivity. Weighted artificial neural network ensembles for PWP and rejection and XGBoost for conductivity achieved fixed-holdout R2 values of 0.855, 0.896, and 0.914, respectively, with distinct SHAP feature-contribution patterns across the three targets. We then coupled the predictive models with residual Gaussian-process uncertainty estimation and sequential Monte Carlo expected hypervolume improvement to search a 3,024-member PANI–DBSA/PES design space and identify 12 formulations for prospective experimental evaluation. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations provided complementary mechanistic insight: increasing PANI from 0.47 to 1.89 wt% decreased the first-shell hydration number around DBSA sulfonate sites from 1.02 to 0.74, while the apparent finite-time water diffusion coefficient declined from 0.6910-10 m2∙s-1 in neat PES to 0.3710-10 m2∙s-1 at 1.89 wt% PANI. Together, these results connect literature-derived learning, uncertainty-aware formulation selection, and molecular-scale interpretation, providing a systematic framework for prospective conductive membrane design
items.authors: Jinyu Liu, Jiayue Hu, Zefang Huang, Bingxin Li, Ling Liu, Heyang Yuan

items.title: Homogeneous Electrochemical Hydrogenation of 1-Octene with [( iPr PNP)CoCl] and Water
items.abstract: Here we present the electrochemical hydrogenation (ECH) of 1-octene to n -octane using the homogeneous complex [( iPr PNP)CoCl] [CoCl] and water as the source of hydrogen atoms. We showcase how tuning only electrode surface area, as well as supporting electrolyte type and concentration can drastically increase the reaction selectivity for ECH over parasitic H 2 evolution from initially 9% to eventually 82% faradaic efficiency, without traditional chemical reaction optimization or catalyst tuning. The ECH process runs via a single electron path of hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) rather than hydride transfer according to quantum chemical calculations. Two consecutive HAT cycles must be completed to hydrogenate one substrate molecule, which renders the process more sensitive to mass transport effects and reaction design than hydride transfer mediated ECH with two electrons transferred in one step. Mechanistically, upon an initial one-electron reduction of [CoCl] , the complex undergoes HAT at one of its benzylic C–H positions to afford a dearomatized ligand structure. A key step of the active ECH cycle is then the oxidative addition of H 2 O to a Co(I) intermediate, affording a fleeting Co(III)-hydroxy-hydride, which immediately undergoes HAT to the substrate, forming a more stable Co(II)–OH species. A proton coupled electron transfer regenerates Co(I) for the next cycle. Using Bu 4 NOH in water as hydrogen atom source proved the resilience towards high pH values and suggests that the process does not rely on high proton activity in the electrolyte.
items.authors: Patrick Mollik, Ganping Wang, Romy L. Ettlinger, Laurent Maron, Dominik P. Halter

items.title: A Highly Proton-Tolerant Multicenter Borane/Phosphazene Catalytic System for Efficient PO/CO2 Copolymerization toward CO2-Based Poly(carbonate-ether) Polyols
items.abstract: Low-molecular-weight CO2-based poly(carbonate-ether) polyols from ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of propylene oxide (PO) with CO2 are highly desired as soft blocks to synthesize sustainable polyurethanes. However, such process remains great challenges because of the demanding of highly proton-tolerant catalysts. Herein, we report a binary organocatalysis system based on a nanoscopic multicenter borane Lewis acid (POSS-B8) combined with various organobases for the tunable ROCOP of PO and CO2. The confined POSS-B8 framework not only endows excellent tolerance to proton but enables cooperative activation of PO and CO2, thereby facilitating PO/CO2 ROCOP while effectively suppressing the formation of cyclic propene carbonate (cPC). Remarkably, the binary system can tolerate high loadings of chain-transfer agents (up to 400 equivalents), affording low-molecular-weight polycarbonate polyols (0.6 kDa) with narrow dispersity (Ð = 1.16). By tuning POSS-B8 loading and CO2 pressure, both the carbonate content (19-64 mol%) and glass transition temperature (-58.6 to 4.7 °C) of resulting polymers can be modulated. This metal-free and tunable platform offers a versatile strategy for the preparation of CO2-based poly(carbonate-ether) polyols with controlled structure and strong potential for industrial applications.
items.authors: Minghao Liu, Lihang Jiang, Zehao Wang, Chenyao Yuan, Zhenwei Zhou, Jinbo Zhang

items.title: Decoupling Dissolution from Water Oxidation at Single-Faceted High-Entropy Perovskite Electrodes
items.abstract: High-entropy oxides (HEOs) are promising anode materials for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to their wide compositional space and electronic flexibility. However, their electrochemical dissolution and OER remains concurrent, preventing decoupled analysis of dissolution kinetics and stability. Here, we present a combined atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) strategy to decouple lattice dissolution from water oxidation under well-defined reaction conditions. Structurally analogous, atomically flat, single-faceted (001) ABO 3 perovskite electrodes, La 1- x Sr x (Cr 0.2 Mn 0.2 Fe 0.2 Co 0.2 Ni 0.2 )O 3 with x = 0 and x = 0.3, serve as model systems to probe dissolution and OER kinetics in acid. Pipette probed localized cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry reveal that the measured current contains contributions from both OER and lattice dissolution, the latter producing nanoscale dissolution pits beneath the SECCM droplet. By correlating pit-growth kinetics with total OER charge as a function of pulse duration (τ), overpotential (η), and pH, we quantitatively separate dissolution from OER. The proportional scaling between dissolution charge and total charge indicates that OER and dissolution proceed within a common kinetic regime, sharing a common intermediate. A rate-law-based analysis yields the standard dissolution rate constant ( k d 0 , cm/s), transfer coefficient ( α ), and proton reaction order ( b ), for the dissolution of the 001 facet of both HEO-P. Our results unravel how aliovalent A -site substitution (30% Sr 2+ ) alters dissolution kinetics, charge partitioning between dissolution and OER, and thickness-dependent stability, thereby enabling quantitative disentangling of the intrinsic activity and stability of HEO electrodes.
items.authors: Subhajit Bhunia, Esteban David Gadea, Alessandro R. Mazza, Mohana V. Kante, Gangli Wang, Sheng Dai

items.title: Engineering Fe-based OER electrocatalyst stability through alloy-driven modulation of Fe-O bond covalency and hydroxyl coverage
items.abstract: Fe-based oxyhydroxides are earth-abundant alternatives to costly Ir and Ru catalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), but their stability in alkaline electrolyte limits their applicability at scale. We show that alloying FeOOH with 4+ ions (My = Se, Sn, Ti, Hf) controls dissolution through the electronegatiity of the alloyed element. In 1 M KOH at 10 mA cm-2, all four alloys exhibited slower steady-state (8–48 h) Fe dissolution rates relative to pure FeOOH; and corresponding first-order rate constants fit to transient mass loss data (enabled by XRF) decrease as My becomes less electronegative. FeTiOOH (of particular note for its affordability relative to Ru and even Ni) dissolves about eight times more slowly than FeOOH; with the steady state rate of Fe mass loss suggesting an electrode half-life of about one month. The particular stability of more electropositive alloys (FeTiOOH and FeHfOOH) is achieved following a transient of about 8 h in which labile sites are stripped away (preferentially dissolved); and this restructuring manifests as an increase in the apparent charge transfer resistance and a decrease in the electrochemically active surface area as the electrode approaches steady state. As a result, more stable FeTiOOH and FeHfOOH anodes exhibit reduced OER activity relative to FeOOH (overpotentials 556, 412 and 370 mV). Nonetheless, these findings identify electropositive alloying as a route to stabilize earth-abundant Fe anodes for the oxygen evolution reaction. In a forthcoming publication, we will employ liquid-phase XPS to demonstrate that the alloy-modulated rates of Fe dissolution are mediated through two coupled effects: the oxidation state and hydroxyl coverage of the surface, and the electron density on lattice oxygens.
items.authors: Shayan Hoseini, Foroogh Khezeli, Ashley Head, Theodore W. Walker

items.title: Two-Electron Photoreduction of Pd(II) Oxalates: In Crystallo Synthesis and Catalysis
items.abstract: Discovery and optimization of cross-coupling catalysts require catalyst activation strategies that balance the operational simplicity of air-stable precatalysts with the need for air-sensitive, lowcoordinate and -valent intermediates for substrate activation and turnover. Here we introduce a general approach for on-demand catalyst activation via two-electron photoreduction of air-stable phosphine-ligated palladium(II) oxalates. The platform exploits rapid ligand exchange at (MeCN)2Pd(ox) to enable modular assembly of catalyst photoprecursors from a single precursor. In crystallo photochemistry and single-crystal Raman spectroscopy of phosphine-supported Pd oxalates establish that photoactivation proceeds via the extrusion of two molecules of CO2 and provide the Uirst crystallographic characterization of a Pd–CO2 adduct. Two-electron photoactivation translates to the solution phase to provide a platform to access Pd oxidative addition complexes (OACs) and to generate poison-free, on-cycle catalyst intermediates. The combination of rapid and quantitative ligand exchange coupled with facile two-electron photoreduction enables application in highthroughput experimentation (HTE) workUlows and on-plate ligand screening. Photogenerated catalysts are competitive with state-of-the-art precatalysts in both C–N cross-coupling and a newly developed base-free Suzuki reaction. These results establish Pd oxalates as general, photoactivated precursors to unsaturated catalyst intermediates that unlock streamlined, combinatorial workUlows for catalyst discovery and data-driven optimization.
items.authors: Aishanee Sur, Pritam Roychowdhury, Subham Sarkar, Matthew T. Figgins, Saim Waheed, Yu-Sheng Chen

items.title: Experimental Inter-Report Scatter Bounds Machine-Learning Accuracy for TADF Singlet–Triplet Gaps—Structure and Semi-Empirical Features Reach the Same Limit
items.abstract: The singlet–triplet gap ∆ESTis the screening parameter for thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF), yet independent experimental reports of the same compound scatter by 0.072 eV RMS, and the per-molecule median regressed on is known only to 0.049 eV, about half of any model’s error. This label noise sets a ceiling on every predictor, yet the models sit below it: neither noise nor capacity alone accounts for the remaining error. Against that ceiling, two-dimensional structure predicts as accurately as a semiempirical excited-state calculation: on 231 donor–acceptor molecules (212 Bemis–Murcko scaffolds, scaffold cross-validation), random forests from Morgan fingerprints (MAE 0.091 eV) and RDKit descriptors (0.100 eV) match natural-transition-orbital descriptors from a GFN2-xTB/sTDA excited state (0.096 eV) to within 0.017 eV on paired folds, so the excited-state step buys no accuracy. Two further results are specific to this corpus. First, under a source-paper split the accuracy advantage over a mean-value baseline disappears, but the excited-state descriptors keep the rank correlation the fingerprints lose (paired ∆ρ = 0.19 on a single split, 95 % CI narrowly excluding zero): they order candidates across laboratories without predicting the gap. Second, the leakage that inflates many computed-gap models is learner-dependent—given the S1 and T1 energies as features, a linear model returns ∆EST ≡ ES1 − ET1 exactly (R2 = 1.000) while an axis-aligned forest on the same features recovers only R2 = 0.59 and clears cross-validation unremarked. Progress past the ≈ 0.1eV ceiling needs a curated, solvent-controlled, single-source experimental benchmark—one that would also expose the remaining modelling headroom. Data, models, and code are available (Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.17436069).
items.authors: Jean-Pierre TCHAPET NJAFA, Steve Cabrel Teguia Kouam, Patrick Sorrel Mvoto Kongo, Panebei Samafou, Serge Guy Nana Engo

items.title: Atomically Precise Platinum Nanocluster Catalysts for Efficient Hydrogen Production via Methylcyclohexane Dehydrogenation
items.abstract: In hydrogen storage technologies with liquid organic hydrogen carriers, the development of efficient catalysts for methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation is highly important. In this study, we developed atomically precise platinum nanocluster catalysts supported on Al2O3 (Ptx/Al2O3; x = 17, ~51). Comprehensive characterization demonstrated that the catalysts remained highly monodisperse and of uniform particle size (0.86 or 1.15 nm), and maintained a cationic electronic state (Ptδ+) even after thermal treatment. Remarkably, the Pt17/Al2O3 and Pt~51/Al2O3 catalysts exhibited a mass activity up to 7.9 and 8.2 times higher than that of conventional nanoparticle catalysts. Furthermore, by effectively suppressing undesirable cracking pathways at a low operating temperature of 250 °C, the catalyst achieved both high selectivity (byproduct yield 3%; below the detection limit) and durability. These findings pave the way for practical guidelines in advanced catalyst design.
items.authors: Yijie Wang, Chaoqi Chen, Tokuhisa Kawawaki, Kaoru Ikeda, Kotaro Sato, Kurinosuke Moriyama

items.title: Atomic Level Characterization of PolyGlycine Assembly
items.abstract: Polyglycine peptides can adopt polyproline II (PPII) helical conformations that assemble into honeycomb-shaped oligomers. These polyglycine II (PGII) helical bundles, which are also found in several natural proteins, lack apolar groups and cannot be stabilized by hydrophobic interactions. Thus, their folding must differ from that of typical globular proteins for which hydrophobic interactions promote structure formation. Despite their fundamental interest and relevance for molecular pathology, the atomic level details on how these PGII assemblies form are scarcely explored. To elucidate this process, we used CD and NMR spectroscopies to show that oligoglycine peptides with a few terminal Asp residues readily form oligomers rich in PPII helix at low pH and cool temperatures. Next, to test whether these structures can emerge without a preformed template, we performed ten independent, unbiased, multi-microsecond, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations starting from dispersed, terminally capped nonaglycine monomers in water. We observed PPII helical bundle formation through an oligomeric intermediate that is relatively poor in nematic order and H-bonds.
items.authors: Rubén López Sánchez, David Pantoja Uceda, Miguel Mompeán, Douglas V. Laurents

items.title: Parallel Production of Uniform Artificial Multicellular Models Using Vibration-Induced Local Microvortices
items.abstract: In this study, we propose a facile and efficient method for constructing artificial multicellular models via vibration-induced flow (VIF), a local fluid flow induced around vibrating microstructures. By applying circular vibration to a substrate with a cylindrical micropillar array, uniform micro-vortices were generated, into which giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs), as artificial cells, rapidly accumulated at the center. We show that by modifying two GUV populations with complementary single-stranded DNAs, we can promote specific adhesion between GUVs, leading to uniform parallel aggregates. Furthermore, the pillar-array design controls the size of GUV aggregates. Finally, we embedded nanopore-forming α-hemolysin with Spytag and SpyCatcher system in GUV populations, allowing the lumens of assembled GUVs to channel with one another and enable close-proximity molecular communication. This technology will contribute to future research on fabricating artificial multicellular models with complex functions.
items.authors: Daiki Miyashita, Yui Katsumata, Xu Han, Zhitai Huang, Mamiko Tsugane, Tomoaki Matsuura

items.title: Transition from Anisotropic to Isotropic Crystal Growth Enables Ultrahigh-Rate Zn Metal Anodes in Batteries
items.abstract: Achieving controllable crystallization under dynamic, far-from-equilibrium conditions remains a fundamental challenge underlying many technologically important processes, including highpower batteries based on metal anodes. Recent studies have identified crystal anisotropy as a key factor governing electrodeposit morphology. Departing from conventional wisdom, we find that suppressing highly anisotropic facet-dependent growth by slowing interfacial kinetics results in more isotropic, morphologically uniform electrodeposition. Taking Zn as an example, we use a nonaqueous Zn(Otf)2 in acetonitrile electrolyte to promote the formation of dense irregular-shaped nuclei in sharp contrast to the faceted nuclei formed in conventional aqueous Zn(Otf)2 and ZnSO4 electrolytes. 3-D profilometry shows the isotropic growth of Zn in the organic electrolyte leads to significantly flatter deposit morphology compared to the aqueous electrolytes. We rigorously characterize the electrochemical properties of the Zn(Otf)2 in acetonitrile electrolyte and compare it to aqueous Zn(Otf)2 and ZnSO4 electrolytes, using a combination of ultra-fast scan cyclic voltammetry on an ultra-microelectrode (UME) and interfacial molecular dynamics simulations. Our measurements show the plating/stripping kinetics in the organic electrolyte are reduced by over 100-fold relative to the aqueous electrolytes, while the transport properties are only slowed by 3 to 4-fold. Using a two-step Butler-Volmer model, we find slow interfacial kinetics in the organic electrolyte eliminate the facet-dependent rate-determining step present in aqueous electrolytes, directly linking sluggish kinetics to isotropic growth. The uniform morphology and the suppression of Zn corrosion reactions in the organic electrolyte lead to over a 10-fold improvement in cycling stability over benchmark aqueous Zn electrolytes, both at moderate current densities (1 mA/cm2) and ultra-fast current densities (200 mA/cm2). Taken together, these results highlight the viability of using a fully organic Zn electrolyte for Zn batteries and Zn electroplating systems, challenging the prevailing assumption that organic electrolytes are inferior under fast cycling conditions. Moreover, the demonstrated correlation between interfacial kinetics and electrodeposit morphology offers a generalized framework for morphological control in metal deposition.
items.authors: Stephen T. Fuller, Zidan Zhang, Venkat Ganesan, J. X. Kent Zheng

items.title: Continuous-wave laser ablation enables high-resolution ambient mass spectrometry imaging
items.abstract: Continuous-wave lasers are generally not considered for applications demanding precision ablation, because sustained heating in bulk tissue causes extensive thermal damage. Here we show that this limitation does not apply to thin sections: a 2.91 µm continuous-wave laser leaves no resolvable heat-affected zone beyond the ablation track on 10 µm thick cryosections, a confinement consistent with heat sinking vertically into the glass slide rather than diffusing laterally. This defines a distinct sampling regime in which confined material removal by a continuous-wave mid-infrared laser preserves the sample morphology for post-hoc staining and optical imaging while generating a laminar plume well suited for aspiration into the atmospheric inlet of a mass spectrometer. Here we demonstrate matrix-free ambient mass spectrometry imaging at 3 µm pixel size with a fibre-delivered beam, uniting few micron scale sampling, broad chemical coverage, and same-section co-registration on a readily adoptable platform assembled entirely from commercial components.
items.authors: William J. C. Francis, Milena Micic, Lucy Noyes, David Blair, Anna Chauvet, Lauren Ford

items.title: Active-Space Selection in Nonadiabatic Dynamics Simulations of Dense Manifolds of Excited States: When Local Diabatization Needs Great Care
items.abstract: Local diabatization (LD) propagates electronic amplitudes using time-overlaps of adiabatic states and is robust to wavefunction phase arbitrariness, root character transport, and rotations within near-degenerate manifolds. However, when truncated dynamical bases are not numerically supported by the consecutive-geometry overlaps, polar orthogonalization underlying the LD approach can enforce unitary evolution in unresolved directions leading to unphysical population transfer. This work introduces an active-space screening protocol based on singular values of time-overlap matrices. Candidate spaces proposed from persistent energy gaps and state character are accepted only when every singular direction remains above the user-defined threshold and can then be tested for physical convergence across nested active spaces. Three-state and 30-state models, controlled overlap-failure tests, and atomistic (TiO2)2 and C20 trajectories show that formal rank and increasing state count alone do not guarantee reliable LD dynamics. Smaller, well-supported spaces can outperform the nominal full space when the latter is ill-conditioned.
items.authors: Alexey V. Akimov

items.title: Integrated Process Environmental and Economic Modeling of Electrically Assisted Forward Osmosis Microbial Desalination for Water and Struvite Recovery
items.abstract: Electrically assisted forward osmosis (eFO) coupled with a microbial desalination cell (MDC) integrates water recovery, nutrient recovery, desalination, and bioelectricity utilization. This study coupled a previously validated hybrid mechanistic–data-driven model with cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic analysis (TEA) to evaluate the sustainability of eFO–MDC across operating conditions and scale-up scenarios. Operational electricity was the dominant environmental hotspot, accounting for 90.7% of the positive life-cycle GWP burden, whereas manufacturing impacts were concentrated in the MDC cathode and energy-management unit. Model-coupled LCA showed that hydraulic throughput strongly governed treatment-normalized impacts, while applied voltage produced comparatively small changes in GWP relative to its effect on nutrient recovery. TEA identified capital intensity, pumping, and treatment scale as the principal economic drivers, with combined scale-up and capital reduction lowering processing cost by 67.8%. Overall, eFO–MDC sustainability depends primarily on improving throughput and energy efficiency while reducing capital intensity during scale-up.
items.authors: Jinyu Liu, Peijie Ye, Bingxin Li, Zefang Huang, Fang Liu, Heyang Yuan

items.title: On the Mechanism of Catalytic Chain Transfer Photopolymerization (CCTP2): the Good, the Bad and the Ugly
items.abstract: Previously, the addition of catalytic quantities of cobalt(II) complexes to standard methacrylatebased formulations was found to reduce the crosslinking density, glass transition temperature, modulus and stiffness of the resultant photopolymeric materials proportional to catalyst loading. We have dubbed this technique catalytic chain transfer photopolymerization (CCTP2), which is conceptually and mechanistically linked to its predecessor catalytic chain transfer polymerization (CCTP), but uses photoinitiation, multifunctional methacrylate monomers, and creates crosslinked 2 materials. Expansion of this technology has been met with issues related to non-linear catalyst performance, limited methacrylate conversion, and long exposure times. These roadblocks prompted us to develop a working mechanistic model for CCTP2 using a combined experimental and computational approach, which is presented here. We anticipate that understanding the good, the bad, and the ugly of this catalytic process will inform future catalyst development, formulation chemistry, and broader applications of this technique towards the synthesis of functional materials and stereolithography.
items.authors: Nicholas R. Bagnall, Meredith H. Jones, Talon M. Kosak, Brian R. Donovan, Abdulaziz W. Alherz, Brady T. Worrell

items.title: Lighten Learners’ Cognitive Load or Create Conceptual Understanding: Looking Beyond Le Chatelier’s Principle.
items.abstract: Here we explore a novel approach to teaching the effect of temperature on exothermic and endothermic reactions. We contend that Le Chatelier’s Principle is best used as a predictive tool. Insights from teacher practice, personal experience and action research are shared. This narrative is a reflective professional journey supported by empirical evidence from action research (n = 17). The insights gained offer strategies to build conceptual understanding by applying Johnstone’s Triangle to reactions like the Haber process. We discuss an approach to making connections among the reaction profile, the overall equation and the Boltzmann distribution curve.
items.authors: Dharmendra Dubay

items.title: Active Noise Cancelling in Point-of-Care Testing
items.abstract: Point-of-care testing (POCT) holds great potential to improve diagnostic accessibility because of its low cost, portability, user-friendliness, and rapid turnaround times. However, the limited analytical precision and high error rates of most POCT platforms usually caused by the assay noises at the POC settings frequently create diagnostic ambiguity and lead to further confirmatory testing. Consequently, these limitations restrict broader clinical translation. To address this issue, we introduce an active assay noise canceling approach, using the deep-learning-based Whole-Process Analysis (WPA), a universal, device-adaptable software paradigm without altering assay hardware or chemistry. Instead of relying on static endpoint readouts, WPA uses a deep-learning architecture to continuously capture the spatiotemporal evolution of the entire POCT assay process. The architecture decodes dynamic, high-dimensional "assay noise footprints" and algorithmically compensate for the signal variations caused by assay noises. We demonstrated the proof of concept, we chose the lateral flow assay (LFA) as a model, which is a leading POCT platform. We validated WPA for xylazine LFA across 251 patient urine samples, benchmarking against gold-standard liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). WPA drastically decreased signal variations among different clinical samples and compressed the diagnostic gray zone, delivering 94.02% accuracy (95% CI: 90.33%-96.62%), 71.15% sensitivity (95% CI: 56.92%-82.87%), and 100% specificity (95% CI: 98.16%-100.00%), compared with human reading, which achieved 89.2% accuracy (95% CI: 84.74%-92.79%), 48.1% sensitivity (95% CI: 34.01%-62.37%), and 100% specificity (95% CI: 98.16%-100.00%). By computationally untangling true analyte signals from assay noises in POC settings, WPA provides a transformative, device-adaptable pathway to improve POCT accuracy and precision without altering assay hardware or chemistry.
items.authors: Minhao Liu, Pu Sun, Nazmul Huda Ovi, Zhicheng Peng, Zhugang Liu, Muhammad Wasim

items.title: Stepwise reduction of a porphyrin nanowire: minimal structural reorganization up to the open-shell tetraanion
items.abstract: π-Conjugated porphyrin oligomers serve as molecular wires: they exhibit high single-molecule conductance and excellent cycling kinetics as organic active electrode materials. These applications require systems in which charge/discharge cycles cause minimal changes in molecular geometry. Here, we use a butadiyne-linked porphyrin dimer as a model compound to show that its chemical reduction with alkali metals leads to subtle changes in the bond lengths in the resulting multiply charged anions, as revealed crystallographically. The small structural changes are consistent with a low inner-sphere reorganization energy, as expected for an efficient redox-active molecular wire. π-Bond Delocalization Function (π-BDF) analysis shows that successive reduction increases π-electron delocalization within the porphyrin cores, while the involvement of the butadiyne linker is strongly charge- and spin-state-dependent. The previously unknown, structurally characterized tetraanion has an open-shell singlet diradical ground state with a thermally accessible triplet state, separated by 14.2 kJ mol −1 , as established experimentally by EPR spectroscopy and supported by DFT calculations. The two open-shell states retain nearly identical covalent-delocalization topologies and differ primarily in the organization and coupling of their two unpaired electrons. Prolonged reaction with lithium metal leads to demetallation of these zinc porphyrins and cleavage of the butadiyne, forming an acetylene-appended porphyrin monomer.
items.authors: Wojciech Stawski, Yikun Zhu, Dariusz W. Szczepanik, Zheng Wei, Marina A. Petrukhina, Harry L. Anderson

items.title: Few-Shot Early-Release Adaptation Enables Generalizable Prediction of PLGA Drug Release
items.abstract: Reliable prediction of long-term drug release remains challenging for formulations developed under experimental conditions that differ from those represented in literature-derived training data. Standard formulation descriptors capture important physicochemical and formulation characteristics, but they do not fully represent study-specific factors that shape the realized release trajectory. Here, we develop a machine-learning-based few-shot adaptation strategy that combines formulation descriptors with sparse early release measurements to forecast the remaining release trajectory under previously unseen experimental settings. Using a public dataset comprising 321 formulations, 4,913 release measurements, and 113 source studies, we evaluate the framework using strict study-grouped validation. Zero-shot prediction shows limited generalization to new experimental domains, whereas incorporating only a few early observations produces a marked and reproducible improvement in predictive performance. Across repeated held-out study splits, two early measurements increase mean pooled from −0.084 to 0.333 and reduce formulation-level MAE by approximately 30%, with further improvements as additional observations are incorporated. Although absolute predictive accuracy remains moderate, the improvement is consistent across repeated splits and demonstrates that limited target-specific information can substantially reduce the generalization gap. These findings show that sparse early release measurements can serve as an effective calibration signal for machine-learning models, providing a practical strategy for improving long-term drug-release forecasting under previously unrepresented experimental conditions.
items.authors: Tengxiao Liu, Juchen Zhang, Alireza Mansouri, Hongtao Sun

items.title: Redox-mediated water electrolysis for on-demand hydrogen production and low-grade heat harvesting
items.abstract: Hydrogen is widely regarded as a key energy carrier for a sustainable, decarbonized economy; however, conventional and decoupled water electrolysis remain highly electricity-intensive because of the thermodynamic water-splitting voltage and sluggish reaction kinetics. Here, we report a thermally regenerative electrochemical cycle (TREC)-based decoupled water electrolysis strategy that incorporates low-grade waste heat to enable hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at cathodic potentials more positive than 0 V versus RHE (after IR correction). We establish a theoretical framework for integrating TREC into water splitting. By leveraging the negative temperature coefficient of the Fe(TiPA) complex, this TREC-base HER process delivers an absolute electricity savings of 7.9% compared to conventional alkaline HER. Operating alongside a highly stable ferrocyanide/ferricyanide anolyte, the flow system exhibits near-97% Faradaic efficiency and exceptional structural reversibility over prolonged cycles. Combined with the temporal flexibility to exploit off-peak electricity arbitrage, our design achieves a 33.1% reduction in overall hydrogen production costs, establishing a commercially viable and scalable paradigm for energy-efficient green hydrogen generation.
items.authors: Heng Wang, Yuxi Song, Zhiyu Wang, Yizhuo He, Zhi Wei Javier Ang, Manxuan Tian

items.title: RealBind: a leakage-controlled benchmark for experimental PXRD and Raman structure retrieval
items.abstract: We present RealBind, a benchmark for retrieving crystal structures from experimental powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) and Raman spectra. It contains 3,288 curated candidate structures, of which 1,468 have linked measured PXRD patterns, and 16,005 experimental Raman spectra, of which 10,547 are linked to structures. We provide quality-control records, prototype-held-out and composition-held-out splits, and evaluation protocols that state candidate-library size and the chemical information available at retrieval time. On a 492-candidate prototype-held-out library, a contrastive model trained on simulated PXRD reaches 78.5% Recall@10 on simulated queries but 5.3% on measured queries; physics-inspired corruption raises measured-query Recall@10 to 34.4%. A model-free correlation against simulated candidate patterns, with no preprocessing beyond the common Q-grid resampling and the measuredwindow mask, achieves 82.8% Recall@10 on the same test library. In a separate split comparison, 44% of random-split test structures have a structure-matched training counterpart; measured-query Recall@10 is 59.1% on that split versus 20.7% on the prototype-held-out split, although test populations and libraries also differ. Holding the trained model and 420 queries fixed, restricting the candidate library and pre-screening candidates by the ground-truth element set of the query’s structure, used as an oracle chemistry-conditioned diagnostic, raises Recall@10 from 27.1% to 99.1%; 37.6% of filtered queries have a single candidate. A Raman-to-structure baseline reaches 34.7% Recall@10 on heldout mineral spectra against 979 candidates in the pooled evaluation and 45.7% on the 485-candidate test-only library, which includes no validation structures. RealBind provides an experimental test bed for comparing learned methods with simple simulation-based matching under explicit, leakage-aware protocols.
items.authors: Preyansh Srivastava

items.title: Base-Dependent Lewis Acidity in Substituted Boranes: Revisiting Intrinsic Acidity through DFT and Machine Learning
items.abstract: The Lewis acidity of boranes is strongly influenced by the electronic nature of their substituents and is commonly assessed through interactions with representative Lewis bases. However, the extent to which the relative Lewis acidity ordering of substituted boranes depends on the identity of the interacting Lewis base has not been systematically investigated. In this work, Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations combined with machine learning (ML) analysis were employed to quantify substituent effects and base dependence in borane–Lewis base interactions. A dataset comprising 816 trisubstituted boranes generated from 16 representative substituents was examined in interaction with five Lewis bases (H2O, NH3, C5H5N, P(CH3)3, and Cl−), yielding 3927 computed adduct formation free energies. The results show that electron-withdrawing substituents generally enhance, whereas electron-donating substituents attenuate, the Lewis acidity of boranes. However, the magnitude of these substituent effects depends on the identity of the interacting
items.authors: Amir Mahdian, Kari Laasonen, Kaveh Farshadfar

items.title: Beyond the Ligand Applicability Domain: Generalization and Local Resolution in Structure-Aware Foundation Models for Affinity Prediction
items.abstract: Structure-aware foundation models that jointly represent proteins and ligands promise to extend affinity prediction beyond the chemical applicability domains of conventional ligand-based models, but whether they provide sufficient resolution to guide fine-grained medicinal-chemistry decisions remains unclear. We evaluatedBoltz-2across12kinasetargetsusinghistoricalbioactivityreconstruction,binding-pocket randomization, cross-target selectivity analysis, and chemical-series evaluation. Across chemically diverse compounds in temporally reconstructed evaluation sets, Boltz-2 and target-specific ligand-based machine learningshowedcomparablemeanglobalrankingacrosstargets,withsubstantialtarget-dependent differences (mean Kendall’s τ = 0.40 vs 0.31). Randomizing the binding pocket reduced mean τ from 0.33 to 0.14, while predictions were centered near −7.64 kcal/mol and retained correlated compound profiles acrossproteins.Together,theseresultssuggestastrongligand-conditionedsignal,withadditional predictive information contributed by the protein pocket. Despite this protein sensitivity, compound-level selectivitypredictionremainedweak(meanτ=0.17),andtheexperimentallystrongesttargetwas recovered for only 18.9% of compounds. Ranking also weakened within 72 temporally classified chemical series and varied substantially among series (protein-balanced mean τ = 0.18 for Boltz-2 and 0.09 for ligand-based models). These results show that structure-aware models can recover affinity information beyond relationshipscaptured by conventionalligand-based approaches whilerevealingaresolution boundary between broad prioritization and the local energetic discrimination required for selectivity and analogue ranking. At their current demonstrated resolution, such models appear best suited to broad compound or series prioritization and complementary hypothesis generation. Extending their use to fine analogueranking,selectivityoptimization,andinterpretationofsmallaffinitydifferenceswillrequire prospective evidence of reliable local resolution.
items.authors: Pieter B. Burger, Thomas M. Kaiser, Parker Dryja, Morné Muller, MacLean Levin, Sandro Belvedere

items.title: Surface-Aware Generative Design of Selective Inhibitors for Protein–Membrane Adsorption
items.abstract: Peripheral membrane proteins (PMPs) bind membrane surfaces through interfacial binding sites (IBSs) that are critical for stable membrane association and proper orientation of catalytic active sites. Dysregulated PMP–membrane interactions can enhance catalytic activity and contribute to diseases including cancer, but many PMPs remain difficult therapeutic targets because their active sites lack well-defined pockets or become accessible only upon membrane binding. In this work, we developed a multistage computational framework that integrates MaSIF-PMP, a surface-centered geometric deep learning model for IBS prediction, with a generative diffusion model to design protein binders that target PMP IBSs and inhibit membrane adsorption. Candidate binders were ranked using MaSIF-PMP prediction scores and geometric descriptors, then validated by molecular dynamics and enhanced sampling simulations. Applied to three disease-relevant PMPs, the framework identified selective binders that disrupted membrane association while minimizing off-target membrane interactions, providing a potential strategy for designing PMP membrane-adsorption inhibitors.
items.authors: ByungUk Park, Reid C. Van Lehn

items.title: Growth-Triggered Nano-vesicle Budding via Leaflet Area Asymmetry in Fatty-Acid Protocells
items.abstract: Fatty-acid vesicles growing by monomer uptake, as demonstrated experimentally for Szostak-type protocells, insert new amphiphiles predominantly into the outer leaflet. Because transbilayer flip-flop is not instantaneous, this generates a growing area mismatch between the two leaflets. We show, using the area-difference-elasticity (ADE) framework for vesicle shape, that this mismatch crosses a threshold beyond which the vesicle relieves it by shedding small, high-curvature nano-vesicles rather than by symmetric division–with no external mechanical forcing required. A leaflet-resolved kinetic model shows that sustained parent growth over many such cycles requires the shed nano-vesicles to be compositionally enriched in the destabilizing (outer-leaflet) material rather than ordinary bilayer: a specific, falsifiable prediction.
