For illustrative growth and flipflop rates the model predicts nano-vesicles of radius 60–90 nm, above the stability floor of fatty-acid vesicles. This mechanism, and its central prediction, match independent experimental observations on fatty-acid and lysolipid-containing vesicles. In an earlier work [1] we explored periodic environmental mechanical forcing (tidal, geyser and vortex-driven shear) as an alternative trigger for vesicle instability; that mechanism rests on poorly constrained assumptions about Hadean orbital dynamics and produces, in its simplest form, no resonance, only a low-pass response. The present mechanism requires no assumption about the early Earth’s mechanical environment at all.
items.authors: Peter Mikuláš

items.title: μ-Oxo-Bridged Iodine(III) Reagents Enable Catalyst- and Light-Free Fluoro(halo)methyl Radical Generation
items.abstract: While conventional radical fluoroalkylation typically requires exogenous catalysts or photoactivation to overcome significant kinetic barriers, here we report bench-stable μ-oxo-bridged iodine(III) reagents that release fluoro(halo)methyl radicals upon heating without an external catalyst, additive, or light. The resulting radicals initiate cascade cyclizations of methacrylamides and methacrylohydrazides to afford fluorinated oxindoles, pyrazolones, and related heterocycles. Variation of the fluorinated carboxylate ligand within the iodine(III) reagent framework controls the identity of the transferred C1 fragment, thereby providing chlorofluoromethyl, bromofluoromethyl, difluoromethyl, and monofluoromethyl products from a common reagent architecture. The transformation is compatible with structurally diverse and natural-product-derived substrates and proceeds efficiently upon scale-up. By encoding the required bond lability directly into the iodine(III) framework, this strategy establishes a general platform for the catalyst-, additive-, and light-free generation and incorporation of fluorinated C1 radicals into complex molecular frameworks.
items.authors: Anupam Das, Nagarajan Ramkumar, Artis Kinēns, Sergey Belyakov, Andris Antuzevičs, Janis Veliks

items.title: RGST-ΔSCF: Response-Guided Construction and Tracking of Excitation-energy-Resolved states along surface Reaction Pathways
items.abstract: Illumination can promote or inhibit catalytic reactions, yet the origin of their excitation-energy dependence remains unclear. Here, constrained ΔSCF calculations and spin- and k-resolved wavefunction-overlap tracking are used to follow nonequilibrium electronic configurations across four excitation-energy intervals along H2-dissociation pathways at doped Cu/ZnO interfaces. The preferred pathway switches from final-state-referenced configurations at low excitation energies to initial-state-referenced configurations at higher energies, with dopant-dependent crossover energies and nonmonotonic barrier responses. Metal-site dopants regulate reactivity primarily through excitation-induced reconstruction of collective metal-H bonding, whereas support-site dopants act through pathway-dependent interfacial spin redistribution. Neither excitation energy nor the magnitude of charge, bonding, or spin redistribution alone universally predicts catalytic promotion; the response depends on its direction, localization, and differential coupling to the initial and transition states. Application to Ag-mediated O2 dissociation further demonstrates that population-dependent interfacial reorganization, rather than net adsorbate charge alone, controls bond activation.
items.authors: Mengru Li, Hao Wang, Hui Yin

items.title: Data-Driven Discovery of Boronic Acid Catalysts for Amidation Reactions
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a powerful tool for catalyst optimization in organic synthesis. Yet, applications are often restricted by the need for large datasets, programming expertise, and specialized knowledge in model development. Boronic acidcatalyzed amidation reactions represent an attractive target for AI-guided optimization because of their synthetic relevance, detailed mechanistic understanding, and the need for improved catalysts for amidations. Here, an AI-guided workflow for catalyst optimization in boronic acidcatalyzed amidation reactions was established using the large-language model ChatGPT for code generation and workflow development. A dataset was generated by high-throughput screening of 459 arylboronic acids and combined with DFT-derived steric and electronic descriptors of the catalysts for model training. The model enabled the identification of the unprecedented catalyst FIBA with higher activity than the benchmark catalyst MIBA. In addition, detailed data analysis of the highly active but poorly predicted diboronic acid catalyst DBA led to the identification of a distinct activation mode involving higher-order boronate aggregates that activate and preorganize the amine nucleophile. Thus, improved catalyst performance and new mechanistic insight were obtained through an AI-guided workflow.
items.authors: Hanna Weller, Tobias Schnitzer

items.title: Enhancing double-duplex invasion by using multiple parallel-stranded peptide nucleic acids
items.abstract: Peptide nucleic acids (PNAs) enable sequence-specific recognition of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) via invasion complex formation. Here, we report a strategy using multiple parallel-stranded PNAs to enhance invasion efficiency. Cooperative binding of PNAs at adjacent target sites markedly improved invasion efficiency and enabled sequence-specific recognition of plasmid DNA under physiological conditions.
items.authors: Masanari Shibata, Kota Ito, Osami Shoji, Yuichiro Aiba

items.title: Machine Learning-Guided QSAR Modeling and Virtual Screening of Medicinal Plant-Derived Phytochemicals for the Identification of Potential hDHFR Inhibitors
items.abstract: Human dihydrofolate reductase (hDHFR) is a well-established anticancer drug target due to its essential role in folate metabolism and DNA synthesis. This study employed integrated machine based structural-activity relationship, virtual screening, and molecular docking to identify potential hDHFR inhibitors from medicinal plant-derived phytochemicals. A curated dataset of 1,368 compounds was obtained from ChEMBL and presented using Morgan fingerprints and RDKit molecular descriptors. Four regression model algorithms, including RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, and SVR were developed and optimized. Among them, SVR achieved the best score with a test R2 of 0.669 and a Spearman coefficient of 0.789. The SVR model was then used to screen the drug like phytocompounds collected from medicinal plants. The top-ranked compounds were subsequently evaluated through molecular docking against hDHFR (PDB ID: 1U72). Several phytochemicals exhibited stronger binding affinities than the reference inhibitor methotrexate. Among them Withaferin A showed the strongest docking score (-11.68 kcal/mol). These findings highlight the potential of combining machine learning and structure based virtual screening to identify promising hDHFR-targeted lead compounds for further validation.
items.authors: Shawon Sarker

items.title: Towards Zero-Waste PFAS Treatment Train: Regeneration of Ion Exchange Resins in Supercritical CO 2 Coupled with Supercritical Water Oxidation
items.abstract: Ion-exchange resins (IXRs) are often used to remove PFAS from aqueous matrices; however, spent media generate secondary waste that must be disposed of. We demonstrate a waste-treatment strategy that combines IXR regeneration in a supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO 2 ) environment followed by destruction of PFAS-containing regenerants via supercritical water oxidation (SCWO). Screening of co-solvent formulation showed that HCl-amended ethanol/water mixture effectively extracted PFOA from both macroporous and gel-type resins marketed for single use. Macroporous IXR maintained sorbent capacity over five adsorption-regeneration cycles. Further optimization identified conditions for solvent reduction: an EtOH/H 2 O/HCl regenerant yielded regeneration efficiencies of ~97.6% for the gel-type and 99.7% for the macroporous resins within 60 minutes at flow rates corresponding to 9 BV. Comparison of the regenerant’s water content provided insights into the regeneration mechanism, progressing via (i) ion exchange in an H 2 O-rich hydration layer at the IXR surface followed by (ii) PFOA transport in the scCO 2 /EtOH-rich gas-like bulk flow. Downstream SCWO treatment of the regenerant shows complete PFOA defluorination. This treatment train advances sustainable PFAS management by combining sorbent reuse, reduced demand for non-toxic organic solvents, and end-of-life treatment of concentrated PFAS residuals.
items.authors: Shuyuan Bai, Almond Lau, Anmol L. Purohit, Mrityunjai Verma, Tatiana Didenko, Mohamed Ateia

items.title: Spin-dependent thermoelectric transport properties of DPH-based molecular device
items.abstract: Examining the thermoelectric qualities that may be useful for directly turning heat into electric energy has become essential due to the rising demand for energy.The electron transport properties and the thermoelectric properties of carbon-based molecular spintronics device consisting of zigzag graphene nanoribbons (ZGNRs), carbon atomic chains and a 1,6-diphenyl-1,3,5-hexatriene (DPH) molecule was studied through utilizing the density functional theory in combination with the non-equilibrium Green's function.As evidenced by the computational outcome, the NDR effect, dual spin-filtering effect and rectifying behavior are exhibited in this carbon-based system by applying different bias voltages.The physical and chemical mechanisms are explained using spin-resolved transmission spectra, local density of states, transmission eigenstates and molecular projected self-consistent Hamiltonian eigenstate.Furthermore, considering the effect of chemical potential the Seebeck coefficients exhibit both positive and negative values, indicating the holes and electrons could be the primary carriers, respectively.Furthermore, by taking into account the impact of phonon vibrations, one can achieve high conversion efficiency between charge and spin current by adjusting the chemical potential.In addition, by tuning the temperature gradient, favorable spin thermoelectric figure of merit in elevated temperature ranges can be accomplished.These findings point to potential uses for
items.authors: Ramen Patra, Mousumi Das

items.title: Mechanism-grounded fragmentation trees enable explicit chemical reasoning for electron ionization mass spectrum prediction
items.abstract: Developing predictive models that connect molecular structures with measured spectra while preserving interpretable links to ion formation and fragmentation chemistry remains a central challenge in predictive spectroscopy. Here we present FragTreeMS, a mechanism-grounded framework that decomposes electron ionization (EI) mass spectrum prediction into fragmentation tree generation and repair followed by pathway- conditioned intensity learning. FragTreeMS organizes source-mechanism-product relations into traceable fragmentation trees and uses candidate-guided self-review to identify and recover plausible omissions before intensity prediction. The repaired fragmentation tree provides the pathway from the molecular root to each retained product ion, and these pathways are directly used for intensity prediction. FragTreeMS improves product ion recovery and complete spectrum similarity relative to direct spectrum prediction and established EI-MS baselines. The inferred ion formation processes and associated putative structural fragments are explicitly represented and visualized, advancing mass spectrum prediction toward interpretable chemical reasoning.
items.authors: Hongyan Sun, Shuofan Li, Quan Shi, Jianxun Wu, Chunming Xu, Shuangyin Li

items.title: GCI-TPs: Identifying Potentially Hazardous Transformation Products of Global Chemical Inventory Compounds
items.abstract: Environmental contamination from an ever-increasing number of chemicals is a subject of high concern, with over one hundred thousand discrete chemicals listed in a recently compiled open global chemical inventory (GCI). As these compounds enter the environment, they often form transformation products (TPs) which may have persistent, mobile and toxic (PMT) properties. Despite this, less than 1% of compounds have openly available TP information. Although TP prediction can fill some data gaps, the models are prone to combinatorial explosion, and predicted TPs must be prioritized. This study implemented multi-step environmental biotic and novel abiotic TP prediction of the ZeroPM GCI chemicals using BioTransformer 4.0, combined with toxicity and mobility models to prioritize which TPs are potentially persistent, mobile and toxic. The resulting GCI-TPs database, contains over 13 million predicted TPs, including 5481 compounds labeled as potential dead-end compounds (compounds that are not predicted to transform further), of which 478 were predicted to be either PMT or PvM compounds. From this, 38 substructures that can act as flags for potential PMT-TP formation were identified. The dead-end PMT-TPs are available on the NORMAN Suspect List Exchange and through the GCI-TPs website (https://gcitps.lcsb.uni.lu/).
items.authors: Emma H. Palm, Mikhail Vorobyov, Bashir Mayahi, Hesam Korki, Moustapha Cheikh, Siyang Tian

items.title: Exploring intermediates in mechanochemical cycle and mechanism of regulation of full-length Dynein
items.abstract: Cytoplasmic dynein is a complex hexameric AAA+ motor protein essential for intracellular transport, yet the structural mechanisms and domain cooperativity driving its mechanochemical cycle remain incompletely understood. In this study, we utilize a dual-basin structure-based model (SBM) to simulate the full-length dynein cycle in the presence of microtubules. Rather than a single concerted transition, our results reveal that dynein moves through discrete, on-pathway conformational intermediates, including a transient, ADP-bound state that bridges the pre- and post-powerstroke configurations. We identify four key regulatory interfaces (AAA1-subdomains, AAA1–AAA2, AAA3–AAA4, and AAA5–AAA6) that function as checkpoints to couple the AAA+ ring changes to power- and recovery stroke. Crucially, we elucidate the regulatory roles of the non-dominant domains: suppressing AAA3 disrupts recovery-stroke progression and linker relocation, while suppressing AAA4 selectively impairs linker stabilization and docking. Together, these findings demonstrate that dynein's force generation relies on a highly coordinated allosteric network across the entire AAA+ ring.
items.authors: Pradipta Kumar Das, Biman Jana

items.title: Understanding the Dynamics of C-OH Bond Activation over Mo 2 C under Hydrodeoxygenation Reaction Conditions
items.abstract: Hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) of biomass to value-added chemicals using transition metal carbides (TMCs) serves as a two-fold solution to overreliance on fossil-based feedstocks and excessive usage of noble metal catalysts. Specifically, Mo 2 C and W 2 C have emerged as viable alternatives to noble metal catalysts for HDO reactions. However, the underlying reaction mechanisms and structure-activity relationships for TMC catalysts are still not fully understood. Our previous mechanistic studies (Meena et al. ACS Catalysis, 2023, 13, 13446–13455), based on static DFT calculations and microkinetic modeling, indicated that C-OH bond dissociation (C 4 H 9 OH⋆ →C 4 H 9 ⋆ + OH⋆) is the rate-determining step (RDS) of HDO reaction over Mo 2 C. Nevertheless, these static calculations, which neglect thermal fluctuations, cannot fully capture the catalysts’ behavior under working conditions. To address this limitation, here, we present a comprehensive computational investigation of the RDS under more realistic reaction conditions using ab initio Molecular Dynamics simulations combined with the path metadynamics enhanced sampling technique. Path metadynamics runs reveal that the Mo 2 C surface is stable at the reaction temperature and no significant surface reconstructions take place. Further, the C-OH activation barrier obtained at 623 K using path metadynamics (38 kcal/mol) is higher than that from static DFT calculation (30 kcal/mol), likely emphasizing the significance of entropic contributions. The comparison of the barriers of C-OH activation over Mo 2 C and Zr- and Co-doped Mo 2 C surfaces revealed similar activity trends compared to that from static DFT, i.e., Zr doping improves the activity and Co doping inhibits the activity
items.authors: Raghavendra Meena, Albert Solé-Daura, Han Zuilhof, Johannes Hendrik Bitter, Bernd Ensing, Guanna Li

items.title: Cooling-induced liquid–liquid separation promotes monazite precipitation through segregation of rare earth elements
items.abstract: Monazite, (Ce,La,Nd)PO4, is a major source of rare earth elements (REEs), which play a vital role in green technology and electronics industries. Investigation into mechanisms of monazite formation from silicic melts provide valuable insights into its stability and behavior at varying temperature. This knowledge is crucial for improving the efficiency of REE extraction from mine slags, which could potentially contribute to expanding demand for critical materials. The present study leverages high-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy to characterize the behavior of monazite during slag cooling and the PARROT module available in Thermo-Calc software to predict thermodynamic conditions that control monazite crystallization within the system SiO2‒P2O5‒Ce2O3. Using an objective optimization technique that incorporates experimental data from various sources, the study provides a representation of phase equilibria. The mechanisms of monazite formation are examined, with CePO4 identified as a stable phase at specific compositions and temperature ranges. A relative enrichment in REE and P is, however, insufficient to ensure monazite crystallization. Local composition, degree of supersaturation, nucleation barriers, and cooling rate also impact on whether a chemically segregated domain crystallizes or becomes kinetically arrested as glass. Although seamless extrapolation of the three component binary systems to the SiO2‒Ce2O3‒P2O5 ternary is currently precluded by a lack of reliable experimental data or ab-initio computational constraints, this optimization work enhances understanding of phase behavior, with relevance for potential REE recovery from copper slags, a largely untapped source of critical materials.
items.authors: Hassan Gezzaz, Cristiana L. Ciobanu, Nigel J. Cook, Kathy Ehrig, Yuxiang Wu

items.title: Structural and Electrochemical Evaluations of Li4Ti5O12 Composite Anodes with an Organic Ionic Plastic Crystal Solid Electrolyte
items.abstract: Li 4 Ti 5 O 12 (LTO) is a commercialized anode active material for battery applications. Using LTO in solid-state batteries (SSBs) is expected to overcome some issues associated with anode active materials working at a low electrode potential, such as graphite and Si. Li+-containing organic ionic plastic crystals (OIPCs) reportedly have issues with these materials, including low Coulombic efficiency and achievable capacity relative to the theoretical value. This study explored the LTO−OIPC composite anode and evaluated its surface structure and electrochemical performance. It was found that the OIPC electrolyte (with carbon black) connects LTO secondary particles to facilitate ion/electron conduction. Although the capacity of the composite anode increased gradually up to ca. 15 cycles, it was close to the theoretical value (175 mAh/g) after stabilization. While applying a vacuum-drying temperature that is higher than the melting point of the Li+-containing OIPC ( 140 °C) to the composite anode adversely affected initial battery performance, it provided multiple benefits thereafter, including more efficient charge transfer and higher discharge capacity than the one vacuum-dried at 50 °C. The best-performing cell contained the 150-°C-dried one, cycled at 1C for 400 cycles. The results provide insights into further development of OIPC-containing electrodes for SSBs.
items.authors: Hiroyuki Ueda, Zak Quattrocchi, Daheng Ou

items.title: Energy ordering of singlet and triplet excited states in s-indacene, Pentalene, Cyclobutadiene derivatives in singlet fission : A model exact and density matrix renormalization group study
items.abstract: Specific molecules show an optimal energy configuration of singlet and triplet states due to the combination of anti-aromatic and aromatic components alongside bulky substituents.They exhibit longlasting triplet excitons and have appropriate structural modifications that make them particularly appealing for use in organic electronics and photovoltaics that rely on singlet fission (SF).Multiple examined molecules meet the energetic criteria necessary for singlet fission, with the differences E(S 1 ) -2E(T 1 ) and E(T 2 ) -2E(T 1 ) indicating an exothermic reaction and the presence of stable triplet excitons.We effectively utilized exact diagonalization along with the Symmetrized Density Matrix Renormalization Group (SDMRG) approach within the context of the correlated model Pariser-Parr-Pople (PPP) Hamiltonian to forecast low-lying excited states and energy levels in both singlet and triplet subspaces.These findings are then contrasted with results obtained from TDDFT, EOM-CCSD, CASPT2, and DMRG-SCF methods.The calculated values for the spin-orbit coupling constant in the triplet to singlet transition (T 1 → S 0 ) are quite low, which
items.authors: Ramen Patra, Mousumi Das

items.title: Analysis of the pH-Dependent Phase Behavior of Amorphous Solid Dispersions Using in situ Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
items.abstract: In this study, in situ stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy was employed as a novel analytical method to investigate the pH-dependent phase behavior of amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) during hydration. Ibuprofen–poly(1-vinylpyrrolidone-co-vinyl acetate) (IBU-PVPVA) ASDS were used as model systems. The ASDs underwent multiple structural changes including polymer swelling, gel-layer formation and phase separation. To monitor these processes, binary IBU-PVPVA ASDs with six drug loadings were studied under four pH conditions using in situ hyperspectral stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy with spectral focusing, further augmented with correlative confocal reflection imaging. Spectral imaging data analysis was performed with classical least squares, preceded by multivariate curve resolution-alternating least squares estimation. Supportive solid-state analysis was performed using modulated temperature differential scanning calorimetry, polarized light microscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and spontaneous Raman spectroscopy combined with principal component analysis. The results show that in situ SRS microscopy enables detailed real-time visualization of pH-dependent structural evolution in ASDs during hydration. The phase behavior was found to be affected by the environmental pH and buffering conditions, expected to ultimately determine drug release performance.
items.authors: Aino Majanen, Clare Strachan, Teemu Tomberg

items.title: Excited-State Planarization Couples Charge-Transfer Character and Spin-Orbit Coupling to Enable High Efficiency Solvatochromism in an Anti-Kasha Donor-Acceptor Phosphor
items.abstract: A single, synthetically controllable structural coordinate capable of simultaneously enhancing charge-transfer (CT) character and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) is highly sought after in purely organic chromophore design, yet has not been demonstrated. We show that excited-state planarization (ESP) in an anthracene-anthraquinone donor-acceptor emitter is exactly such a coordinate, governing one electronic variable, the CT weight of the emissive singlet, that simultaneously sets SOC into an acceptor-localized triplet channel in a near-linear, quantified relationship (R2 = 0.997), and we propose this as a general, transferable design principle for donor-acceptor chromophores. The resulting CT character exhibits a Solvatochromic response that exceeds current literature values for a neutral, purely organic, small-molecule donor-acceptor chromophore, with a slope of 25,384 cm-1 per unit Δf and R2 = 0.928 across a nine-solvent panel, which is the best yet reported. Finally, the compound exhibits genuine room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) despite an anomalously small experimental singlet-triplet gap (0.08 eV), with emission confirmed, computationally and experimentally, to originate from the second triplet state rather than the lowest, a definitive instance of anti-Kasha phosphorescence; we provide a plausible, computationally supported mechanism for this behavior, in which reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) suppression is the most plausible explanation.
items.authors: Ajeet K. Singh, Nancy Punia, Ayushi Tiwari, Swapnil Ganguly, Inamur Rahaman Laskar

items.title: Synthesis of Buprenorphine from Morphine
items.abstract: Buprenorphine is a WHO essential medicine widely used to treat pain and opioid addiction, which is currently manufactured from thebaine, a morphinan alkaloid obtained from the poppy plant. However, thebaine has a low abundance in natural poppy strains, its production is geographically concentrated, and recent years have seen global shortages. These factors present a potential vulnerability in the buprenorphine supply chain. Herein, we report the synthesis of buprenorphine from morphine, the most abundant and cheapest poppy alkaloid. To streamline the synthesis, with practical manufacture in mind, our route combines multiple transformations into several one-pot sequences. The synthesis of buprenorphine from a more available starting material may help to ensure continued supply of this critical therapeutic.
items.authors: Robert Messias, Jonathan C. Moore, Kieran D. Jones, Stephen P. Argent, Aakarsh Saxena, Hon Wai Lam

items.title: Toward a New Paradigm for Renewable Biopolymer Selection: A Structure–Processing–Architecture–Property–Scalability Framework (Alginate, Cellulose, Lignin, Chitosan, and Starch)
items.abstract: Renewable biopolymers are increasingly explored as alternatives to fossil-derived materials, yet bio-based origin alone does not determine performance or commercial relevance. This review compares alginate, lignin, cellulose, chitosan, and starch through an integrated structure–processing–architecture–property–scalability framework. Molecular functionality — carboxylate-rich, aromatic, hydroxyl-rich, amine-rich, crystalline, branched, and charged structures — is linked to processing pathways and to the resulting coatings, fibers, crosslinked networks, porous structures, carbon materials, and composite architectures. A dedicated cross-cutting discussion then argues why the three comparison axes dominant in the existing literature, chemistry, biodegradability, and application category, each fail, on their own, to predict which material and processing combination is actually useful for a given job, and what a comparison needs to include instead. The review closes with application-specific design rules to support material and processing selection for sustainable packaging, thermal insulation, water purification and separations, CO2 capture, energy storage and electrocatalysis, biomedical scaffolds and controlled release, and construction materials.
items.authors: Parastou Kharazmi

items.title: A Decision-Making Framework for Renewable Biopolymer Selection: Integrating Structure, Processing, Properties, Scalability, Techno-Economics, and Life-Cycle Assessment
items.abstract: Renewable biopolymers are often compared by feedstock origin, biodegradability, or isolated material properties. These comparisons do not, by themselves, support an engineering decision because a useful material is not a polymer in isolation: it is a biopolymer processed into a defined architecture for a specified application and manufactured under practical constraints. This study presents a semi-quantitative multi-criteria decision-making framework for selecting renewable biopolymer systems across alginate, cellulose, lignin, chitosan, and starch. The framework evaluates a material–processing route–architecture–application decision unit through five linked dimensions: molecular functionality, processing compatibility, resulting architecture, applicationrelevant performance, and scalability. Scores are accompanied by evidence-confidence flags and are tested under three application-specific weighting scenarios — balanced, performance-led, and manufacturability-led — so that the framework reports conditional candidates and genuine ranking reversals rather than a universal material ranking. Sustainable packaging coatings and films, thermal-insulation panels and porous materials, and adsorption-based water treatment using biopolymer sorbents are used as contrasting demonstration cases. For packaging, barrier performance under relevant humidity, mechanical integrity, food-contact compatibility, converting compatibility, and end-of-life are prioritised. For insulation, thermal conductivity at realistic moisture content, density, dimensional stability, drying intensity, moisture management, and manufacturability are prioritised. For water treatment, adsorption capacity and selectivity, regeneration and reuse, aqueous-state stability, and feedstock cost and availability at scale are prioritised. The method explicitly separates reported evidence from missing evidence, and the worked sensitivity analysis finds genuine ranking reversals for packaging and insulation alongside a stable, target-class-specific robust result for water treatment. Available technoeconomic and life-cycle evidence is incorporated as illustrative, application-specific data points rather than as a substitute for a dedicated assessment. The framework provides a reproducible bridge between qualitative renewable-biopolymer reviews and application-specific materialsystem design.
items.authors: Parastou Kharazmi

items.title: Diabat 2.0: A Comprehensive Diabatization Toolkit for Multichromophoric Systems
items.abstract: The construction of physically meaningful quasi-diabatic states and the evaluation of their electronic couplings are essential for describing nonadiabatic processes in molecular aggregates and other multichromophoric systems. Existing software implementations, however, are often restricted to dimers, two-state models, or particular types of quasi-diabatic states. Here, we present Diabat 2.0, a comprehensive toolkit for multistate diabatization in multichromophoric systems. It constructs the adiabatic-to-diabatic (ATD) transformation based on the adiabatic-state wave functions and energies obtained from external quantum chemistry calculations, yielding quasi-diabatic states and their electronic couplings in a nearly black-box manner. Diabat 2.0 implements several advanced ATD methods, including a general approach that can reliably construct quasi-diabatic states with diverse charge and excitation distributions without prescribing state types. This enables Diabat 2.0 to support diabatization in a broad range of scenarios that involve not only conventional charge-transfer, locally excited, and correlated triplet pair states, but also a variety of exotic states, such as mixed radical-triplet states, trion states, radical-coupled triplet-pair states, and charge-localized dicationic states. These capabilities are demonstrated in applications to several multichromophoric systems that pose substantial challenges to existing software.
items.authors: Yu-Chen Wang, Yicheng Qin, Yi Zhao, WanZhen Liang

items.title: Dual-Ligand Engineering of a Stable and High-Utilization Iron Complex Anolyte for Alkaline All-Iron Flow Batteries
items.abstract: Alkaline all-iron flow batteries offer a low-cost and inherently safe approach to large-scale energy storage, but Fe-complex anolytes remain limited by insufficient coordination stability, solubility, and utilization at high concentrations. Here, we develop a dual-ligand Fe(TEA)(PS) anolyte using triethanolamine as the primary ligand and pyridine-3-sulfonate (PS) as the secondary ligand. The secondary ligand reinforces the Fe coordination environment through pyridyl-N coordination while introducing a hydrophilic sulfonate group. Computational calculations and Fe K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal an enlarged molecular configuration and a more saturated coordination environment. Fe(TEA)(PS) exhibits a reversible Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox couple at -0.87 V versus SHE and a solubility of 1.41 M in 2 M NaOH. The resulting full cell achieves 95.12% electrolyte utilization at 1.0 M and a peak power density of 422.8 mW cm -2 . It retains 98.28% of its capacity over 1200 cycles at 100 mA cm -2 . Moreover, a cell containing 0.8 M Fe(TEA)(PS) maintains 96.87% capacity after 1800 cycles, corresponding to a decay rate of only 0.0017% per cycle. These results establish second-ligand engineering as an effective strategy for developing stable, highly soluble, and highly utilized Fe-complex anolytes for alkaline all-iron flow batteries.
items.authors: Heng Wang, Zhiyu Wang, Tianyu Yang, Hongtao Xie, Yingjia Hu, Qing Wang

items.title: Physics-Guided Soft Sensing under Sparse Laboratory Measurements and Temporal Regime Shifts in Industrial Monoammonium Phosphate Production
items.abstract: Industrial plants collect high-frequency telemetry while critical quality variables may be measured only every few hours. We study soft sensing for an industrial monoammonium phosphate process using 260,642 one-minute records and 1,325 paired laboratory observations. The grey-box model reconstructs latent acid properties from conductivity and combines them with material-balance calculations to estimate molar ratio and downstream density. Validation is entirely chronological: nine pre-gap rolling tests, a short-term regime-transfer test, a strict external post-gap test on 438 future laboratory pairs, and ten post-gap rolling comparisons. To prevent uncontrolled extrapolation, the conductivity input to the fitted latent-property mappings is limited to the range observed in the corresponding training data. Ridge and LSBoost remain more accurate than the physics-guided model, particularly in the independent long-horizon evaluation. The results show that physical structure improves interpretability but does not by itself ensure temporal robustness, motivating regime-aware monitoring, recalibration, and fallback logic for industrial virtual telemetry.
items.authors: German A. Karnup, Andrey N. Sychev, Oleg A. Telminov, Evgeny S. Gornev

items.title: Toward transparent rigid packaging from sugarcane bagasse: a consistency-testing framework for nanocellulose–chitosan sheets
items.abstract: Transparent rigid packaging is dominated by fossil-derived polymers, whereas fiber-based packaging is opaque. Dense cellulose nanofibril (CNF) and nanocrystal sheets are transparent as flat films, but whether transparency, wet stiffness and a three-dimensional shape can coexist in one sugarcane-bagasse-derived package has not been established, and one reported attempt to mold transparent CNF objects failed through drying shrinkage. This paper reports no experiments. It applies three consistency screens to a proposed bagasse CNF–chitosan–wax architecture: an optical screen derived from Debye–Bueche scattering theory, a wet-stiffness screen and a geometric forming screen, each propagated through a seeded Monte Carlo analysis over ranges traced to cited literature or explicitly stated assumptions. Under the stated optical-screen assumptions, a 100 µm wall at 10% haze and 5% voids requires a correlation length of about 10 nm or less, and because stiffness fixes a minimum wall thickness, the liquid the package must resist feeds back into the optical budget. Chitosan raises modeled wet stiffness mainly through cross-linking (median gain +1.1 GPa with it, -0.1 GPa without), but its gain in an acidic liquid is small and of uncertain sign. A tray, bowl and cup need total strain tolerances of 0.26, 0.67 and 1.10; no combination of the assumed ranges forms the cup (best case 0.96), which would need a flange wrinkling strain above 0.64. Pass shares depend on the priors, whereas the thresholds, the cup bound and the rank ordering do not. Barrier performance is untested, so every feasibility result is provisional.
items.authors: Leon Sandler

items.title: Inflammatory Hematological Indices in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: Associations with Disease Severity and 12-Month Outcomes
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is increasingly recognized as a systemic inflammatory syndrome with limited diagnostic and prognostic tools applicable in routine practice. Hematological indices derived from complete blood count, including neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), red cell distribution width (RDW), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), have emerged as potential markers of systemic inflammation and cardiovascular risk. This study aimed to compare these indices between patients with HFpEF and individuals without heart failure and to examine their associations with disease severity and 12-month clinical outcomes. Methods: In this retrospective observational study, 221 patients with confirmed HFpEF were compared with 143 control subjects without heart failure. NLR, RDW, and PLR were calculated from routine laboratory tests. Associations with echocardiographic parameters, NT-proBNP levels, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. Patients were followed for 12 months to assess major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), all-cause mortality, and heart failure-related rehospitalization. Multivariable Cox regression models were used to evaluate independent prognostic value. Results: Patients with HFpEF exhibited significantly higher NLR (3.98 ± 0.98 vs. 2.72 ± 0.81), RDW (14.62 ± 1.09% vs. 13.48 ± 0.92%), and PLR (152.4 ± 38.7 vs. 131.9 ± 29.6) compared with controls (all p 0.001). NLR and RDW correlated with NT-proBNP, E/e′ ratio, left atrial volume index, and NYHA class. Higher tertiles of NLR and RDW were associated with progressively increased rates of MACEs and all-cause mortality, with statistically significant trends across tertiles (all p-trend ≤ 0.008). In multivariable analysis, NLR (HR 1.28, p = 0.001) and RDW (HR 1.32, p 0.001) remained independently associated with 12-month MACEs, while PLR showed borderline significance. However, ROC analysis demonstrated limited discrimination, with AUC values ranging from approximately 0.55 to 0.61, indicating that none of the three indices reliably discriminated between patients with and without MACEs when considered individually. Conclusions: NLR and RDW were elevated in patients with HFpEF and were independently associated with disease severity and 12-month MACEs. However, all three indices showed limited individual discrimination and should not be considered standalone prognostic tools. Their potential clinical value, if any, requires evaluation as part of validated multivariable prediction models.
items.authors: Cristian Maghet, Diana-Aurora Arnăutu, Sergiu-Florin Arnautu, Bogdan-Flaviu Buz, Mirela-Cleopatra Tomescu, Tudor Rareș Olariu
items.title_zh: 心力衰竭伴射血分数保留的炎症血液指标研究
items.summary_zh: 背景/目的：心力衰竭伴射血分数保留（HFpEF）被越来越多地视为一种系统性炎症综合征，但在常规实践中缺乏有效的诊断和预后工具。本研究旨在比较HFpEF患者与无心力衰竭个体的血液指标，包括中性粒细胞与淋巴细胞比率（NLR）、红细胞分布宽度（RDW）和血小板与淋巴细胞比率（PLR），并探讨其与疾病严重程度及12个月临床结果的关联。方法：本回顾性观察研究比较了221例确诊HFpEF患者与143例无心力衰竭对照者的NLR、RDW和PLR。分析了这些指标与超声心动图参数、NT-proBNP水平及临床结果的关联。患者随访12个月，评估主要不良心血管事件（MACEs）、全因死亡率及心力衰竭相关再住院情况。结果：HFpEF患者的NLR（3.98 ± 0.98 vs. 2.72 ± 0.81）、RDW（14.62 ± 1.09% vs. 13.48 ± 0.92%）和PLR（152.4 ± 38.7 vs. ...）显著升高。

items.title: Substrate-Specific Responses of Tissue Paper Mill Residue and Wastewater Treatment Sludge to Effective Microorganisms: Organic Matter Transformation and Nutrient Dynamics
items.abstract: Tissue paper mill residue (TPMR) and wastewater treatment sludge (WTS) are organic wastes with potential for sustainable resource recovery, but their contrasting properties may affect their responses to Effective Microorganisms (EM) application. This study evaluated the effects of an EM preparation containing Bacillus subtilis, Bacillus amyloliquefaciens, and Saccharomyces cerevisiae on organic matter transformation, nutrient dynamics, and seed germination in TPMR and WTS during a 36-day microcosm incubation. Treatments included an untreated control and single- and repeated-application EM treatments. In TPMR, lower measured organic matter contents were observed in EM-treated samples than in the control on Day 29, with reductions of 31.50–45.49%. Cellulose contents were also 17.08–22.53% lower on Day 36. Total potassium concentrations were 108.92–265.32% higher from Day 22 onward. In WTS, few differences were observed in organic matter, total nitrogen, or total phosphorus. However, total potassium concentrations in the single-application treatment were 105.11–459.24% higher than those in the control. On Day 36, the germination index exceeded 70% in all treatments except the repeated-application TPMR (64.99%). All WTS treatments showed germination index values above 90%. These results demonstrate that TPMR and WTS exhibited substrate-specific responses to EM application, highlighting the importance of considering waste characteristics when optimizing EM-based strategies for resource recovery.
items.authors: Peiran Xu, Xueyan Zhu, Bishun Zhu, Wei Liu, Yafang Tang, Hongxia Huang
items.title_zh: 组织纸厂残渣与污水处理污泥对有效微生物的特异反应
items.summary_zh: 组织纸厂残渣（TPMR）和污水处理污泥（WTS）是具有可持续资源回收潜力的有机废物，但其不同特性可能影响其对有效微生物（EM）应用的反应。本研究评估了含有枯草芽孢杆菌、淀粉芽孢杆菌和酿酒酵母的EM制剂对TPMR和WTS在36天微生态培养期间的有机物转化、营养动态和种子发芽的影响。处理包括未处理对照和单次及重复应用的EM处理。在TPMR中，第29天EM处理样品的有机物含量比对照低31.50–45.49%，纤维素含量在第36天也降低了17.08–22.53%。从第22天起，总钾浓度提高了108.92–265.32%。在WTS中，有机物、总氮或总磷差异较小，但单次应用处理的总钾浓度比对照高105.11–459.24%。第36天，除重复应用TPMR（64.99%）外，所有处理的发芽指数均超过70%。所有WTS处理的发芽指数均超过90%。结果表明，TPMR和WTS对EM应用表现出特异性反应。

items.title: Quantifying Environmental Impacts Across Multiple Future Lifecycles of Steel and AAC Structures: Results, Uncertainties, and Methodological Challenges
items.abstract: Although circular strategies in construction can substantially reduce environmental impacts (EI), their effectiveness depends on aligning technological capacities with socio-economic conditions, requiring a future-oriented assessment. This study quantifies the EI of steel-frame and autoclaved aerated concrete (AAC) structures under various circular end-of-life scenarios, including multiple future lifecycles in Poland. A prospective consequential life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted, integrating Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) for sensitivity analysis. The inventory was based on literature, spatial analysis, and expert input. Two methodological challenges were identified: lack of material quality differentiation in LCA databases, limiting reuse modelling, and difficulties in defining robust functional units across multifunctional technologies. Results indicate substantial mitigation potential from AAC recycling, particularly in single-family housing. EI of concrete recycling depends on distances and substitution of energy-intensive materials. High-quality recovery is critical for steel ( 70% recycling or reuse). SSP modelling revealed the ‘crediting paradox’, highlighting the need for clear methodological boundaries.
items.authors: Aleksandra Kręt-Grześkowiak, Sławomir Rowiński

items.title: SemLRA: Lightweight Robust Aggregation Against Poisoning Attacks in Semantic Federated Learning
items.abstract: Semantic federated learning couples task-oriented semantic communication with distributed training, reducing on-device training burden and end-to-end inference latency. However, poisoning through local data, task labels, or transmitted semantic features can degrade task performance and system reliability. We propose semantic lightweight robust aggregation (SemLRA) for an information-separated dual-server architecture. SemLRA calibrates task losses already generated during split training using the within-round median and median absolute deviation to construct bounded client reliability coefficients. These coefficients jointly reweight client- and server-side model aggregation and regulate subsequent server-side optimization. SemLRA estimates reliability without reference data, client-update inspection, or prior knowledge of the malicious-client count or fraction, while retaining FedAvg-order aggregation complexity. On CIFAR-10, SemLRA maintains accuracy close to its clean-training level under continuous attacks, exceeding the strongest competing defense in mean final-stage accuracy by 3.77 percentage points under label flipping. Under burst attacks, SemLRA provides the strongest accuracy retention across all evaluated scenarios. Measured training runtime shows negligible additional overhead.
items.authors: Zepei Liu, Zhigang Jin, Zimeng Li, Houyang Luo

items.title: Multi-Objective Distributed Operating Room Scheduling in Collaborative Hospital Networks: Balancing Operating Costs, Patient Deterioration, and Patient Utility
items.abstract: Collaborative hospital networks are hospital groups that collaborate to provide healthcare services and share medical resources. They are an important part of the accessibility and efficiency of healthcare delivery. Nevertheless, existing research pays limited attention to multi-hospital scenarios. Furthermore, most studies adopt optimization objectives from the perspective of healthcare providers rather than prioritizing patient-centered service quality. Accordingly, this paper investigates the multi-objective distributed operating room scheduling problem (MDORSP), with the objectives of simultaneously minimizing operating costs and patient deterioration and maximizing patient utility. A multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming model is formulated for the MDORSP. Within this model, to embed patient-centered healthcare considerations, heterogeneous patient preferences for surgeons of varying professional qualifications are quantified based on random utility theory. To tackle this NP-hard MDORSP, a problem-tailored multi-objective evolutionary algorithm is developed. It incorporates priority-based chromosome representation, a heuristic initialization strategy, custom decoding and repair mechanisms, and a refined selection strategy. Extensive computational experiments show that the proposed algorithm obtains higher HV values than TLMOVNS on all benchmark instances and surpasses CPLEX in 86.7% of instances, with its average computational runtime being 78.6% and 85.9% less than TLMOVNS and CPLEX, respectively. The findings underscore the effectiveness of collaborative resource coordination in reconciling operational efficiency and patient-centered service quality.
items.authors: Hongbo Li, Yuechen Wang, Zhichao Lv, Zehui Wei, Xianchao Zhang
items.title_zh: 协作医院网络中的多目标手术室调度研究
items.summary_zh: 协作医院网络是指多个医院共同提供医疗服务并共享医疗资源的组织。本文研究了多目标分布式手术室调度问题（MDORSP），旨在同时最小化手术成本和患者恶化风险，并最大化患者效用。为此，构建了一个多目标混合整数线性规划模型，量化了患者对不同专业资格外科医生的偏好。针对这一NP难问题，提出了一种定制的多目标进化算法，采用基于优先级的染色体表示、启发式初始化策略、自定义解码和修复机制，以及精细的选择策略。大量计算实验表明，所提算法在所有基准实例上获得的HV值均高于TLMOVNS。

items.title: Image-Based Quantitative Pore Analysis of Cementitious Materials: A Scale-Resolved Review of X-Ray CT Methods and Metrics
items.abstract: X-ray computed tomography (CT) has become the reference non-destructive technique for the three-dimensional characterization of the pore structures of cementitious materials. This review maps 140 application studies—spanning cement paste, mortar and concrete, from air-entrained, cellular and recycled-aggregate systems to alkali-activated binders, ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) and 3D-printed materials—and the underlying image-analysis methodology is inventoried separately and excluded from all frequency statistics. Each study is classified by voxel-size class (sub-micron, 1 µm; micro, 1–20 µm; meso, 20–100 µm; macro, 100 µm; multiscale), with voxel size being a sampling parameter rather than a spatial resolution, and by the pore metrics it reports under six metric families. The synthesis reveals similar concentrations at the micro (48/140) and meso (50/140) scales, a dominance of porosity and pore-size distribution at every scale, and pronounced under-use of higher-order shape and spatial statistics: flatness, elongation and pair-correlation functions each appear in less than 2% of studies. Systematic discrepancies between scales are analyzed: resolution-conditioned porosity, the representative elementary volume–resolution dilemma, segmentation-induced variance comparable to material effects, and the persistent CT–mercury intrusion porosity mismatch. Priorities are standardized segmentation benchmarks, scale-bridging registration protocols, routine uncertainty reporting and broader adoption of quantitative shape and spatial descriptors. Provisional assignments are flagged in the dataset.
items.authors: Minje Kim, Minjae Han, Sung-Chul Bae, Heongwon Suh

items.title: Robust PD-Type Iterative Learning Fault-Tolerant Control for Discrete Systems with Polytopic Uncertainties and Actuator Faults
items.abstract: For a class of discrete systems with polytopic uncertainties and actuator faults, a robust PD-type iterative learning fault-tolerant control scheme is investigated in this article. By providing a two-dimensional analysis of the learning process, the fault system of a repetitive nature is equivalently converted into an uncertain linear repetitive process. Additionally, employing repetitive process stability theory, new sufficient conditions with less conservatism for the robust stability of the designed fault-tolerant controller are derived in terms of linear matrix inequality constraints. The controller gain matrices are exactly given as well. Finally, simulation results of an industrial SCARA robot demonstrate the efficiency and feasibility of the proposed strategy in comparison to the developed robust P-type iterative learning fault-tolerant control strategy.
items.authors: Wei Zou, Lei Wang, Weiwei Shao

items.title: The Narcissism, Entitlement, and Self-Esteem Conduit to Quiet Quitting
items.abstract: Quiet quitting has become a focus of employee engagement research, yet its psychological antecedents remain understudied. Trait grandiose narcissism (i.e., an inflated sense of self-importance) may be one such antecedent, driving entitlement (i.e., the belief in deserving preferential treatment despite disproportionate effort). This study tested entitlement as the mechanism linking narcissism to quiet quitting. A convenience sample of U.S. employees completed surveys through CloudResearch. Moderated mediation analysis utilizing SPSS PROCESS tested entitlement as the mediator and self-esteem as a moderator of the narcissism–entitlement indirect pathway. Self-esteem was examined as a boundary condition, given that heightened self-regard may intensify narcissistic individuals’ sense of entitlement. Narcissism associated with greater entitlement, which associated with greater quiet quitting. High levels of narcissism and self-esteem associated with greater entitlement, and thereby greater quiet quitting. Rather than serving as a protective factor, higher self-esteem was associated with a stronger relationship between narcissism and entitlement, thereby strengthening the indirect association with quiet quitting. Organizations may reduce quiet quitting among narcissistic employees by addressing ego-related needs and managing entitlement perceptions. These findings offer a practical extension of equity sensitivity theory, translating its principles into actionable strategies for managing modern workplace disengagement.
items.authors: Stephen Bok, James Shum, Maria Lee

items.title: Adipose Tissue Adaptations to Chronic Kumquat Consumption in High-Fat Diet-Induced Obese Mice
items.abstract: White adipose tissue dysfunction is a central event in the development of obesity-associated metabolic disorders. Kumquat (Fortunella japonica) is consumed whole, allowing intake of peel-derived bioactive compounds. Although increasing evidence suggests that kumquat exerts beneficial metabolic effects, its impact on white adipose tissue homeostasis remains poorly understood. We investigated whether chronic supplementation with lyophilized whole kumquat could attenuate adipose tissue dysfunction in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice. Male C57BL/6J mice received a standard diet, HFD, or HFD supplemented with 5% (w/w) kumquat (HFD + K) for 24 weeks. Kumquat attenuated body weight gain, reduced food intake and caloric efficiency, and decreased epididymal white adipose tissue mass. Histological analysis showed reduced adipocyte hypertrophy and a shift toward smaller adipocytes. Kumquat also decreased macrophage crown-like structures and Tnf and Il1b expression, while increasing circulating adiponectin, lowering leptin, and improving the leptin/adiponectin ratio. At the molecular level, kumquat increased Pparg, Ppargc1a, Sirt1, Cox4i1, and Ucp1 expression, together with mitochondrial DNA copy number, consistent with changes in molecular markers associated with mitochondrial remodelling and thermogenic pathways. Overall, these findings identify white adipose tissue as a relevant target of chronic whole-kumquat consumption during diet-induced obesity and suggest that preservation of adipose tissue homeostasis involves coordinated anti-inflammatory, endocrine, and mitochondrial-related molecular adaptations.
items.authors: Simona Terzo, Pasquale Calvi, Marta Giardina, Salvatore Timeo, Assunta Lombardi, Antonella Amato

items.title: Solar-Driven CO2 Methanation at Industrial Interfaces: Technology Readiness, Process Integration, and Techno-Economics
items.abstract: Solar-driven CO2 methanation is being investigated as a pathway for carbon utilization and renewable-energy storage, yet deployment at industrial point sources, including ammonia–urea complexes, remains constrained by heterogeneous reporting, uncertain feedstock availability, heat-management requirements, and boundary-dependent process economics. This structured critical narrative review evaluates thermocatalytic Power-to-Methane, H2-fed photothermal and light-assisted methanation, and direct photocatalytic CO2-to-CH4 conversion across catalyst, reactor, and plant scales. A domain-specific evidence-grading framework is applied to distinguish comparatively well-supported mechanistic conclusions from studies with incomplete local thermometry, matched-temperature dark controls, photon-flux calibration, isotope tracing, or material and charge balances. The review further examines the stoichiometric and operational constraints governing residual process-CO2 availability at ammonia–urea sites and assesses how renewable-H2 supply, buffer storage, gas conditioning, heat recovery, and product specifications affect process integration. An illustrative industrial screening case for a 2000 t d−1 NH3/2000 t d−1 urea complex yields a nominal residual of 472.4 t d−1 CO2 before operational deductions, corresponding to 86.5 t d−1 H2 demand and an approximately 198 MW electrolyzer load at 55 kWh kg−1 H2. Published techno-economic and life-cycle results are interpreted within their reported functional units and system boundaries rather than directly rank-ordered. The evidence base is strongest for conventional thermocatalytic methanation at pilot and industrial scale, whereas photothermal and direct photocatalytic routes retain substantial diagnostic, transport, durability, and scale-up uncertainties. Commercial feasibility depends not only on nominal CO2 availability but also on the economically and environmentally justified conversion fraction, renewable-electricity cost, electrolyzer utilization, reactor durability, methane losses, product-conditioning requirements, and heat and co-product credits. Accordingly, complete methanation of a nominal residual CO2 stream should not be adopted as a design objective without site-specific marginal techno-economic and life-cycle evaluation. A five-gate framework is proposed to guide progression from mechanistic credibility and reproducible performance to module qualification and site-specific deployment.
items.authors: Rafah Mohammed Thyab, Elsayed G. Blall, Monica Toderas, Ahmed H. Abdel-Salam, Ashraf Morsy

items.title: Extremal Hysteretic Energy Dissipation in a Dry-Friction Vibration Isolator with a Longitudinally Slit Cylindrical Shell and Deformable Filler
items.abstract: Vibration isolators based on a slit cylindrical shell with an elastic filler are proposed for the needs of the mining, oil and gas, and construction industries; in these devices, energy dissipation is provided by the effects of distributed positional dry friction between the contacting elements. Such vibration isolators are intended to operate under considerable loads and severe dimensional constraints, which requires a combination of high load-bearing capacity, sufficient compliance, and efficient energy dissipation. The aim of this work is an analytical study of hysteretic energy dissipation in the nonconservative contact system “slit cylindrical shell–deformable filler” with dry friction at the contact interface, and the determination of the conditions of maximum energy dissipation. A quasi-static model is developed in which the bending compliance of the slit shell is reproduced by an energetically equivalent orthotropic shell, while the filler is assumed to be elastic and incompressible. An analytical description of the hysteresis loop and an explicit expression for the energy dissipated per cycle are obtained. A nonmonotonic influence of the friction coefficient on energy dissipation is established: as friction increases, the dissipation first grows, reaches a maximum, and then decreases. The extremum is caused by the competition between the growth of the work of the friction forces and the reduction of the region of relative slip. An optimal level of compliance of the contact system is also established. As the depth of the loading cycle decreases, this optimum shifts toward larger values, while the maximum attainable dissipation is reduced. Joint variation of friction and compliance does not produce an isolated interior maximum, but forms an extended region of enhanced energy dissipation. Within a prescribed domain of admissible parameters, the global maximum is attained on its outer boundary. The relationships obtained provide a physically justified analytical basis for the rational design of shell-type vibration isolators, for the construction of numerical models, and for the planning of experimental tests.
items.authors: Andrii Velychkovych, Ivan Shatskyi

items.title: Patient-Reported Adherence, Knowledge and Perceived Outcomes After Specialist Nursing Education in a Multidisciplinary Headache Unit: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Migraine is a leading cause of disability worldwide. Despite advances such as calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)-targeted therapies, suboptimal treatment adherence, limited health literacy, and weak self-management remain common, and patient-reported data on the contribution of specialist headache nurses within European tertiary units are scarce. This study describes patient-reported adherence to acute treatment and to lifestyle recommendations, self-perceived knowledge, and perceived quality of life in adults with migraine who had attended a structured, nurse-led educational consultation in a tertiary multidisciplinary headache unit. Methods: This cross-sectional descriptive study included 90 adults (≥18 years) with migraine diagnosed according to the International Classification of Headache Disorders, third edition (ICHD-3), who were starting treatment with an anti-CGRP monoclonal antibody and consecutively attended a specialist nursing consultation; patients with documented cognitive impairment or without written informed consent were excluded. Between January and December 2021, participants completed, on a single occasion after the consultation, an electronic, structured, piloted ad hoc survey covering knowledge (with pre-consultation knowledge rated retrospectively), adherence to pharmacological and lifestyle recommendations, perceived changes in attack frequency and intensity, and self-reported quality of life. Data were analysed descriptively, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for proportions and without formal hypothesis testing. Results: Participants were mostly women (67.8%), with a mean age of 43.1 ± 10.7 years. Overall, 74.4% (95% CI 64.6–82.3) reported always following acute-treatment instructions and 66.7% (56.4–75.5) always following lifestyle recommendations; 68.9% (58.7–77.5) felt the education had improved their understanding of migraine and their quality of life, and 67.8% (57.6–76.5) perceived fewer attacks. Self-rated adequate knowledge was higher at the time of the survey than retrospectively recalled for the pre-consultation period in all five domains. The main barriers were limited prior knowledge and difficulty maintaining a headache diary. Conclusions: Most patients who had received structured nurse-led education reported good adherence and perceived benefits in their understanding of migraine and quality of life. Given the cross-sectional design, the retrospective assessment of prior knowledge, the use of a non-validated questionnaire, and the absence of a control group, these findings cannot be attributed to the consultation itself, and perceived changes in attack frequency cannot be separated from the effect of the newly started anti-CGRP treatment; prospective, controlled studies using validated outcome measures are needed. This study was not registered.
items.authors: María José Ruiz-Castrillo, Leonardo Portocarrero-Sánchez, Lucía Zaballa-Pérez, Alejandro Sánchez-Huertas, Javier Díaz-de-Terán
items.title_zh: 多学科头痛单位专科护理教育后患者报告的依从性与知识
items.summary_zh: 背景/目的：偏头痛是全球主要的残疾原因。尽管有针对降钙素基因相关肽（CGRP）的治疗进展，但治疗依从性不足、健康素养有限和自我管理能力较弱仍然普遍，关于欧洲三级单位专科头痛护士贡献的患者报告数据稀缺。本研究描述了参加三级多学科头痛单位结构化护理教育咨询的成人偏头痛患者在急性治疗和生活方式建议的依从性、自我感知知识和生活质量的情况。方法：本横断面描述性研究纳入90名符合国际头痛分类第三版（ICHD-3）诊断的成人偏头痛患者，他们开始接受抗CGRP单克隆抗体治疗并连续参加专科护理咨询；有认知障碍记录或未提供书面知情同意的患者被排除。在2021年1月至12月期间，参与者在咨询后单次完成了一份电子结构化调查，涵盖知识（回顾性评估咨询前知识）、药物和生活方式建议的依从性及感知变化。

items.title: Durability Testing of Prefabricated Pervious Concrete Pavers
items.abstract: Pervious concrete pavements have received increasing research attention because of their potential to improve stormwater runoff management in urban environments. Since they are usually exposed to low temperatures during the winter period, it is important to test their durability in a cold climate. Existing protocols for testing of the frost resistance of ordinary concrete are not completely suitable for this type of material, particularly for prefabricated pervious concrete pavers. The frost resistance of pervious concrete pavers designed with partial replacement of cement with fly ash (10 and 20%) was tested with and without the presence of de-icing salts. Two exposure conditions were used: specimens were either sealed in plastic foil to prevent drainage during cycling or were allowed to drain. Each freeze–thaw cycle lasted 24 h. After every seven cycles, specimen mass and ultrasonic pulse velocity were measured; the specimens were then rewetted and testing continued. At the end of the test, the specimens were dried and their flexural and compressive strengths were determined. The results indicate that ultrasonic pulse velocity is sensitive to changes in the properties of pervious concrete. The proposed method therefore shows promise for further development and application.
items.authors: Marina Škondrić, Vera Obradović, Ognjen Govedarica, Branislava Lekić, Vladana Rajaković-Ognjanović, Aleksandar Savić

items.title: Molecular Profiles, Treatment-Associated Survival, and Prognosis in Early-Onset Versus Late-Onset Gastric Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Background: Whether early-onset gastric cancer (EOGC) represents a distinct clinical entity requiring age-specific management remains uncertain. We synthesized molecular profiles, treatment-associated survival, and prognosis to determine what current evidence supports in practice and requires prospective validation. Methods: This PROSPERO-registered, PRISMA-compliant review searched four databases (PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase, and the Cochrane Library) from 1990 to 2025. Random-effects models compared EOGC with late-onset gastric cancer (LOGC) using each study’s reported age definition, provided that the upper age cutoff for EOGC did not exceed 50 years, and evaluated treatment–survival associations within EOGC. Robustness was evaluated by restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimation with Knapp–Hartung adjustment, subgroup analyses, meta-regression, and prediction intervals; certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). Results: Fifty-eight studies involving 194,671 patients were included. EOGC showed lower observed odds of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) positivity (odds ratio [OR], 0.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.53–0.84) and microsatellite instability (MSI)/deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) positivity (OR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.12–0.91); p53 protein overexpression was less frequent, whereas the lower tumor protein p53 (TP53) mutation frequency represented only a non-significant numerical trend. E-cadherin loss was more frequent only under uniform immunohistochemical criteria (OR, 1.82; 95% CI, 1.16–2.85). These largely unadjusted molecular estimates indicate prevalence patterns rather than independent age effects. Radical resection was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.37; 95% CI, 0.22–0.61), but confounding by indication and a prediction interval crossing unity precluded causal inference. The chemotherapy association was not retained under REML–Knapp–Hartung analysis. Evidence was insufficient to establish differences in overall, disease-free, or cancer-specific survival. Certainty was low to very low. Conclusions: Age alone does not justify altered biomarker testing, systemic treatment, or surveillance. This review distinguishes actionable practice from unsupported extrapolation: established biomarker testing should be applied irrespective of age, and young age should not deter assessment for curative-intent resection. It also defines the evidence standards required before any EOGC-specific stratification can be adopted.
items.authors: Jianbin Wen, Linyong Zhao
items.title_zh: 早发与晚发胃癌的分子特征及预后分析
items.summary_zh: 背景：早发胃癌（EOGC）是否为需要特定年龄管理的独特临床实体尚不明确。本研究综合了分子特征、治疗相关生存率和预后，以确定当前证据的支持情况及未来验证需求。方法：本系统评价遵循PROSPERO注册和PRISMA标准，检索了1990年至2025年间的四个数据库（PubMed、Web of Science Core Collection、Embase和Cochrane Library）。采用随机效应模型比较EOGC与晚发胃癌（LOGC），并评估EOGC内的治疗-生存关联。结果：纳入58项研究，共194,671名患者。EOGC患者的HER2阳性率（比值比[OR]为0.66，95%置信区间[CI]为0.53–0.84）和微卫星不稳定性（MSI）/缺陷错配修复（dMMR）阳性率（OR为0.33，95% CI为0.12–0.91）均较低；p53蛋白过表达的发生率也较低。

items.title: A Study on the Enhanced Longitudinal Resolution in Radio-Electromagnetic Wave Transillumination Detection
items.abstract: Based on the governing equations of the electromagnetic radiation field and the theory of multi-layer media propagation, the governing equations for electromagnetic wave attenuation are derived. A stable solution to the resulting large-scale sparse linear system is obtained using Tikhonov regularization. A typical collapse column forward model is established using locally refined triangular mesh discretization. Forward and inverse modeling are conducted at three transmission frequencies: 0.3 MHz, 0.5 MHz, and 1.5 MHz. The results indicate that the 1.5 MHz frequency yields the best vertical resolution, with inversion results most closely matching the modeled anomaly location. In the field application at working face number 3308 using 1.5 MHz, the local polynomial interpolation inversion delineates an anomalous vertical extent of approximately 70 m (75–145 m), whereas the Kriging interpolation method yields a vertical extent of about 140 m (20–160 m), representing a reduction of approximately 50% in the vertical extent of the delineated anomaly. Post-mining exposure reveals the X16 collapse column, with a major axis of 53 m and a minor axis of 34 m, which is generally consistent with the detection results. This study confirms that local polynomial interpolation combined with locally refined triangular meshing effectively enhances the vertical resolution of radio wave transillumination, providing reliable technical support for the accurate delineation of concealed collapse columns.
items.authors: Yueming Kang, Shaobei Cui, Zhongguang Sun, Baixiang Liu, Kang Guo

items.title: CMV Detection and Pneumocystis Infection in the PERCH Cohort
items.abstract: The Pneumonia Etiology Research for Child Health (PERCH) study identified pneumonia due to the fungus Pneumocystis jirovecii as the most common fungal cause of pneumonia in infants. Whether Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) is complicated by other pathogens remains unclear. To address this, we performed targeted next-generation sequencing on archived PERCH samples and found that human cytomegalovirus (CMV) was the most common virus detected, particularly in Africa. Here, CMV status was defined as detection of CMV nucleic acid in the nasopharyngeal specimen by targeted sequencing, not CMV seropositivity. Despite CMV detection being common, analyses of clinical metadata did not show any impact on clinical parameters such as oxygen requirement or hospital stay. Because sequence detection reflects the presence of CMV at the upper respiratory tract, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of a causal role in pneumonia. However, future studies should consider assessing CMV co-infection to determine if CMV affects post-pneumonia sequelae in children.
items.authors: Dora Pungan, Ava Wasserstein, Mst Shamima Khatun, Haiyan Miller, Jerry S. Zifodya, Jay K. Kolls
items.title_zh: PERCH队列中CMV检测与肺囊虫感染研究
items.summary_zh: 肺炎病因研究儿童健康（PERCH）研究发现，肺囊虫肺炎（PJP）是婴儿最常见的真菌性肺炎。尚不清楚PJP是否会受到其他病原体的影响。为此，我们对存档的PERCH样本进行了靶向下一代测序，发现人类巨细胞病毒（CMV）是检测到的最常见病毒，尤其在非洲地区。CMV状态通过靶向测序在鼻咽标本中检测到CMV核酸来定义，而非CMV血清阳性。尽管CMV检测普遍存在，临床元数据分析未显示对氧气需求或住院时间等临床参数的影响。由于序列检测反映了CMV在上呼吸道的存在，这些发现不应被解读为肺炎因果关系的证据。然而，未来的研究应考虑评估CMV共感染，以确定CMV是否影响儿童肺炎后的后遗症。

items.title: Sustaining Safe Harbors: The Mediating Roles of SARC and Safety Culture in the Relationship Between OHSMS and Safety Performance in the Port Industry: A Case of Korea
items.abstract: The sustainability of global maritime supply chains ultimately depends on the safety of frontline port workers, yet high-risk, multi-stakeholder port operations continue to face persistent occupational hazards that threaten this goal. Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems (OHSMS) serve as a core governance tool for sustainable safety management, but their effectiveness depends not on formal existence alone, but on workers’ cognitive recognition and cultural internalization, particularly under South Korea’s Serious Accidents Punishment Act. This study examined how OHSMS perception is related to safety performance (SP) among port workers, testing the parallel and serial mediating roles of Serious Accident Response Capability (SARC) and Safety Culture (SC) as pathways toward socially sustainable safety outcomes. Cross-sectional survey data from 432 South Korean port workers were analyzed using structural equation modeling. OHSMS perception was positively associated with both SARC and SC, and SC showed the strongest direct association with SP. In the main model, the direct paths from OHSMS and SARC to SP were non-significant, consistent with indirect-only mediation through SC, and the serial pathway (OHSMS → SARC → SC → SP) was significant; however, the SARC → SP path became significant in a common method sensitivity analysis. These cross-sectional results represent associations rather than causal effects. The findings suggest that safety performance in the port sector is associated less with formal regulatory compliance alone than with the internalization of safety practices in a shared safety culture, which is relevant to United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being).
items.authors: Dong-Il Yang

items.title: Effects of Discharge Ratio and Temperature Difference on Three-Dimensional Flow and Thermal Mixing at a 90° Confluence
items.abstract: River confluences are highly heterogeneous hydraulic environments where flows with different discharges and temperatures merge, generating complex three-dimensional flow structures and thermal mixing that directly influence downstream mass transport, water quality, and aquatic ecosystems. In this study, a three-dimensional numerical model was used to investigate flow structures and thermal mixing at a 90° open-channel confluence. The study was designed to systematically examine how changes in discharge ratio modify three-dimensional flow and thermal mixing under the same channel geometry and total discharge, and how these responses differ between isothermal and non-isothermal conditions. Four main-to-tributary discharge ratios were combined with two thermal conditions. In the isothermal condition, the main channel and tributary had equal inflow temperatures. In the non-isothermal condition, the main channel inflow was 10 °C warmer than the tributary inflow. Eight cases were analyzed quantitatively in terms of the spatial trajectories of the maximum-velocity and thermal cores, momentum ratio, densimetric Froude number, mixing index, and gradient Richardson number. The results showed that the initial position of the maximum-velocity core was governed primarily by the relative momentum of the two incoming flows, whereas density and buoyancy effects induced by the temperature difference developed progressively downstream, indicating distinct spatial ranges over which momentum and buoyancy influenced the flow. When tributary momentum was substantially dominant, rapid initial mixing occurred together with a spatially extensive density-inversion structure. In contrast, when main-channel momentum was dominant, stable density stratification developed and delayed thermal homogenization. These results suggest that thermal mixing at river confluences with temperature differences is governed not by buoyancy alone, but by the interaction between the relative momentum of the main-channel and tributary flows and buoyancy. In particular, even under the same temperature difference, variations in discharge ratio altered the relative importance of inertia-driven three-dimensional rearrangement of the incoming water masses and density stratification, thereby producing distinct thermal-mixing characteristics. This study provides a quantitative basis for interpreting thermal mixing at river confluences in terms of the coupled effects of flow structure, momentum, and density-driven processes.
items.authors: Dong Yeol Lee, Kyong Oh Baek, Young Do Kim

items.title: An Evolutionary Weakness: Can We Exploit Parasite–Bacteria Symbiosis?
items.abstract: Exploiting the endosymbiotic relationship between some parasites and bacteria may be an exciting therapeutic strategy. The obligate relationship between Wolbachia and nematodes represents a successful model, where the disruption of bacterial metabolism leads to parasite death, although challenges in applying novel drugs remain. Obligate endosymbiosis is rare in protozoa, limiting its broader application. Instead, facultative associations, such as those between Trichomonas vaginalis and Mycoplasma hominis and Entamoeba spp. and gut bacteria, demonstrate complex effects on parasite virulence and treatment outcomes. Successfully exploiting symbiosis depends on the stability and necessity of the symbiotic relationship, as well as the accessibility of the bacterial partner.
items.authors: Stephanie Berry, Felix Theml, Terry K. Smith

items.title: Polygenic Risk Scores in Alzheimer’s Disease: A Cross-Scale View from Genes to Brain and Behavior
items.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a genetically complex disorder in which inherited susceptibility is distributed across rare high-impact variants, the apolipoprotein E (APOE) locus, and a broad polygenic background of common risk alleles. Polygenic risk scores (PRSs) provide a quantitative framework for summarizing this distributed genetic liability and have become increasingly important tools for risk stratification, cohort enrichment, and biological interpretation. In this review, we synthesize evidence on AD PRSs across multiple biological and clinical scales, moving from genes and molecular pathways to biomarkers, brain structure and function, cognition, behavior, and clinical translation. Genome-wide PRSs capture aggregate inherited risk, whereas pathway-, tissue-, cell-type-, and biomarker-specific PRSs may help clarify the biological routes through which genetic susceptibility is expressed, including amyloid and tau metabolism, lipid homeostasis, endosomal trafficking, immune regulation, glial activation, proteostasis, and mitochondrial quality control. Evidence indicates that AD PRSs are most consistently associated with amyloid-related biomarkers, while associations with tau, neurodegeneration, brain atrophy, functional connectivity, cognitive decline, and neuropsychiatric manifestations are more heterogeneous and often depend on APOE, disease stage, biomarker context, and variable computation methodologies. Although PRSs show promise for research enrichment and mechanistic stratification, their individual-level clinical utility remains limited by modest predictive performance, ancestry-related transferability, calibration challenges, and ethical considerations. Future progress will require multi-ancestry cohorts, integration of common and rare variation, multi-omic annotation, longitudinal modeling, and multimodal prediction frameworks. Ultimately, PRSs are best viewed not as stand-alone diagnostic tools, but as cross-scale instruments for linking inherited susceptibility to the heterogeneous biological and clinical manifestations of AD.
items.authors: Efthalia Angelopoulou, Ioannis Stamelos, Stefanos Sampatakakis, Sokratis Papageorgiou, Nikolaos Scarmeas, Alexandros Hatzimanolis
items.title_zh: 阿尔茨海默病中的多基因风险评分：从基因到大脑与行为的跨尺度视角
items.summary_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（AD）是一种遗传复杂的疾病，其遗传易感性分布于稀有高影响变异、载脂蛋白E（APOE）位点及广泛的多基因背景。多基因风险评分（PRS）为总结这种分布的遗传负担提供了定量框架，并在风险分层、队列丰富和生物学解释中变得越来越重要。本文综述了AD PRS在多个生物和临床尺度上的证据，从基因和分子通路到生物标志物、大脑结构与功能、认知、行为及临床转化。全基因组PRS捕捉了聚合的遗传风险，而特定于通路、组织、细胞类型和生物标志物的PRS有助于阐明遗传易感性表达的生物途径。证据表明，AD PRS与淀粉样蛋白相关的生物标志物最为一致，而与tau、神经退行性变、大脑萎缩、功能连接、认知衰退及神经精神表现的关联则更为异质，通常依赖于APOE、疾病阶段及生物标志物背景。

items.title: Physically Constrained Temporal Fusion Transformer with LLM-Assisted Hyperparameter Optimization for Multi-Scenario Energy Time Series Forecasting
items.abstract: Accurate forecasting of battery state of health (SOH), wind power, and photovoltaic (PV) power is challenged by non-stationarity, multiscale dependencies, and physically implausible outputs. This study proposes a physically constrained Temporal Fusion Transformer (PC-TFT) that coordinates enhanced temporal representation, physical regularization, and LLM-assisted Bayesian optimization.
